# v1 Wave 0b: Platform and Surfaces Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: the skill the **Execution:** line names — dforge:subagent-driven-development for `subagent`, dforge:executing-plans for `inline`. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Build spec sections 1.4–1.8, 1.11, 1.13 and 1.14 on top of the merged lifecycle core: agent background tasks and module enablement, the guard context plumbing, controller events and module streams, per-action availability, scope and internal reads, the host-client additions of `internal/platform` (exec rules, units, file kinds), uninstall options and the uninstall barrier wiring, CLI overrides and reveal actions, plus the open seams w0a left (S3–S8, S17) and register rows 73, 75, 77 and 81.

**Architecture:** Every new core type is declared once in `internal/core` (Task 6); each new `core.AgentClient` and `core.Dispatcher` method is declared as a small named interface and embedded by the task that finishes its last implementer, so the tree builds after every task (w0a's S2 staging). Agent-side features land runtime first, then the agent route, client and embedding together, then the dispatcher, then the controller API and the CLI. Controller events flow through one in-process bus (`internal/controller/events`): one-second pollers publish controller changes and module state, the audit ingester publishes agent changes, the session registry's online hook publishes hosts, and the engine's existing `Publish` hook publishes `composite.step`. Every server-sent-event response goes through one writer in `internal/controller/api`, and stream and event requests authenticate passively, so an open stream never extends its session's idle limit.

**Tech Stack:** Go 1.27 (`GOTOOLCHAIN=local`), `database/sql` over `modernc.org/sqlite` through `internal/core/store`, `github.com/godbus/dbus/v5` through `internal/platform`, `golang.org/x/sys/unix` (`openat2`, `fstatfs`, `renameat`, `unlinkat`), `github.com/invopop/jsonschema` v0.14.0 and `github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6` through `internal/core/schema`, `github.com/hashicorp/yamux` through `internal/transport`, `net/netip`, `net/http`, `github.com/spf13/cobra`; web: TypeScript, React 19, `@tanstack/react-query`, Vitest with jsdom. No new dependency.

**Spec:** docs/dforge/specs/2026-10-21-v1-completion-design.md

**Execution:** subagent — `claude --model sonnet --effort high` — the plan runs parallel waves, and each task's **Implementer:** line chooses its implementer

**Parallelism:** waves — 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6-8 | 9-11 | 12 | 13 | 14 | 15 | 16 | 17 | 18 | 19-21 | 22-24 | 25-26 | 27 | 28 | 29 | 30 | 31-33 | 34 | 35 | 36 | 37 | 38 | 39 | 40-42 | 43-45 | 46 | 47 | 48-50 | 51-53 | 54-55 | 56 | 57 | 58-60 | 61-62 | 63 | 64 | 65-66 | 67-68 | 69-70 | 71-72 | 73 | 74 | 75 | 76-78 | 79 | 80 | 81 | 82 | 83 | 84 | 85 | 86 | 87

## Global Constraints

- Scope is spec revision 8 as amended on `main`: sections 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 1.7, 1.8 (without its four wave-0b clients), 1.11, 1.13 and 1.14, the row `core.stream_limit` of section 11, and the entries of Contracts that concern them, plus w0a's open seams S3, S4, S5, S6 (`core.stream_limit` only), S7, S8 and S17 and register rows 73, 75, 77 and 81. The rulings R1–R6 of the plan brief are settled and are not reopened. Later work, which this plan does not build:
  - w0c: 1.9, 1.10 (runtime listeners and trusted proxies; this plan uses today's web listeners and leaves `PanelListen`'s runtime listeners and "streams close when their listener is revoked" to it), 1.12 (`internal/core/ext`, which exposes this plan's `Dispatcher.ReadInternal`), the remaining codes of section 11, ADR 0014, 1.3's web UI and the change dialog that greys out unavailable actions;
  - wave 0b parts 0b-1 to 0b-4 (register row 79): `internal/platform/dockerapi`, `tslocal`, `netstat` and `netfilter`;
  - wave 1 (register row 80): the agent's live guard facts and the controller-on-host detection. This plan builds the guard plumbing only.
  Where this plan builds part of a later section, it builds exactly the part a task names and nothing more.
- Build only with the toolchain `go.mod` pins: every `go` command runs with `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` (ADR 0001).
- `/tmp` on this host is a small tmpfs that parallel Go builds fill. Every `go` command, `golangci-lint`, `make` and `pnpm` runs with `TMPDIR=/root/.cache/w0b-tmp/<task number>`, also where a step's command omits it. Create the directory with `mkdir -p` and empty it when the task ends.
- Dependencies: no task edits `go.mod`, `go.sum`, `web/package.json` or `web/pnpm-lock.yaml`. After every task `GOTOOLCHAIN=local go mod tidy -diff` prints nothing.
- Deferred minors of w0a (`docs/dforge/notes/w0a-lifecycle-core-deferred.md`): a task fixes one only when it already edits that code and the fix is cheap; no task exists for them. Task 19 edits `systemd.go` and may fix the three minors w0a's Task 8 left there (the sub-microsecond `RuntimeMax`, the error string without the `platform:` prefix at `systemd.go:174`, the weak negative-runtime test).
- Values copied from the spec, used exactly:
  - Background tasks: one goroutine per task; passes on start, `Every` after the previous pass ended, and after a wake; wakes during a pass coalesce into one further pass; a held lock key skips the pass without error; `Run` and `Watch` errors back off from 1 s to 5 min, reset by a successful pass; the `core_meta` key is `module_enabled.<id>` with value `"1"` or `"0"`, absent meaning the manifest's `DefaultEnabled`; the task's actor is `system:<task id>` with scope `admin`; `core_changes.system` is `INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`.
  - Availability: the controller re-asks an agent before dispatching an action whose cached answer is older than 60 s.
  - Streams and events: at most 64 KiB per stream event; of the 32 streams per agent session, actions and confirmations use at most 16 and module streams at most 16; a write deadline of 30 s renewed per write; an idle timeout of 10 minutes; a hard limit of 2 hours; a comment heartbeat every 20 s; session and token checks every 30 s; 4 open streams per principal and 16 per host; a relay buffer of 256 events ending with `overflow`; a ring of 1,024 events; at most 4 `GET /api/v1/events` connections per principal; SSE ids `<epoch hex>-<seq>`, `seq` from 1 within an epoch.
  - Exec: each argument at most 4,096 bytes with no NUL or control character; the base environment `PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin`, `LANG=C.UTF-8`, `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8` plus a rule's `Env`, nothing inherited; the runner's 30 s default timeout stays; `<version>` matches `^[0-9][0-9A-Za-z.+~-]{0,63}$`; the `apt-get` vectors are `APT-1`–`APT-6` word for word (C14).
  - Files: a `managed-dir` is created with mode 0700 and its default name pattern is `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`; a `service-dir` has mode 0700 and its default name pattern is `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,127}$`; a sysctl `<iface>` segment matches `all`, `default` or `^[A-Za-z0-9_.@-]{1,15}$` other than `.` and `..` that exists as a directory beside `all`.
  - Reveal: routes need scope `admin` and answer `200 {"value": <Value>}` with `Cache-Control: no-store`.
  - Uninstall option keys match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$`; the plan line is `<module>.<key>=<value> (default <d>; <help>)`.
- Names copied from the spec: the agent routes and API routes of W1 and W2; the headers `Darkpanel-Call` (with the member `guardRefresh`) and `Darkpanel-Internal: 1`; the event types `change`, `composite.step`, `host`, `module`, `reset`; the SSE event names `data` and `end` and the end reasons `done`, `overflow`, `expired`, `revoked`, `error`; the owned-path kinds `restore`, `managed-dir`, `sysctl`, `service-dir`; the label `darkpanel.module`; the CLI flags `--module-option`, `--stop-tasks`, `--abort`, `--override` and `--follow`; the error code `core.stream_limit` (C4).
- JSON fields are camelCase. Migrations are expand-only (ADR 0005): `ADD COLUMN`, `CREATE TABLE`, `CREATE INDEX`, and the one allowed rebuild that widens a `CHECK` list while keeping every column, row and index, inside the migration's transaction (C12).
- Nothing in a unit test talks to the real systemd, D-Bus, `/proc/sys`, `/etc/systemd`, the Docker socket, a network beyond `127.0.0.1`, `/etc`, `/var/lib`, `/run` or `/usr/local`:
  - systemd is a fake implementing `core.Units`, or `newSystemd` over a fake bus (`systemd_test.go`);
  - every file-provider test runs `platform.Files` with `TestMode: true` over `t.TempDir()`; sysctl tests point `FilesConfig.ProcSys` at a `t.TempDir()` tree shaped like `/proc/sys`; service-dir tests set `FilesConfig.LookupUser` to a function returning `os.Geteuid()` and `os.Getegid()` (C13);
  - exec tests run only `/usr/bin/printf`, `/usr/bin/cat`, `/usr/bin/env`, `/usr/bin/true`, `/usr/bin/false`, `/usr/bin/sleep` and the test binary through test rules, as `exec_test.go` does today; the production table is tested with `Match` alone, never by running its programs;
  - servers use `127.0.0.1:0` or `httptest`; Unix sockets live under `os.MkdirTemp("", "dp")`;
  - time comes from `coretest.NewFakeClock` wherever a duration above one second is waited on, including every SSE, scheduler, poller and backoff timer;
  - web tests use Vitest's jsdom with an injected `EventSource` constructor (C40).
  The one exception is `TestSystemdLive` (`internal/platform/systemd_test.go`), which Tasks 8 and 19 run with `DARKPANEL_SYSTEMD_LIVE=1` as root on this host and which starts only transient units named `darkpanel-live-<pid>-<nanoseconds>` and stops them. Tasks of one wave therefore share no port, path or global state.
- Live systemd tests run only with `DARKPANEL_SYSTEMD_LIVE=1` and as root, start only units with their own `darkpanel-live-` prefix, and never start, stop, restart, reload, kill, reset or otherwise touch any other unit: this host runs an installed `darkpanel-agent` and `darkpanel-controller` whose units are active.
- Tests run as root on this host (`id -u` prints 0). A test that needs a file owned by another user runs only as root and skips otherwise; a test that cannot hold as root skips as root, as `internal/platform/files_test.go:285-297` does.
- Tasks that share a Go package declare no top-level identifier, test helpers included, that another task of the plan declares. A task's new test helpers carry a short prefix of its own (as each task's opening paragraph names them). ## Contracts

Every name below is produced by exactly one task (named in brackets) and consumed as written. Later tasks cite these entries as C<n> or W<n>. Bodies are the producing task's; the declarations are fixed. A later task that changes a declaration is named after the producer ("Task 59 adds").

### C1. Core declarations [Task 6]

`internal/core/contract.go`:

```go
// ActionSpec gains, after Unwind:
	Guards    []GuardSpec                              // the guards the action's plan may report (1.5)
	Available func(ctx context.Context, env Env) error // per-action availability; the error text is the reason (1.7)
	MinScope  Scope                                    // raises the scope the class and side require; "" keeps it (1.7)
	Internal  bool                                     // dispatched only by the controller itself; read actions only (1.7)
	Reveal    bool                                     // returns one stored secret once; read actions only, MinScope admin (1.14)

// CallContext gains, after Retired:
	GuardRefresh *GuardContext // apply only: the controller's topology at apply time; never stored with the plan

// Guard gains, after Message:
	Overridable bool `json:"overridable"` // the engine copies it from the action's GuardSpec
	Overridden  bool `json:"overridden"`  // the plan's input listed this Overridable guard in overrides; OK is then true

// ErasedHandler gains, after Output:
	Reveal func(ctx context.Context, env Env, in json.RawMessage) (identity string, value json.RawMessage, err error) // DefineReveal and DefineInternalRead only

// Env gains, after Agents:
	Units Units // agent: the action's module's unit client (1.8, C16); nil on the controller and without a unit client

// The owned-path kinds gain:
const (
	OwnedRestore    = "restore"     // a regular file a snapshot may rewrite or remove
	OwnedManagedDir = "managed-dir" // a root-owned directory of flat module files
	OwnedSysctl     = "sysctl"      // a kernel parameter under /proc/sys
	OwnedServiceDir = "service-dir" // a directory owned by a module's service user
)

// OwnedPath gains, after CommentPrefix:
	Pattern string   // sysctl: the value pattern; managed-dir, service-dir: the file-name pattern
	User    string   // service-dir: the owning system user (an OwnedUser of the same module)
	Subdirs []string // service-dir: the only subdirectories, one level, created with it

// Manifest gains, after DefaultEnabled:
	ExternalUnits []ExternalUnit // units the module drives but does not own (1.8)

// ExternalUnit is a unit a module may drive without owning it.
type ExternalUnit struct {
	Name string   // "tailscaled.service"
	Ops  []string // a subset of UnitOpState, UnitOpStart, UnitOpStop, UnitOpRestart
}

// The operations of ExternalUnit.Ops.
const (
	UnitOpState   = "state"
	UnitOpStart   = "start"
	UnitOpStop    = "stop"
	UnitOpRestart = "restart"
)

// RestoreEntry is one file a snapshot restores (1.8).
type RestoreEntry struct {
	Path     string
	Present  bool
	Mode     fs.FileMode
	UID, GID int
	Data     []byte
}

// LabelModule labels the containers, networks and volumes a module creates (1.8).
const LabelModule = "darkpanel.module"

// Revealed is a reveal handler's result; Out is the action's output type.
type Revealed[Out any] struct {
	Identity string // what is revealed, for the audit ("npm admin password, host h1")
	Value    Out    // the output, never redacted
}

// ModuleAvailability is one module's availability on a host, per action (1.7).
type ModuleAvailability struct {
	Module    string
	Available bool
	Reason    string // "" when available
	Actions   []ActionAvailability
}

// ActionAvailability is one action's availability; Reason is "" when available.
type ActionAvailability struct {
	Name      string
	Available bool
	Reason    string
}
```

`internal/core/guard.go` (new):

```go
// GuardSpec declares one guard an action's plan may report.
type GuardSpec struct {
	ID          string // "firewall.lockout"; a plan reporting an undeclared id fails with internal
	Overridable bool   // only 2.3's and 4.1's lockout guards
}

// Guarded is embedded in the input type of every action with Guards.
type Guarded struct {
	Guard     *GuardContext `json:"guard,omitempty"`     // filled by the controller
	Overrides []string      `json:"overrides,omitempty"` // ids of Overridable guards
}

// GuardContext is the controller's topology a guard protects.
type GuardContext struct {
	Client      *Peer            `json:"client,omitempty"`      // the browser or CLI as the controller's transport saw it
	Via         *ProxyPath       `json:"via,omitempty"`         // set when the request came through an exposure (8)
	PanelListen []netip.AddrPort `json:"panelListen,omitempty"` // the controller's web listeners (runtime listeners: w0c)
	AgentListen []netip.AddrPort `json:"agentListen,omitempty"` // the controller's agent listeners
	AgentPeers  []netip.Addr     `json:"agentPeers,omitempty"`  // live agents' source addresses
}

// Peer is one end of a connection.
type Peer struct {
	Addr netip.Addr `json:"addr"`
	Port uint16     `json:"port"`
}

// ProxyPath is the exposure a request came through.
type ProxyPath struct {
	ExposureID   string           `json:"exposureId"`
	Kind         string           `json:"kind"` // npm | tunnel
	ProxyAddr    netip.Addr       `json:"proxyAddr"`
	ListenerAddr netip.AddrPort   `json:"listenerAddr"`
	Public       []netip.AddrPort `json:"public"`
}
```

### C5. Units listing and main PID [Task 19], `internal/core/units.go`, `internal/platform/systemd.go`

```go
// added to core.Units:
	// List returns the loaded units whose names match one glob pattern
	// (systemd's ListUnitsByPatterns), states as State reports them.
	List(ctx context.Context, pattern string) ([]UnitStatus, error)
```

`DBusSystemd.List` calls `Manager.ListUnitsByPatterns(states as = [], patterns as = [pattern])`, whose answer is `a(ssssssouso)` (name, description, load, active, sub, followed, path, job id, job type, job path); `PendingJob` is the job type, and `MainPID` is read for names ending in `.service` only. `DBusSystemd.State` reads `org.freedesktop.systemd1.Service.MainPID` (`u`) for a `.service` unit whose `LoadState` is not `not-found`. Every other `core.Units` implementer gains `List`: `devSystemd` (`cmd/darkpanel/agent.go`, returns `errDevSystemd`), `stubSystemd` (`internal/agent/daemon/daemon_test.go`), `fakeSystemd` (`internal/install/fakes_test.go`), `fakeSystemd` (`internal/update/systemd_test.go`), `taskUnits` (`internal/core/lifecycle/taskunit_test.go`). The install `fakeSystemd` (`internal/install/fakes_test.go`) gains the field `patterns []string`; its `List` appends the pattern to `patterns`, records nothing in `calls`, and returns, sorted by name, every unit of its `states` map (set by a job or `setState`) that is not in `missing` and whose name matches the pattern (`path.Match(pattern, name)`). `platform` gains the alias `type UnitStatus = core.UnitStatus`.

### C6. Owned-path and external-unit rules [Task 20], `internal/core/registry.go`

`NewRegistry` refuses, naming module and path:
- a `Kind` outside `file`, `block`, `dir`, `user`, `unit`, `restore`, `managed-dir`, `sysctl`, `service-dir`;
- for a module other than `core`, a `unit` path not matching `^/etc/systemd/system/darkpanel-[a-z0-9-]+\.service$`;
- a `restore`, `managed-dir` or `service-dir` path that is not absolute and clean;
- a `sysctl` path that is absolute, has an empty segment, a segment outside `^[a-z0-9_.-]+$` other than `<iface>`, a segment `.` or `..`, or more than one `<iface>`; a `sysctl` path without `Pattern`;
- a `Pattern` that does not compile, or that is set on a kind other than `sysctl`, `managed-dir` and `service-dir`;
- a `service-dir` whose `User` is empty or not an `OwnedUser` of the same module, or `User` on another kind;
- `Subdirs` on a kind other than `service-dir`, or an entry not matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`, or a duplicate;
- an `ExternalUnits` entry whose `Name` does not match `^[A-Za-z0-9@._-]+\.service$`, whose `Ops` is empty, repeats an op or names an op outside C1's four, or whose `Name` the module lists twice.

```go
// lifecycle.Config gains:

// engine.go: env takes the action, so every handler call gets its module's units.
func (e *Engine) env(p core.Principal, def core.ActionDef) core.Env
```

### C20. File kinds [Tasks 35–38], `internal/platform`

Spec 1.8's "Restore writes", "Kernel parameters", "Managed directories" and "Service-user directories" bullets are the behaviour, with these decisions: `WriteManaged` and `EnsureServiceDir` record the directory in the ownership store (kinds `managed-dir`, `service-dir`) before creating it; `Restore`, `ReadSysctl` and `WriteSysctl` record nothing; a sysctl `<iface>` that does not exist fails with an error wrapping `fs.ErrNotExist`; `RemoveManaged` and `RemoveIn` unlink a symlink without following it, and a missing name is not an error; `WriteSysctl` writes the value with one `write` at offset 0 without truncation, then reads the key back and fails unless the content, trimmed of one trailing newline, equals the value. An existing `managed-dir` or `service-dir` directory that `Owns` does not report is refused by `WriteManaged`, `RemoveManaged`, `EnsureServiceDir` and `RemoveServiceDir`. A managed directory must be root-owned with no group or other permission bits. `EnsureServiceDir` hands a recorded directory or declared subdirectory that is still root-owned (an interrupted creation) to `User`, and refuses any other owner. `RenameIn` and `RemoveIn` take `name` or `<subdir>/name`, and a rename stays within one directory. `RemoveServiceDir` does not look the user up. `Rename` forgets the source path's ownership record.

```go
// sseWrite writes b under a fresh SSEWriteTimeout deadline and flushes it.
func sseWrite(w http.ResponseWriter, b []byte) error
```

### C33. Runtime streams [Tasks 34, 56]

```go
// internal/agent/runtime/streams.go [Task 56]
const MaxStreamEvent = 64 << 10
func (r *Runtime) Streams(ctx context.Context) ([]core.StreamInfo, error)
func (r *Runtime) OpenStream(ctx context.Context, p core.Principal, module, name string, params url.Values) (io.ReadCloser, error)

// internal/core/schema/params.go [Task 34]
// ParamsJSON turns query parameters into the JSON object t's input schema describes: a
// string, integer, number or boolean property from one value, an array property from every
// value; an unknown key or a value of the wrong type is request.invalid_input.
func ParamsJSON(t reflect.Type, q url.Values) (json.RawMessage, error)
// ValidateType is ValidateInput for a bare type, compiled once per type.
func (v *Validator) ValidateType(t reflect.Type, raw json.RawMessage) error
```

The stream body is JSON lines: `{"data": <event>}` per event, then exactly one `{"end": {"reason": "done"}}` or `{"end": {"reason": "error", "error": <problem>}}`, where `<problem>` is `{"code", "detail"}` from `errcode.From`; for a 5xx code the detail is the code's title. An event over `MaxStreamEvent` makes `emit` fail with `request.too_large` and ends the stream with `error`. Closing the reader, or the end of `OpenStream`'s `ctx`, cancels `Run`'s context, and no end line is written then. `Runtime.Close` first cancels every open stream's `Run` context and waits until each `Run` returned; a stream still read then ends with `error` `unavailable`, and `OpenStream` on a closed runtime answers `unavailable`. `ParamsJSON` and `ValidateType` live in `internal/core/schema/params.go` [Task 34]; `Validator` gains `types typeNames`; `ParamsJSON` returns members sorted by key.

### C35. Dispatcher availability [Task 70], `internal/controller/dispatch/availability.go`


`Read`, `Plan` and `Apply` refuse an unavailable action with `module.unavailable`, detail `action <name> is unavailable on host <host>: <reason>`; a controller-side action is asked through `Engine.Available` each time. An agent answering `not_found` for the availability route (an agent without it) leaves every action available. The check exempts agent-side actions of the core module, as enablement does. Any error asking the agent other than `not_found` is logged, refuses nothing and is not cached; `Dispatcher.Availability` itself returns it. A module the registry lacks is `not_found`. A controller-side refusal's detail is `action <name> is unavailable on the controller: <reason>`. ### C36. Uninstall barrier [Tasks 18, 57, 66]

```go
// internal/install.UninstallConfig gains [Task 57]:
	StopTasks bool   // --stop-tasks
	Actor     string // the audit actor of --abort: local:root@<host id>, or core.ActorUnenrolled
// internal/install [Task 57]
// AbortUninstall clears the barrier when the agent service is active and reports what it did.
func AbortUninstall(ctx context.Context, cfg UninstallConfig) (string, error)
// internal/core/lifecycle/uninstall.go [Task 18]: the package function gains the actor and audits in its transaction
func AbortUninstall(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB, actor string) error
```

The new `barrier` step runs first: `lifecycle.BeginUninstall(ctx, db, cfg.StopTasks)`; without `StopTasks` it also refuses with `core.change_busy` while `Systemd.List("darkpanel-task-*.service")` reports an active unit, naming it; with `StopTasks` it stops every listed unit that is not inactive and waits, bounded by `StopTimeout` per unit, until each is inactive. `AbortUninstall` (the package function) deletes the `core_meta` row and appends the agent journal entry `{Actor: actor, Action: "core.uninstall", Version: 1, Phase: "uninstall-abort", Result: "ok", Input: {}}` in one transaction. `install.AbortUninstall` reads `darkpanel-agent.service`: active → clears and reports `the uninstall barrier is cleared; the agent accepts changes again`; otherwise reports `the services were stopped; there is nothing to abort` and changes nothing. Without `StopTasks` the unit check runs before `BeginUninstall`, so a refusal leaves no barrier; "active" means an `ActiveState` that is neither `inactive` nor `failed`. The `--keep-data` data step deletes the `uninstalling` row. `install.AbortUninstall` uses only `Layout`, `Systemd` and `Actor`. [Task 66] `cmd/darkpanel` sets `Actor` from the agent credentials; `--abort` with `--stop-tasks`, `--keep-data` or `--module-option` is a usage error.

### W4. SSE framing

Every frame is `id: <id>\n` (when set), `event: <name>\n`, `data: <one-line JSON>\n\n`; a heartbeat is `: ping\n\n`. `GET /api/v1/events`: `id` is `events.FormatID(epoch, seq)`, `event` the event type, `data` the event's data. A `Last-Event-ID` whose epoch is the bus's and whose events after its sequence are all still in the ring replays them; any other value gets one `reset` frame (id of the bus's last sequence) first, then live events; the stream closes without an end frame. The relay: `event: data` per stream event with the event JSON, then exactly one `event: end` with `{"reason": "done" | "overflow" | "expired" | "revoked" | "error", "error"?: <problem>}`, no ids.

- Decided seam: the client peer travels in the request context (C9), set by the API's `authenticate` middleware; the dispatcher reads it. Composite children are planned and applied on the engine's run context and so carry no client peer.

- Decided seam: task-unit actions never receive `GuardRefresh`, because the task process is a separate process that works from stored rows; no guarded action is a task action in v1.
- Decided seam: a composite's own undo or release of its steps through `dispatchChildren` is not gated on the support window: R1 covers operator routes, and gating would strand recovery.
- Decided seam: `GuardContext` and its parts carry camelCase JSON names, every `GuardContext` member `omitempty` (C1), because the spec gives the Go types without tags.
- Decided seam: the engine fills `Guard.Overridable`, records an override as a diff line, and the audit records `overrides` through the redacted input the journal already stores (C18).
- Decided seam: `Env.Units` comes from `lifecycle.Config.ModuleUnits` (C7, C16, C19): the core module gets the unrestricted client, the controller gets nil.
- Decided seam: the scoped units client allows `Reload` only to a module that declares a `unit` path and refuses transient starts (C16); spec 1.8's list is otherwise followed literally.
- Decided seam: `Internal` is allowed on read actions only (C17), the only kind spec 1.7 describes.
- Decided seam: `Engine.Reveal` and `Engine.ReadInternal` are two methods (C24) so the spec's four-argument `Engine.Reveal` stays; `AgentClient.Reveal`'s `internal` chooses between them on the agent.
- Decided seam: a reveal and an internal read are audited only when they succeed, as phase `reveal` with the identity in `Input` (C24); `--abort` is audited as phase `uninstall-abort`, action `core.uninstall` (C36); both need C12's `core_audit` widening.
- Decided seam: enablement pushes are best effort: a failed `SetModuleEnabled` after `hello` or in `core.module.enable`/`disable` is logged, and the next `hello` pushes the flag again (Task 67).
- Decided seam: the UI reads the cached availability through the new `GET /api/v1/hosts/{host}/modules/{module}/availability` (W2, Task 54), served by the concrete `Dispatcher.Availability` (wired by Task 72), so `core.Dispatcher` gains no method (spec 1.7); the web UI that greys actions out is w0c's.
- Decided seam: controller change and module events come from one-second pollers, agent changes from the audit ingester, host events from the session registry and `composite.step` from the engine's `Publish` (C29, C32).
- Decided seam: the SSE writer lives in `internal/controller/api` (`sse.go`, C27) and both `GET /api/v1/events` and the relay use it; the idle timeout and the hard limit end a relay with `expired`; `GET /api/v1/events` ends without an end frame and the browser reconnects with `Last-Event-ID`.
- Decided seam: the agent stream body frames events as `{"data": …}` lines and ends with one `{"end": …}` line (C33), so the relay can tell `done` from `error`; query parameters become JSON through the params schema (`schema.ParamsJSON`).
- Decided seam: the dispatcher asks `Streams` on every open instead of caching it, and stream limits are counted per `Principal.Actor` (C39).
- Decided seam: the 16/16 budget is `Session.OpenModule` plus `api.ClientConfig.DialStream` (C34, C37).
- Decided seam: a missing sysctl interface wraps `fs.ErrNotExist`; `ProcSys` other than `""` skips the procfs check so tests can use a temporary tree (C13, C20).
- Decided seam: `managed-dir` and `service-dir` record their directory, `restore` and `sysctl` record nothing (C20); uninstall stops and disables a module's recorded units before removing them (Task 47).
- Decided seam: `--abort` clears the barrier only while `darkpanel-agent.service` is active, which is how "after the services were stopped there is nothing to abort" is told apart (C36); `--stop-tasks` waits up to the existing `StopTimeout` (30 s) per task unit, more than the two 10 s fence gaps the parked w0a finding cv-47-a asks for.
- Decided seam: `PlanUninstall` checks the modules' option declarations (C11), because the registry does not look for `Uninstaller`.
- Scores assume the drafted steps carry the complete implementation code (spec 0), as the repository's earlier plans do.
- Plan size: 87 tasks, above the usual 20–35. Most tasks are one feature layer in one package so that Rule S holds, and 32 of them carry risk 3 (security, migration or concurrency) and run alone in their wave.

- Ruling (owner, 2026-10-22, register row 75): undo, repair and resolve are refused with `host.version_unsupported` outside the support window, like plan and apply; they are not gated on module enablement, so disabling a module never strands a pending or failed change (Task 9).
- Ruling: the agent's live guard facts and the controller-on-host detection need `internal/platform/netstat` (wave 0b-3), so they are register row 80 for wave 1; this plan builds the guard plumbing only (row 48).
- Ruling: "a plan reporting an undeclared id fails with internal" applies only to actions that declare `Guards`. Six existing controller actions report guards without declaring them (`hostenroll.go`, `enroll.go`, `users.go`, `hostrevoke.go`); declaring them would add `Guarded` to released input schemas.
- Ruling: the new audit phases are `reveal` and `uninstall-abort`. Only a successful reveal is audited, because a failed one has no `Identity`.
- Ruling: composite children carry no client peer in their guard context, because the runner plans and applies them in the background. Wave 8's panel exposure must revisit this.
- Ruling: stream routes (`GET /api/v1/events` and the relay) authenticate passively and never extend a session's idle limit (C27, Task 4).
- Ruling: `ApplySystem` refuses an action of class irreversible before planning, because a background task has no operator to confirm and the spec's only task actions (`firewall.containers.apply`, `firewall.docker.repair`) are revertible (C26).
- Ruling: the daemon's `guard` holds `d.mu` around an agent stream request only until the answer's header or first byte is written, and `Runtime.Close` cancels and waits for open streams (C33, C37, Task 81).
- Ruling (rows 73 and 81, Task 12): both service units gain `SuccessExitStatus=70`, `RestartForceExitStatus=70` and `RestartMode=direct`. Research on 2026-10-22 against systemd NEWS 215, 239, 251 and 254 and `service.c` at v255: exit 70 then never fails the unit or fires `OnFailure=` on 249–257; restarts still count toward the start limit; on 254+ `OnFailure=` otherwise fires before every auto-restart, which contradicts the M2 spec's "five starts two seconds apart exhaust the start limit" (docs/dforge/specs/2026-10-19-m2-fleet-lifecycle-design.md); 249 and 252 ignore `RestartMode=` with a warning. Task 12's test checks `burst × (MinConfirmTimeout + RestartSec) ≥ StartLimitIntervalSec` (5 × 12 s = 60 s against `StartLimitIntervalSec=60` today).

---

- Decided seam (C35): an agent answers `404 not_found` both when it lacks the availability route and when it lacks the module; the cache treats both as "every action available". That is safe because `Hosts.usable` (`internal/controller/dispatch/hosts.go:233-255`) already refuses a module the agent never reported (`coreactions.ReasonNotReported`) before availability is asked.
- Decided seam (C14): spec 1.8 says "the allowlist test runs each one and a reordering of each". The plan tests the production table through each rule's `Match` (every APT vector and a reordering of each accepted or refused), never by executing `apt-get`, `ufw` or `docker`, because unit tests never touch the real host (Global Constraints).

```go
// surfacesRows lists a table's rows, each as one JSON array of columns, in a
// stable order.
func surfacesRows(t *testing.T, db *DB, query string) []string {
	t.Helper()
	rows, err := db.Read().QueryContext(context.Background(), query)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
	var out []string
	for rows.Next() {
		var row string
		if err := rows.Scan(&row); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		out = append(out, row)
	}
	if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return out
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the migrations**

Create `internal/core/store/migrations/agent/0007_platform_surfaces.sql`:

```sql
-- A background task's changes are marked system (spec 1.4), so rollbacks and
-- snapshot retention can tell them apart. Only TaskContext.Apply sets it.
ALTER TABLE core_changes ADD COLUMN system INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (system IN (0, 1));

-- Uninstall removes the managed and service-user directories a module
-- created (spec 1.8), so the manifest records those kinds too. SQLite cannot
-- change a CHECK constraint in place, so the table is rebuilt, keeping every
-- column, row and the primary key. Only a marked block has a block id.

CREATE TABLE core_owned_files_new (
    path       TEXT NOT NULL,
    module     TEXT NOT NULL,
    kind       TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('file', 'block', 'dir', 'user', 'unit', 'managed-dir', 'service-dir')),
    block_id   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (path, module, block_id),
    CHECK ((kind = 'block') = (block_id <> ''))
) STRICT;

INSERT INTO core_owned_files_new (path, module, kind, block_id, created_at)
    SELECT path, module, kind, block_id, created_at FROM core_owned_files;

DROP TABLE core_owned_files;

ALTER TABLE core_owned_files_new RENAME TO core_owned_files;
```

Create `internal/core/store/migrations/controller/0011_platform_surfaces.sql`:

```sql
-- A background task's changes are marked system (spec 1.4), on the
-- controller as on the agent. Only TaskContext.Apply sets it.
ALTER TABLE core_changes ADD COLUMN system INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (system IN (0, 1));

-- The controller's change watcher asks every second for the changes updated
-- since its last poll (spec 1.6). Agent changes reach the controller through
-- the audit ingester, so agent.db needs no such index.
CREATE INDEX core_changes_updated ON core_changes (updated_at);

-- A reveal (spec 1.14) and an aborted uninstall (spec 1.11) are journaled
-- with the phases reveal and uninstall-abort, on the controller engine and in
-- the agent journals the controller ingests. SQLite cannot change a CHECK
-- constraint in place, so the table is rebuilt with the wider list, keeping
-- every column, row and index. The previous binary reads phase as a plain
-- string (ADR 0005).

CREATE TABLE core_audit_new (
    id         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    seq        INTEGER,
    at         TEXT NOT NULL,
    actor      TEXT NOT NULL,
    host_id    TEXT,
    action     TEXT NOT NULL,
    version    INTEGER NOT NULL,
    phase      TEXT NOT NULL
        CHECK (phase IN ('apply', 'confirm', 'revert', 'recover', 'interrupt', 'login', 'logout',
                         'undo', 'resolve', 'release', 'revert-watchdog', 'reveal', 'uninstall-abort')),
    change_id  TEXT,
    input_json TEXT,
    result     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (result IN ('ok', 'error', 'override')),
    error_code TEXT,
    source     TEXT,
    epoch      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''
) STRICT;

INSERT INTO core_audit_new (id, seq, at, actor, host_id, action, version, phase, change_id, input_json, result,
                            error_code, source, epoch)
    SELECT id, seq, at, actor, host_id, action, version, phase, change_id, input_json, result, error_code, source,
           epoch
    FROM core_audit;

DROP TABLE core_audit;

ALTER TABLE core_audit_new RENAME TO core_audit;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX core_audit_host_epoch_seq ON core_audit (host_id, epoch, seq);
```

### Task 2: Exec rules over whole argument vectors

**Files:**
- Modify: `internal/platform/exec.go:3-52` (imports, environment, Runner, NewRunner, ProductionAllowlist), `:75-104` (Run)
- Test: `internal/platform/exec_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: nothing.
- Produces: C14's `ExecRule` and `NewRunner(rules []ExecRule)`; `ProductionRules`, `TailscaleDebDir` and the `apt-get` vectors are Task 13's. Until Task 13, `ProductionAllowlist` returns two rules that allow any vector of `useradd` and `userdel`, today's allowlist, so its callers compile unchanged.

**Items:** 49

**Depends on:** none

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-opus-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 2 - risk 3 = 6
**Lenses:** security

Replaces the runner's path allowlist with `ExecRule`s that check the whole argument vector and add a fixed environment (C14). The runner refuses an unknown path as before, then any argument over 4,096 bytes or holding a control character (NUL, newline, any `unicode.IsControl` rune), before a rule's `Match` runs, then tries each rule of the path in order and runs the program with the base environment plus the first matching rule's `Env`. Every refusal names the path and at most an argument's position, never an argument, which may carry a secret; a rule's `Match` error is never shown. A rule without `Match` panics in `NewRunner` like a relative path, since a nil `Match` would otherwise read as "any vector". Security risk: it runs alone. The test helper `execAny(paths...)` (rules that allow any vector) is used by Task 13's tests too.

with:

```go
// maxOutput is the most a program may write to either stream.
const maxOutput = 4 << 20

// maxExecArg is the longest argument the runner passes on.
const maxExecArg = 4096

// environment is the base environment of every program; a rule adds its Env
// and nothing is inherited from the agent's own (ADR 0009).
var environment = []string{"PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin", "LANG=C.UTF-8", "LC_ALL=C.UTF-8"}

var errOutputTooLarge = errors.New("output too large")

// ExecRule allows a program to run with the argument vectors Match accepts.
type ExecRule struct {
	Path  string                    // absolute, clean
	Match func(args []string) error // nil error: the vector is allowed
	Env   []string                  // KEY=VALUE pairs appended to the base environment; nothing else is inherited
}

// Runner is the core.Runner of the agent: it runs only programs a rule
// allows, by absolute path, with an argument vector a rule of that path
// accepts, and never through a shell.
type Runner struct {
	rules          map[string][]ExecRule
	defaultTimeout time.Duration // applied when the caller's context has no deadline
}

var _ core.Runner = (*Runner)(nil)

// NewRunner returns a runner for rules; several rules may share a path. A
// relative or unclean path, or a rule without Match, is a programming error
// and panics.
func NewRunner(rules []ExecRule) *Runner {
	r := &Runner{rules: map[string][]ExecRule{}, defaultTimeout: 30 * time.Second}
	for _, rule := range rules {
		if !filepath.IsAbs(rule.Path) || filepath.Clean(rule.Path) != rule.Path {
			panic(fmt.Sprintf("platform: exec rule path %q is not a clean absolute path", rule.Path))
		}
		if rule.Match == nil {
			panic(fmt.Sprintf("platform: exec rule for %s has no Match", rule.Path))
		}
		r.rules[rule.Path] = append(r.rules[rule.Path], rule)
	}
	return r
}

// match returns the environment of the first rule of path that allows args.
// Its errors name the path and an argument's position, never an argument,
// which may carry a secret.
func (r *Runner) match(path string, args []string) ([]string, error) {
	rules, ok := r.rules[path]
	if !ok {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("platform: %s is not in the exec allowlist", path)
	}
	for i, a := range args {
		if len(a) > maxExecArg {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("platform: %s: argument %d is longer than %d bytes", path, i, maxExecArg)
		}
		if strings.ContainsFunc(a, unicode.IsControl) {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("platform: %s: argument %d contains a control character", path, i)
		}
	}
	for _, rule := range rules {
		if rule.Match(args) == nil {
			return append(slices.Clone(environment), rule.Env...), nil
		}
	}
	return nil, fmt.Errorf("platform: %s: argument vector not allowed", path)
}

// ProductionAllowlist is the agent's allowlist. The installer runs
// useradd and userdel for the controller's system user; every systemd
// operation goes through D-Bus instead (Systemd).
func ProductionAllowlist() []ExecRule {
	anyVector := func([]string) error { return nil }
	return []ExecRule{{Path: "/usr/sbin/useradd", Match: anyVector}, {Path: "/usr/sbin/userdel", Match: anyVector}}
}
```

Creates the package `internal/controller/events` with C15's bus: a random 64-bit epoch, sequence numbers from 1, a ring of the last 1,024 events for `Since`, and a fan-out that never blocks a publisher, because only `Publish` sends, under the bus's lock, so a full subscriber can be drained and handed one `reset`. A subscription's channel is closed under the same lock, so no send can hit a closed channel. Concurrency risk: it runs alone. Its test helpers `busRecv`, `busEmpty` and `busPublish` are reused by Task 16's tests in the same package.

```go
package events

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"log/slog"

	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

// busRecv receives one event from ch within five seconds.
func busRecv(t *testing.T, ch <-chan Event) Event {
	t.Helper()
	select {
	case ev, ok := <-ch:
		if !ok {
			t.Fatal("the subscription closed")
		}
		return ev
	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("timed out waiting for an event")
	}
	return Event{}
}

// busEmpty fails unless ch holds no event right now.
func busEmpty(t *testing.T, ch <-chan Event) {
	t.Helper()
	select {
	case ev := <-ch:
		t.Fatalf("unexpected event %+v", ev)
	default:
	}
}

// busPublish publishes n change events whose data carries their index.
func busPublish(b *Bus, n int) {
	for i := range n {
		b.Publish(TypeChange, map[string]int{"i": i})
	}
}

		if ev.Seq != uint64(i+2) || ev.Type != TypeChange || string(ev.Data) != want {

func TestBusSlowSubscriber(t *testing.T) {
	b := NewBus(nil)
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	defer cancel()
	slow, _ := b.Subscribe(ctx)
	fast, _ := b.Subscribe(ctx)
	got := make(chan []uint64, 1)
	go func() {
		var seqs []uint64
		for ev := range fast {
			seqs = append(seqs, ev.Seq)
			if len(seqs) == SubscriberBuffer+1 {
				got <- seqs
				return
			}
		}
	}()
	for i := range SubscriberBuffer + 1 {
		b.Publish(TypeChange, map[string]int{"i": i})
		// Waiting for the fast reader keeps its buffer from filling, which
		// would reset it too.
		deadline := time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second)
		for len(fast) > 0 && time.Now().Before(deadline) {
			time.Sleep(time.Millisecond)
		}
	}
	select {
	case seqs := <-got:
		for i, s := range seqs {
			if s != uint64(i+1) {
				t.Fatalf("the fast subscriber got %v, want 1 to %d", seqs, SubscriberBuffer+1)
			}
		}
	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("the fast subscriber did not get every event")
	}
	if ev := busRecv(t, slow); ev.Type != TypeReset || ev.Seq != SubscriberBuffer+1 || string(ev.Data) != `{}` {
		t.Fatalf("the slow subscriber read {%d %s %s}, want {%d reset {}}", ev.Seq, ev.Type, ev.Data, SubscriberBuffer+1)
	}
	busEmpty(t, slow)
	b.Publish(TypeHost, HostEvent{HostID: "h1"})
	if ev := busRecv(t, slow); ev.Type != TypeHost || ev.Seq != SubscriberBuffer+2 {
		t.Fatalf("after the reset the slow subscriber read {%d %s}, want {%d host}", ev.Seq, ev.Type, SubscriberBuffer+2)
	}
}

	var buf bytes.Buffer
	b := NewBus(slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(&buf, nil)))
	ch, _ := b.Subscribe(t.Context())
	b.Publish(TypeChange, make(chan int))

	busEmpty(t, ch)
	if evs, ok := b.Since(0); !ok || len(evs) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("Since(0) = %d events, want none", len(evs))
	}
	b.Publish(TypeHost, HostEvent{HostID: "h1"})
	if ev := busRecv(t, ch); ev.Seq != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("the next event has seq %d, want 1", ev.Seq)
	}
}

func TestBusPublishNeverBlocks(t *testing.T) {
	b := NewBus(nil)
	stalled, _ := b.Subscribe(t.Context())
	done := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		defer close(done)
		busPublish(b, 10_000)
	}()

	case <-done:
	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("10,000 publishes to a stalled subscriber did not return")
	}
	if ev := busRecv(t, stalled); ev.Type != TypeReset {
		t.Fatalf("the stalled subscriber read %s first, want reset", ev.Type)
	}
}
```

Create `internal/controller/events/bus.go`:

```go
// Package events is the controller's in-process event bus (spec 1.6). It
// numbers events within a random epoch, keeps the last RingSize of them for
// replay, and hands each one to every subscriber without ever blocking the
// publisher.
package events

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/rand"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"log/slog"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"time"
)

// Bus limits (spec 1.6).
const (
	RingSize         = 1024
	SubscriberBuffer = 256
)

// The event types of spec 1.6.
const (
	TypeChange        = "change"
	TypeCompositeStep = "composite.step"
	TypeHost          = "host"
	TypeModule        = "module"
	TypeReset         = "reset"
)

// Event is one published event; Seq increases from 1 within the bus's epoch.
type Event struct {
	Seq  uint64
	Type string
	Data json.RawMessage
}

// ChangeEvent is the data of a change event.
type ChangeEvent struct {
	HostID    string    `json:"hostId"`
	ChangeID  string    `json:"changeId"`
	Action    string    `json:"action"`
	State     string    `json:"state"`
	UpdatedAt time.Time `json:"updatedAt"`
}

// HostEvent is the data of a host event.
type HostEvent struct {
	HostID string `json:"hostId"`
	Online bool   `json:"online"`
}

// ModuleEvent is the data of a module event.
type ModuleEvent struct {
	HostID    string `json:"hostId"`
	ModuleID  string `json:"moduleId"`
	Enabled   bool   `json:"enabled"`
	Available bool   `json:"available"`
}

var resetData = json.RawMessage(`{}`)

// Bus fans events out to subscribers. Its methods are safe for concurrent
// use.
type Bus struct {
	log   *slog.Logger
	epoch string

	mu   sync.Mutex
	seq  uint64
	ring [RingSize]Event // the event of seq s is at ring[(s-1)%RingSize]
	subs map[chan Event]struct{}
}

// NewBus returns a bus with a new random epoch; a nil log discards.
func NewBus(log *slog.Logger) *Bus {
	if log == nil {
		log = slog.New(slog.DiscardHandler)
	}
	var b [8]byte
	_, _ = rand.Read(b[:])
	return &Bus{log: log, epoch: hex.EncodeToString(b[:]), subs: map[chan Event]struct{}{}}
}

// Epoch is the bus's epoch, 16 lower-case hex digits.
func (b *Bus) Epoch() string { return b.epoch }

// Publish marshals data and hands the event, with the next sequence number,
// to every subscriber. It never blocks: a subscriber whose buffer is full
// loses what it holds and gets one reset event instead, so it refetches
// everything. A marshal error is logged and the event dropped.
func (b *Bus) Publish(eventType string, data any) {
	raw, err := json.Marshal(data)
	if err != nil {
		b.log.Error("events: marshal event; it is dropped", "type", eventType, "err", err)
		return
	}
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	b.seq++
	ev := Event{Seq: b.seq, Type: eventType, Data: raw}
	b.ring[(ev.Seq-1)%RingSize] = ev
	for ch := range b.subs {
		select {
		case ch <- ev:
			continue
		default:
		}
		// Only Publish sends, under b.mu, so once the buffer is drained the
		// reset always fits.
		for drained := false; !drained; {
			select {
			case <-ch:
			default:
				drained = true
			}
		}
		ch <- Event{Seq: ev.Seq, Type: TypeReset, Data: resetData}
	}
}

// Subscribe returns a channel of the events published after the returned
// sequence number. The channel is closed once ctx ends.
func (b *Bus) Subscribe(ctx context.Context) (<-chan Event, uint64) {
	ch := make(chan Event, SubscriberBuffer)
	b.mu.Lock()
	b.subs[ch] = struct{}{}
	last := b.seq
	b.mu.Unlock()
	go func() {
		<-ctx.Done()
		b.mu.Lock()
		delete(b.subs, ch)
		close(ch)
		b.mu.Unlock()
	}()
	return ch, last
}

// Since returns the ring's events whose Seq is above after, oldest first.
// It reports false when one of those events has already left the ring.
func (b *Bus) Since(after uint64) ([]Event, bool) {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	if after >= b.seq {
		return nil, true
	}
	if b.seq-after > RingSize {
		return nil, false
	}
	out := make([]Event, 0, b.seq-after)
	for s := after + 1; s <= b.seq; s++ {
		out = append(out, b.ring[(s-1)%RingSize])
	}
	return out, true
}

// FormatID is the SSE id of the event seq of epoch.
func FormatID(epoch string, seq uint64) string {
	return epoch + "-" + strconv.FormatUint(seq, 10)
}

// ParseID splits an SSE id that FormatID made; ok is false for anything
// else.
func ParseID(id string) (epoch string, seq uint64, ok bool) {
	epoch, digits, found := strings.Cut(id, "-")
	if !found || len(epoch) != 16 || digits == "" {
		return "", 0, false
	}
	for _, c := range epoch {
		if (c < '0' || c > '9') && (c < 'a' || c > 'f') {
			return "", 0, false
		}
	}
	for _, c := range digits {
		if c < '0' || c > '9' {
			return "", 0, false
		}
	}
	seq, err := strconv.ParseUint(digits, 10, 64)
	if err != nil {
		return "", 0, false
	}
	return epoch, seq, true
}
```

### Task 4: Stream authentication that leaves the idle clock

**Files:**
- Modify: `internal/controller/auth/login.go:36-43` (Credentials), `:222` (Authenticate)
- Modify: `internal/controller/auth/session.go:94-97`, `:130`
- Test: `internal/controller/auth/session_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: nothing.
- Produces: `auth.Credentials.Passive` (C27); Task 15 sets it for the stream routes.

**Items:** 47

**Depends on:** none

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-opus-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 2 - risk 3 = 6

Adds `Credentials.Passive`: a session authenticated passively is checked exactly as before, including its idle limit, but its `last_seen_at` is not moved, so the request does not extend the session's 1-hour idle limit (spec section 9). The stream routes use it (Task 15): an open tab's event stream reconnects and re-checks its session every 30 s, and must not keep an idle session alive. A token has no idle limit, so its `last_used_at` is still recorded. `authenticateSession` keeps its signature for its callers and tests and calls the new `checkSession` with `touch` set. Authentication risk: it runs alone.

### Task 5: Host online hook in the session registry

**Files:**
- Modify: `internal/controller/fleet/registry.go:27-41` (RegistryConfig), `:80-87` (NewRegistry), `:124-127` (Register), `:151-163` (watch), `:182-191` (Disconnect), `:195-200` (Close)
- Test: `internal/controller/fleet/registry_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: nothing.
- Produces: C32 (`RegistryConfig.OnOnline`); Task 52 wires it.

**Items:** 47

**Depends on:** none

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-opus-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 2 - risk 3 = 6

Adds `RegistryConfig.OnOnline`: `true` when `Register` makes a host's first live session, `false` when the live session ends, when `Disconnect` closes it and, for each live host, when `Close` closes them; a replaced session reports nothing. Every call is made under the registry's mutex: called after the unlock, a session that ends at once could report `false` before `Register` reported `true`, leaving the host shown online. The hook therefore must not block or call the registry; the server's hook only publishes on the bus, which never blocks. Concurrency risk: it runs alone. Test helpers carry the prefix `hon`.

```go
// honLog records the OnOnline calls as "<host> <online>".
type honLog struct {
	mu    sync.Mutex
	calls []string
}

func (l *honLog) add(hostID string, online bool) {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	l.calls = append(l.calls, fmt.Sprintf("%s %v", hostID, online))
}

func (l *honLog) all() []string {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	return append([]string(nil), l.calls...)
}

// want fails unless the calls so far are exactly calls.
func (l *honLog) want(t *testing.T, calls ...string) {
	t.Helper()
	if got := l.all(); !slices.Equal(got, calls) {
		t.Fatalf("OnOnline calls = %q, want %q", got, calls)
	}
}

// honRegistry is newRegistry with its OnOnline calls recorded.
func honRegistry(t *testing.T) (*registryEnv, *honLog) {
	t.Helper()
	a, db, clock := newAuthority(t)
	addHost(t, db, "H1", core.HostEnrolled)
	serial := transport.SerialText(issue(t, a, db, "H1").SerialNumber)
	l := &honLog{}
	r, err := NewRegistry(RegistryConfig{
		DB: db, Clock: clock, CheckPeer: a.CheckPeer, Version: "1.2.3", ControllerID: "C1",
		Heartbeat: transport.HeartbeatConfig{Interval: time.Hour}, Log: quietLog, OnOnline: l.add,
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(r.Close)
	return &registryEnv{r: r, a: a, db: db, clock: clock, serial: serial}, l
}

func TestRegistryOnOnline(t *testing.T) {
	e, l := honRegistry(t)
	session := func() (ctrl, agent *transport.Session) {
		ctrl, agent = livePair(t)
		serveAgent(t, agent, helloAgent("H1", "v"))
		e.register(t, ctrl)
		return ctrl, agent
	}

	_, agent1 := session()
	l.want(t, "H1 true")
	_, agent2 := session()
	eventually(t, "the replaced session to end", func() bool { return ended(agent1) })
	time.Sleep(20 * time.Millisecond) // the replaced session's watcher has run
	l.want(t, "H1 true")
	_ = agent2.Close()
	eventually(t, "the ended session to go offline", func() bool { return len(l.all()) == 2 })
	l.want(t, "H1 true", "H1 false")

	_, agent3 := session()
	e.r.Disconnect("H1")
	eventually(t, "the disconnected session to end", func() bool { return ended(agent3) })
	time.Sleep(20 * time.Millisecond)
	l.want(t, "H1 true", "H1 false", "H1 true", "H1 false")

	session()
	e.r.Close()
	l.want(t, "H1 true", "H1 false", "H1 true", "H1 false", "H1 true", "H1 false")
}
```

```go
	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &back); err != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(back, g) {
		t.Errorf("json.Unmarshal = %+v, %v; want %+v", back, err, g)
	}
}

func TestStreamInfoJSON(t *testing.T) {
	b, err := json.Marshal(StreamInfo{Module: "docker", Name: "logs", SchemaHash: "ab"})
	if want := `{"module":"docker","name":"logs","schemaHash":"ab"}`; err != nil || string(b) != want {
		t.Errorf("json.Marshal = %s, %v; want %s", b, err, want)
	}
}

func TestGuardSerialisesOverrideFields(t *testing.T) {
	b, err := json.Marshal(Guard{ID: "a", OK: true, Overridable: true, Overridden: true})
	if want := `{"id":"a","ok":true,"message":"","overridable":true,"overridden":true}`; err != nil || string(b) != want {
		t.Errorf("json.Marshal = %s, %v; want %s", b, err, want)
	}
}
```

Create `internal/core/guard.go`:

```go
package core

import "net/netip"

// GuardSpec declares one guard an action's plan may report.
type GuardSpec struct {
	ID          string // "firewall.lockout"; a plan reporting an undeclared id fails with internal
	Overridable bool   // only the lockout guards of the firewall and Tailscale modules
}

// Guarded is embedded in the input type of every action with Guards. The
// controller fills Guard; the API and the agent socket refuse an input that
// carries it.
type Guarded struct {
	Guard     *GuardContext `json:"guard,omitempty"`     // filled by the controller
	Overrides []string      `json:"overrides,omitempty"` // ids of Overridable guards
}

// GuardContext is the controller's topology a guard protects: the flows
// that must survive a change.
type GuardContext struct {
	Client      *Peer            `json:"client,omitempty"`      // the browser or CLI as the controller's transport saw it
	Via         *ProxyPath       `json:"via,omitempty"`         // set when the request came through an exposure
	PanelListen []netip.AddrPort `json:"panelListen,omitempty"` // the controller's web listeners
	AgentListen []netip.AddrPort `json:"agentListen,omitempty"` // the controller's agent listeners
	AgentPeers  []netip.Addr     `json:"agentPeers,omitempty"`  // live agents' source addresses
}

// Peer is one end of a connection.
type Peer struct {
	Addr netip.Addr `json:"addr"`
	Port uint16     `json:"port"`
}

// ProxyPath is the exposure a request came through.
type ProxyPath struct {
	ExposureID   string           `json:"exposureId"`   // the panel exposure; what a retirement names
	Kind         string           `json:"kind"`         // npm | tunnel
	ProxyAddr    netip.Addr       `json:"proxyAddr"`    // the proxy container's address on the panel network
	ListenerAddr netip.AddrPort   `json:"listenerAddr"` // the runtime listener
	Public       []netip.AddrPort `json:"public"`
}
```

Create `internal/core/background.go`:

```go
package core

import (
	"context"
	"time"
)

// BackgroundTask is a module's agent-side loop. The runtime runs it only
// while the module's agent-side enabled flag is set and its preflight passes.
type BackgroundTask struct {
	ID       string        // "firewall.reconcile"; audit actor system:<ID>
	Every    time.Duration // 0: run only on wakes
	LockKeys []string      // the lock keys of every action the task may apply
	// Run is one pass: it returns when the pass is done. It mutates only
	// through tc.Apply.
	Run func(ctx context.Context, tc TaskContext) error
	// Watch, when set, is a long-lived subscription (Docker events) that
	// calls wake for each relevant event; it returns only on error or ctx done.
	Watch func(ctx context.Context, env Env, wake func()) error
}

// TaskContext is what one pass of a background task may use.
type TaskContext struct {
	Env Env // Principal is system:<ID>, ScopeAdmin; Call is empty
	// Apply plans and applies one action of the task's own module through
	// the runtime's lifecycle engine (never a second engine), confirms a
	// revertible change as soon as its verify passes, and marks the change
	// system. A plan with a failed guard returns plan.guard_failed.
	Apply func(ctx context.Context, action string, input any) (ChangeView, error)
}

// Background is implemented by a module with background tasks, found with a
// type assertion on the Module.
type Background interface{ BackgroundTasks() []BackgroundTask }
```

```go
package core

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"reflect"
)

// StreamDef is a read-only event stream of a module, "<module>.<name>",
// served with scope read.
type StreamDef struct {
	Name       string       // "logs"; the stream is "<module>.<name>"
	ParamsType reflect.Type // validated like action input (query parameters decoded to JSON)
	EventType  reflect.Type // one event; its schema is part of the hash
	// Run emits events until it returns. emit fails once the reader is
	// gone or a limit ended the stream; Run must then return.
	Run func(ctx context.Context, env Env, params json.RawMessage, emit func(event any) error) error
}

// Streamer is implemented by a module with streams, found with a type
// assertion on the Module.
type Streamer interface{ Streams() []StreamDef }

// StreamInfo is one stream an agent serves, as GET /agent/v1/streams lists it.
type StreamInfo struct {
	Module     string `json:"module"`
	Name       string `json:"name"`
	SchemaHash string `json:"schemaHash"`
}
```

**Files:**

**Items:** 75

Applies ruling R1 (register row 75): `Dispatcher.Undo`, `Repair` (the plan answer and repair-by-undo, which are one agent call) and `Resolve` refuse an agent change with `host.version_unsupported` while its agent is outside the support window, exempting `core.update.*` changes exactly as `inWindow` does. The change's action comes from `core_change_index`, or from the agent's view of the change when the index has no row (the index write after an apply is best effort). Module enablement is not checked, and `Release`, `Confirm`, `Revert`, `Effects`, `Observe` and `Steps` keep their behaviour. A composite's own unwind and release go through `dispatchChildren` (`children.go`), which calls the agent directly and stays ungated, so recovery is never stranded. It adds the test helper `(*harness).windowOps` to `window_test.go`.

```go
// Undo undoes a change where it lives, then ingests its host's journal. The

```

```go
// changeSideInWindow is changeSide for undo, repair and resolve: an agent
// change is refused with host.version_unsupported while its agent is outside
// the support window, unless its action is a core.update action, as plan and
// apply are. Module enablement is not checked: disabling a module must not
// strand a pending or failed change.
func (d *Dispatcher) changeSideInWindow(ctx context.Context, changeID string) (string, core.AgentClient, error) {
	hostID, c, err := d.changeSide(ctx, changeID)
	if err != nil || c == nil {
		return hostID, c, err
	}
	action, err := d.changeAction(ctx, hostID, changeID, c)
	if err != nil {
		return "", nil, err
	}
	if err := d.inWindow(hostID, action); err != nil {
		return "", nil, err
	}
	return hostID, c, nil
}

// changeAction is the action of hostID's change changeID: core_change_index's
// row, else the action of the change as the agent reports it, because the
// index write after an apply may have failed.
func (d *Dispatcher) changeAction(ctx context.Context, hostID, changeID string, c core.AgentClient) (string, error) {
	var action string
	err := d.cfg.DB.Read().QueryRowContext(ctx,
		"SELECT action FROM core_change_index WHERE change_id = ? AND host_id = ?", changeID, hostID).Scan(&action)
	switch {
	case err == nil:
		return action, nil
	case !errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
		return "", fmt.Errorf("dispatch: read change index: %w", err)
	}
	v, err := c.Change(ctx, changeID)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if v, err = checkChange(v, hostID, changeID); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return v.Action, nil
}
```

```go
// peerTCPPair returns the two ends of one session over a TCP connection on
// 127.0.0.1, closed at the end of the test.
func peerTCPPair(t *testing.T) (ctrl, agent *transport.Session) {
	t.Helper()
	ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer func() { _ = ln.Close() }()
	dialed, err := net.Dial("tcp", ln.Addr().String())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	conn, err := ln.Accept()
	if err != nil {

		t.Fatal(err)

	if agent, err = transport.AgentSession(dialed); err != nil {

	t.Cleanup(func() {
```

```go
// Peers returns the source addresses of the live sessions, deduplicated and
// sorted, IPv4-mapped addresses unmapped. A session whose connection has no
// IP address has none.
func (r *Registry) Peers() []netip.Addr {
	r.mu.Lock()
	var out []netip.Addr
	for _, ls := range r.live {
		if ap, err := netip.ParseAddrPort(ls.session.RemoteAddr().String()); err == nil {
			out = append(out, ap.Addr().Unmap())
		}
	}
	r.mu.Unlock()
	slices.SortFunc(out, netip.Addr.Compare)
	return slices.Compact(out)
}

// Disconnect closes hostID's live session, if any.
```

### Task 12: Watchdog exits versus the start limit

**Files:**
- Modify: `internal/install/units/darkpanel-agent.service`, `internal/install/units/darkpanel-controller.service` (the `[Service]` restart lines)
- Modify: `internal/core/lifecycle/revert.go:20-23` (the `WatchdogExitCode` comment)
- Modify: `docs/dforge/specs/2026-10-21-v1-completion-design.md:551-553` (spec 1.2's watchdog text)
- Test: `internal/install/units_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `lifecycle.WatchdogExitCode` (70), `lifecycle.MinConfirmTimeout` (10 s).
- Produces: the unit lines `RestartMode=direct`, `SuccessExitStatus=70` and `RestartForceExitStatus=70` in both service units.

**Items:** 73, 81

**Depends on:** none

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-sonnet-medium
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 1 - risk 2 = 4
**Approach:** advisor - research compared three unit-level options on systemd 249/252/255/257; A plus B chosen.

Register rows 73 and 81 and w0a seam S17, following the ruling: both service units declare the revert watchdog's status 70 a successful exit that forces a restart (`SuccessExitStatus=70`, `RestartForceExitStatus=70`), so a watchdog exit never fails the unit and never fires `OnFailure=darkpanel-rollback.service` on any systemd version, while `RestartSec=2` still restarts it. The restarts still count toward `StartLimitBurst`, so a binary that exits 70 forever still hits the limit, fails and is rolled back. `RestartMode=direct` (systemd 254 and later; 249 and 252 ignore it with a warning) stops `OnFailure=` from firing on every failed exit before an auto-restart, which on 254+ would otherwise start the rollback after a single crash (row 81); with it the rollback starts only once the start limit fails the unit, as the M2 spec intends. The values stay literal in the templates; the test builds the expected lines from `lifecycle.WatchdogExitCode`, so the two cannot drift apart. A second test pins why watchdog exits alone cannot exhaust the limit: each needs a new revertible change whose deadline is at least `MinConfirmTimeout` (10 s) after its apply, then `RestartSec` (2 s), so `StartLimitBurst` (5) of them take at least `StartLimitIntervalSec` (60 s), and strictly more, because starting the service and applying the change take time; systemd resets the start-limit window only once more than the interval has passed. The draft checked the new lines with `systemd-analyze verify` on systemd 257 (no warning). This task touches `internal/install/`, so gate 7 (harness) applies to the branch: the existing harness scenario 7 (`test/harness/m2_update_test.go`, `scenarioCrashLoop`, the `harnesscrash` build, which exits 1) must still roll back a crash-looping update, now after the start limit on systemd 255+ too; no new scenario. Test helpers carry the prefix `wd`.

```go
// wdUnitLines are the lines that let a service restart after a revert
// watchdog exit without failing the unit, and that make OnFailure= wait for
// the start limit on systemd 254 and later.
func wdUnitLines() []string {
	code := strconv.Itoa(lifecycle.WatchdogExitCode)
	return []string{"SuccessExitStatus=" + code, "RestartForceExitStatus=" + code, "RestartMode=direct"}
}

// wdUnitValue returns the value of the one line key=value of a unit.
func wdUnitValue(t *testing.T, unit, text, key string) int {
	t.Helper()
	for _, l := range strings.Split(text, "\n") {
		if v, ok := strings.CutPrefix(l, key+"="); ok {
			n, err := strconv.Atoi(v)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("%s: %s=%q is not a number", unit, key, v)
			}
			return n
		}
	}
	t.Fatalf("%s has no %s line", unit, key)
	return 0
}

```

```go
// TestWatchdogExitsStayInsideTheStartLimit checks that revert watchdog exits
// alone never exhaust a service's start limit: each one needs a new
// revertible change whose deadline is at least MinConfirmTimeout after its
// apply, and then RestartSec, so burst of them take at least the interval,
// and more, since starting and applying take time too.
func TestWatchdogExitsStayInsideTheStartLimit(t *testing.T) {
	units := unitsByPath(t, RoleController, nil, "")
	for _, name := range []string{"darkpanel-controller.service", "darkpanel-agent.service"} {
		text := units["/etc/systemd/system/"+name]
		interval := time.Duration(wdUnitValue(t, name, text, "StartLimitIntervalSec")) * time.Second
		burst := wdUnitValue(t, name, text, "StartLimitBurst")
		cycle := lifecycle.MinConfirmTimeout + time.Duration(wdUnitValue(t, name, text, "RestartSec"))*time.Second
		if time.Duration(burst)*cycle < interval {
			t.Errorf("%s: %d watchdog exits %v apart fit into the start limit's %v", name, burst, cycle, interval)
		}
	}
}

```

```go
func TestAptVectors(t *testing.T) {
	deb := TailscaleDebDir + "/tailscale_1.80.2_amd64.deb"
	tests := []struct {
		name  string
		got   []string
		words string // the spec's vector, word for word
	}{
		{"APT-1", AptUpdateTailscale(), "update -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=120 -o Dir::Etc::sourcelist=/etc/apt/sources.list.d/tailscale.list " +
			"-o Dir::Etc::sourceparts=- -o APT::Get::List-Cleanup=0"},
		{"APT-2", AptInstallTailscale(), "install -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=120 -y tailscale"},
		{"APT-3", AptInstallVersion("1.80.2"), "install -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=120 -y --allow-downgrades tailscale=1.80.2"},
		{"APT-4", AptStageVersion("1.80.2"),
			"install -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=120 -y --allow-downgrades --download-only --reinstall tailscale=1.80.2"},
		{"APT-5", AptInstallDeb(deb), "install -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=120 -y --allow-downgrades " + deb},
		{"APT-6", AptRemoveTailscale(), "remove -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=120 -y tailscale"},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if want := strings.Fields(tt.words); !slices.Equal(tt.got, want) {
				t.Fatalf("vector %q, want %q", tt.got, want)
			}
			if !execAllowed("/usr/bin/apt-get", tt.got...) {
				t.Errorf("%q is refused", tt.got)
			}
			for i := range len(tt.got) - 1 {
				swapped := slices.Clone(tt.got)
				swapped[i], swapped[i+1] = swapped[i+1], swapped[i]
				if execAllowed("/usr/bin/apt-get", swapped...) {
					t.Errorf("the reordering %q is allowed", swapped)
				}
			}
		})
	}
	refused := map[string][]string{
		"a version outside the pattern":   AptInstallVersion("../x"),
		"an empty version":                AptStageVersion(""),
		"a version of 65 characters":      AptInstallVersion("1" + strings.Repeat("a", 64)),
		"a package outside the directory": AptInstallDeb("/tmp/x.deb"),
		"a file that is not a package":    AptInstallDeb(TailscaleDebDir + "/tailscale_1.80.2_amd64"),
		"a package in a subdirectory":     AptInstallDeb(TailscaleDebDir + "/sub/x.deb"),
		"a package without a name":        AptInstallDeb(TailscaleDebDir + "/.deb"),
		"another package":                 {"install", "-o", "DPkg::Lock::Timeout=120", "-y", "nginx"},
		"no arguments":                    nil,
	}
	for name, args := range refused {
		if execAllowed("/usr/bin/apt-get", args...) {
			t.Errorf("%s: %q is allowed", name, args)
		}
	}
}
```

```go
package platform

import (
	"errors"
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"
	"slices"
	"strings"
)

// TailscaleDebDir is the tailscale module's managed-dir of staged packages
// (spec 4.1).
const TailscaleDebDir = "/var/lib/darkpanel/agent/tailscale-debs"

const aptLockTimeout = "DPkg::Lock::Timeout=120"

var (
	aptVersionPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^[0-9][0-9A-Za-z.+~-]{0,63}$`)
	// aptDebStemPattern is the managed-dir default name pattern, which a
	// staged package's name before ".deb" matches.
	aptDebStemPattern  = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`)
	execNftNamePattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64}$`)
)

// errExecVector is a Match refusal; the runner reports it without the
// arguments.
var errExecVector = errors.New("argument vector not allowed")

var (
	execSystemUsers = []string{"darkpanel", "darkpanel-derp"}
	execUfwVerbs    = []string{
		"allow", "deny", "reject", "limit", "route", "insert", "prepend", "delete", "default", "logging",
		"enable", "disable", "reload",
	}
	execSaveTables  = []string{"filter", "nat", "raw", "mangle", "security"}
	execNftFamilies = []string{"ip", "ip6", "inet", "arp", "bridge", "netdev"}
)

// AptUpdateTailscale is APT-1: refresh the Tailscale repository only.
func AptUpdateTailscale() []string {
	return []string{
		"update", "-o", aptLockTimeout, "-o", "Dir::Etc::sourcelist=/etc/apt/sources.list.d/tailscale.list",
		"-o", "Dir::Etc::sourceparts=-", "-o", "APT::Get::List-Cleanup=0",
	}
}

// AptInstallTailscale is APT-2: install or update to the repository's
// current version.
func AptInstallTailscale() []string {
	return []string{"install", "-o", aptLockTimeout, "-y", "tailscale"}
}

// AptInstallVersion is APT-3: install an exact version.
func AptInstallVersion(version string) []string {
	return []string{"install", "-o", aptLockTimeout, "-y", "--allow-downgrades", "tailscale=" + version}
}

// AptStageVersion is APT-4: download a version's package without
// installing it.
func AptStageVersion(version string) []string {
	return []string{
		"install", "-o", aptLockTimeout, "-y", "--allow-downgrades", "--download-only", "--reinstall", "tailscale=" + version,
	}
}

// AptInstallDeb is APT-5: install a staged package, TailscaleDebDir/<name>.deb.
func AptInstallDeb(deb string) []string {
	return []string{"install", "-o", aptLockTimeout, "-y", "--allow-downgrades", deb}
}

// AptRemoveTailscale is APT-6: uninstall.
func AptRemoveTailscale() []string {
	return []string{"remove", "-o", aptLockTimeout, "-y", "tailscale"}
}

// ProductionRules is the complete exec allowlist of the agent binary (spec
// 1.8); nothing else may run. Which caller may run a vector is a code rule,
// not a runner rule, and systemd stays on D-Bus (ADR 0012).
func ProductionRules() []ExecRule {
	exactly := func(vectors ...[]string) func([]string) error {
		return func(args []string) error { return execOneOf(args, vectors...) }
	}
	noninteractive := []string{"DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive"}
	rules := []ExecRule{
		{Path: "/usr/sbin/useradd", Match: execMatchUseradd},
		{Path: "/usr/sbin/userdel", Match: execMatchUserdel},
		{Path: "/usr/sbin/ufw", Match: execMatchUfw},
		{Path: "/usr/sbin/iptables", Match: exactly([]string{"--version"})},
		{Path: "/usr/sbin/ip6tables", Match: exactly([]string{"--version"})},
		{Path: "/usr/bin/apt-get", Match: execMatchAptGet, Env: noninteractive},
		{Path: "/usr/bin/apt-mark", Match: exactly([]string{"hold", "tailscale"}, []string{"unhold", "tailscale"}, []string{"showhold"})},
		{Path: "/usr/bin/dpkg", Match: exactly([]string{"--configure", "-a"}), Env: slices.Clone(noninteractive)},
		{Path: "/usr/sbin/nft", Match: execMatchNft},
		{Path: "/usr/bin/docker", Match: execMatchDocker, Env: []string{
			"DOCKER_CONFIG=/var/lib/darkpanel/agent/docker-config", "HOME=/var/lib/darkpanel/agent/docker-config",
			"COMPOSE_EXPERIMENTAL_GIT_REMOTE=false", "COMPOSE_EXPERIMENTAL_OCI_REMOTE=false",
		}},
	}
	for _, family := range []string{"iptables", "ip6tables"} {
		for _, variant := range []string{"", "-legacy", "-nft"} {
			rules = append(rules,
				ExecRule{Path: "/usr/sbin/" + family + variant + "-save", Match: execMatchSave},
				ExecRule{Path: "/usr/sbin/" + family + variant + "-restore", Match: exactly([]string{"-n"})},
			)
		}
	}
	return rules
}

func execOneOf(args []string, vectors ...[]string) error {
	for _, v := range vectors {
		if slices.Equal(args, v) {
			return nil
		}
	}
	return errExecVector
}

func execMatchUseradd(args []string) error {
	if len(args) == 0 || !slices.Contains(execSystemUsers, args[len(args)-1]) {
		return errExecVector
	}
	return execOneOf(args, []string{"--system", "--no-create-home", "--shell", "/usr/sbin/nologin", args[len(args)-1]})
}

func execMatchUserdel(args []string) error {
	if len(args) != 1 || !slices.Contains(execSystemUsers, args[0]) {
		return errExecVector
	}
	return nil
}

// execMatchUfw allows [--force | --dry-run] <verb> <arg>...; the arguments
// after the verb are constrained by the firewall module's input schema.
func execMatchUfw(args []string) error {
	if len(args) > 0 && (args[0] == "--force" || args[0] == "--dry-run") {
		args = args[1:]
	}
	if len(args) == 0 || !slices.Contains(execUfwVerbs, args[0]) {
		return errExecVector
	}
	return nil
}

func execMatchSave(args []string) error {
	if len(args) != 2 || args[0] != "-t" || !slices.Contains(execSaveTables, args[1]) {
		return errExecVector
	}
	return nil
}

func execMatchNft(args []string) error {
	if slices.Equal(args, []string{"list", "tables"}) {
		return nil
	}
	if len(args) != 4 || args[0] != "list" || args[1] != "table" ||
		!slices.Contains(execNftFamilies, args[2]) || !execNftNamePattern.MatchString(args[3]) {
		return errExecVector
	}
	return nil
}

// execMatchAptGet allows exactly the vectors APT-1 to APT-6.
func execMatchAptGet(args []string) error {
	if len(args) == 0 {
		return errExecVector
	}
	last := args[len(args)-1]
	allowed := [][]string{AptUpdateTailscale(), AptInstallTailscale(), AptRemoveTailscale()}
	if version, ok := strings.CutPrefix(last, "tailscale="); ok && aptVersionPattern.MatchString(version) {
		allowed = append(allowed, AptInstallVersion(version), AptStageVersion(version))
	}
	if aptStagedDeb(last) {
		allowed = append(allowed, AptInstallDeb(last))
	}
	return execOneOf(args, allowed...)
}

// aptStagedDeb reports whether deb is TailscaleDebDir/<name>.deb.
func aptStagedDeb(deb string) bool {
	dir, file := filepath.Split(deb)
	stem, ok := strings.CutSuffix(file, ".deb")
	return ok && dir == TailscaleDebDir+"/" && aptDebStemPattern.MatchString(stem)
}

// execMatchDocker allows compose --project-directory <dir> -p <name>
// (-f <file>)+ (--env-file <f>)* (--profile <p>)* <verb>, every path
// absolute and clean.
func execMatchDocker(args []string) error {
	if len(args) < 5 || args[0] != "compose" || args[1] != "--project-directory" || !execCleanAbs(args[2]) ||
		args[3] != "-p" || args[4] == "" {
		return errExecVector
	}
	rest := args[5:]
	files := 0
	for len(rest) >= 2 && rest[0] == "-f" && execCleanAbs(rest[1]) {
		rest, files = rest[2:], files+1
	}
	for len(rest) >= 2 && rest[0] == "--env-file" && execCleanAbs(rest[1]) {
		rest = rest[2:]
	}
	for len(rest) >= 2 && rest[0] == "--profile" && rest[1] != "" {
		rest = rest[2:]
	}
	if files == 0 {
		return errExecVector
	}
	return execOneOf(rest, []string{"up", "-d", "--no-build"}, []string{"down"}, []string{"pull"}, []string{"restart"},
		[]string{"config", "--format", "json"})
}

func execCleanAbs(p string) bool { return filepath.IsAbs(p) && filepath.Clean(p) == p }
```
