```go
	}
}

func TestEventsLimit(t *testing.T) {
	h, _, base := sseHarness(t)
	token := h.token(core.ScopeRead)
	var open []*http.Response
	for range MaxEventStreams {
		resp, _ := sseOpen(t, base, token, "")
		open = append(open, resp)
	}
	defer func() {
		for _, resp := range open {
			_ = resp.Body.Close()
		}
	}()

	fifth := sseGet(t, base, token, "")
	body, err := io.ReadAll(fifth.Body)
	_ = fifth.Body.Close()
	var p problem
	if err != nil || fifth.StatusCode != http.StatusTooManyRequests || json.Unmarshal(body, &p) != nil || p.Code != errcode.StreamLimit {
		t.Fatalf("fifth stream = %d %s (%v), want 429 %s", fifth.StatusCode, body, err, errcode.StreamLimit)
	}

	other, _ := sseOpen(t, base, h.token(core.ScopeRead), "")
	_ = other.Body.Close()

	_ = open[0].Body.Close()
	open = open[1:]
	deadline := time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second)
	for {
		resp := sseGet(t, base, token, "")
		if resp.StatusCode == http.StatusOK {
			open = append(open, resp)
			break
		}
		_ = resp.Body.Close()
		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusTooManyRequests || time.Now().After(deadline) {
			t.Fatalf("after a stream closed: %d, want a new stream accepted", resp.StatusCode)
		}
		time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
	}
}

// sseOpen opens GET /api/v1/events on base with a bearer token and, when
// set, a Last-Event-ID, and checks the stream's status.
func sseOpen(t *testing.T, base, token, lastID string) (*http.Response, *bufio.Reader) {
	t.Helper()
	resp := sseGet(t, base, token, lastID)
	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK || resp.Header.Get("Content-Type") != "text/event-stream" {
		_ = resp.Body.Close()
		t.Fatalf("GET /api/v1/events = %d %s, want 200 text/event-stream", resp.StatusCode, resp.Header.Get("Content-Type"))
	}
	return resp, bufio.NewReader(resp.Body)
}

// sseGet sends GET /api/v1/events; the caller closes the body.
func sseGet(t *testing.T, base, token, lastID string) *http.Response {
	t.Helper()
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	t.Cleanup(cancel)
	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, base+"/api/v1/events", nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
	if lastID != "" {
		req.Header.Set("Last-Event-ID", lastID)
	}
	resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return resp
}
```

```go
package api

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"net/http"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/controller/events"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
)

// handleEvents serves GET /api/v1/events (spec 1.6): the controller's
// events as server-sent events, after the events a Last-Event-ID missed or
// a reset. The stream ends without an end frame; the browser reconnects
// with the last id it saw.
func (s *Server) handleEvents(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	c, _ := callerFrom(r.Context())
	if err := authorize(c.principal, core.ScopeRead); err != nil {
		writeProblem(w, s.log, err)
		return
	}
	bus := s.cfg.Events
	if bus == nil {
		writeProblem(w, s.log, errcode.New(errcode.NotFound, "this controller publishes no events"))
		return
	}
	release, err := s.eventSlot(c.principal.Actor)
	if err != nil {
		writeProblem(w, s.log, err)
		return
	}
	defer release()
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(r.Context())
	defer cancel()
	live, last := bus.Subscribe(ctx)
	backlog := eventBacklog(bus, r.Header.Values("Last-Event-ID"), last)
	frames := make(chan sseFrame)
	go func() {
		defer close(frames)
		send := func(ev events.Event) bool {
			select {
			case frames <- sseFrame{ID: events.FormatID(bus.Epoch(), ev.Seq), Event: ev.Type, Data: ev.Data}:
				return true
			case <-ctx.Done():
				return false
			}
		}
		for _, ev := range backlog {
			if !send(ev) {
				return
			}
		}
		for ev := range live {
			if !send(ev) {
				return
			}
		}
	}()
	s.sseStream(w, r, frames)
}

// eventBacklog is what a stream sends before the events published after
// last: nothing without a Last-Event-ID; the events after it when it names
// this epoch and none of them has left the ring; otherwise one reset.
func eventBacklog(bus *events.Bus, lastIDs []string, last uint64) []events.Event {
	if len(lastIDs) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	if epoch, seq, ok := events.ParseID(lastIDs[0]); ok && len(lastIDs) == 1 && epoch == bus.Epoch() && seq <= last {
		if missed, ok := bus.Since(seq); ok {
			n := 0
			for n < len(missed) && missed[n].Seq <= last {
				n++
			}
			return missed[:n]
		}
	}
	return []events.Event{{Seq: last, Type: events.TypeReset, Data: json.RawMessage(`{}`)}}
}
```

```go
// scpGuardedIn is an input that embeds Guarded.
type scpGuardedIn struct {
	Guarded
	Name string `json:"name"`
}

// scpMutator is a forward-only handler over input In.
type scpMutator[In any] struct{}

func (scpMutator[In]) Plan(context.Context, Env, In) (PlanOutcome, error) { return PlanOutcome{}, nil }

func (scpMutator[In]) Apply(context.Context, Env, In) (echoOut, error) { return echoOut{}, nil }

func (scpMutator[In]) Verify(context.Context, Env, In, echoOut) error { return nil }

// scpAction is the forward-only compensable agent action scp.rule.add over
// input In, with spec's Guards and MinScope.
func scpAction[In any](spec ActionSpec) ActionDef {
	spec.Name, spec.Version, spec.Class, spec.Side = "scp.rule.add", 1, ClassCompensable, SideAgent
	spec.ForwardOnly, spec.Converges = true, true
```

```go
package core

// DefaultScope is the scope an action of class on side needs (spec section
// 10): read for read actions, operate for agent-side mutations, admin
// otherwise. An unknown class or side needs admin, so a mistake fails closed.
func DefaultScope(class Class, side Side) Scope {
	switch {
	case class == ClassRead:
		return ScopeRead
	case side == SideAgent && (class == ClassRevertible || class == ClassCompensable || class == ClassIrreversible):
		return ScopeOperate
	default:
		return ScopeAdmin
	}
}

// RequiredScope is the higher of DefaultScope(s.Class, s.Side) and
// s.MinScope. An unknown MinScope is returned as it is, which no principal's
// scope allows.
func RequiredScope(s ActionSpec) Scope {
	need := DefaultScope(s.Class, s.Side)
	if s.MinScope == "" || need.Allows(s.MinScope) {
		return need
	}
	return s.MinScope
}
```

```go
// guardedType is the type an action with Guards embeds in its input.
var guardedType = reflect.TypeFor[Guarded]()

// embedsGuarded reports whether t is a struct with an anonymous field of type
// Guarded.
func embedsGuarded(t reflect.Type) bool {
	if t == nil || t.Kind() != reflect.Struct {
		return false
	}
	for i := range t.NumField() {
		if f := t.Field(i); f.Anonymous && f.Type == guardedType {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// checkGuardsAndScope applies the guard and scope declaration rules (spec
// 1.5, 1.7): Guards and an embedded Guarded go together, so the schema
// carries guard and overrides exactly when a plan may report a guard, and
// MinScope only raises the scope the class and side require.
func checkGuardsAndScope(a ActionDef) error {
	s := a.Spec
	ref := a.Ref()
	guarded := embedsGuarded(a.InputType)
	switch {
	case len(s.Guards) > 0 && !guarded:
		return fmt.Errorf("action %s: an action with Guards has an input type that embeds core.Guarded", ref)
	case len(s.Guards) == 0 && guarded:
		return fmt.Errorf("action %s: an input type that embeds core.Guarded belongs to an action with Guards", ref)
	}
	ids := map[string]bool{}
	for _, g := range s.Guards {
		switch {
		case g.ID == "":
			return fmt.Errorf("action %s: a guard has an empty ID", ref)
		case ids[g.ID]:
			return fmt.Errorf("action %s: guard %s is declared twice", ref, g.ID)
		}
		ids[g.ID] = true
	}
	switch need := DefaultScope(s.Class, s.Side); {
	case s.MinScope == "":
	case s.MinScope != ScopeRead && s.MinScope != ScopeOperate && s.MinScope != ScopeAdmin:
		return fmt.Errorf("action %s: unknown MinScope %q", ref, s.MinScope)
	case !s.MinScope.Allows(need):
		return fmt.Errorf("action %s: MinScope %s is below the %s scope the action needs; MinScope only raises", ref, s.MinScope, need)
	}
	return nil
}

// Action returns one action version.
```

```go
// parseModuleOptions reads --module-option values, each
// <module>.<key>=<value>, by module id and key. The key ends at the first
// "=", so a value may hold one.
func parseModuleOptions(values []string) (map[string]map[string]string, error) {
	if len(values) == 0 {
		return nil, nil
	}
	out := map[string]map[string]string{}
	for _, v := range values {
		module, rest, dot := strings.Cut(v, ".")
		key, value, eq := strings.Cut(rest, "=")
		if !dot || !eq || module == "" || key == "" {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("--module-option %q is not <module>.<key>=<value>", v)
		}
		if _, dup := out[module][key]; dup {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("--module-option %s.%s is given twice", module, key)
		}
		if out[module] == nil {
			out[module] = map[string]string{}
		}
		out[module][key] = value
	}
	return out, nil
}
```

```go
package lifecycle

import (
	"context"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
)

// Available runs ref's Spec.Available under Protect with the env of a call
// without a principal, and returns its error, whose text is the reason the
// action is unavailable (spec 1.7). An action that declares no Available is
// available. An unknown action, or one of the other side, is action.unknown.
func (e *Engine) Available(ctx context.Context, ref core.ActionRef) error {
	def, err := e.action(ref)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if def.Spec.Available == nil {
		return nil
	}
	return e.protect(ref, "Available", func() error { return def.Spec.Available(ctx, e.env(core.Principal{}, def)) })
}
```

```go
	Follow bool     `json:"follow"`
	Name   []string `json:"name"`
}

type paramsMixed struct {
	Ratio float64 `json:"ratio,omitempty"`
	Since string  `json:"since,omitempty"`
	Ports []int   `json:"ports,omitempty"`
	Inner struct {
		N int `json:"n"`
	} `json:"inner,omitzero"`
}

func TestParamsJSON(t *testing.T) {
	logs, mixed := reflect.TypeFor[paramsLogs](), reflect.TypeFor[paramsMixed]()
	tests := []struct {
		name  string
		typ   reflect.Type
		query string
		want  string // members sorted by key; "" wants request.invalid_input at path
		path  string
	}{
		{"every kind", logs, "tail=100&follow=true&name=a&name=b", `{"follow":true,"name":["a","b"],"tail":100}`, ""},
		{"one array value", logs, "name=a", `{"name":["a"]}`, ""},
		{"no parameters", logs, "", `{}`, ""},
		{"number and string", mixed, "ratio=0.5&since=2026-10-22T00:00:00Z", `{"ratio":0.5,"since":"2026-10-22T00:00:00Z"}`, ""},
		{"integer items", mixed, "ports=80&ports=443", `{"ports":[80,443]}`, ""},
		{"not an integer", logs, "tail=s3cr3t", "", "/tail"},
		{"not a boolean", logs, "follow=maybe", "", "/follow"},
		{"repeated scalar", logs, "tail=1&tail=2", "", "/tail"},
		{"unknown key", logs, "other=1", "", "/other"},
		{"not a number", mixed, "ratio=NaN", "", "/ratio"},
		{"bad item", mixed, "ports=80&ports=x", "", "/ports"},
		{"nested object", mixed, "inner=1", "", "/inner"},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			q, err := url.ParseQuery(tt.query)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			got, err := ParamsJSON(tt.typ, q)
			if tt.want != "" {
				if err != nil || !jsonEqual(t, got, []byte(tt.want)) {
					t.Errorf("ParamsJSON(%s) = %s, %v; want %s", tt.query, got, err, tt.want)
				}
				return
			}
			var coded *errcode.Error
			if !errors.As(err, &coded) || coded.Code != errcode.InvalidInput || len(coded.Fields) != 1 || coded.Fields[0].Path != tt.path {
				t.Fatalf("ParamsJSON(%s) = %s, %v; want %s at %s", tt.query, got, err, errcode.InvalidInput, tt.path)
			}
			if strings.Contains(err.Error(), "s3cr3t") {
				t.Errorf("the refusal %v quotes the value", err)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestValidateType(t *testing.T) {
	v := NewValidator()
	typ := reflect.TypeFor[paramsLogs]()
	if err := v.ValidateType(typ, json.RawMessage(`{"tail":1,"follow":false,"name":[]}`)); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("ValidateType of a valid value = %v", err)
	}
	err := v.ValidateType(typ, json.RawMessage(`{"tail":1,"follow":false,"name":[],"extra":1}`))
	var coded *errcode.Error
	if !errors.As(err, &coded) || coded.Code != errcode.InvalidInput || len(coded.Fields) != 1 || coded.Fields[0].Path != "/extra" {
		t.Fatalf("ValidateType of an unknown member = %v, want %s at /extra", err, errcode.InvalidInput)
	}
	if err := v.ValidateType(reflect.TypeFor[paramsMixed](), json.RawMessage(`{}`)); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("ValidateType of a second type = %v", err)
	}
	if len(v.schemas) != 2 || len(v.types) != 2 {
		t.Errorf("compiled %d schemas for %d types, want 2 and 2", len(v.schemas), len(v.types))
	}
}
```

```go
package schema

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"maps"
	"math"
	"net/url"
	"reflect"
	"slices"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
)

// typeNames maps each bare type ValidateType has seen to its key in the
// schema cache.
type typeNames map[reflect.Type]string

// ValidateType is ValidateInput for a bare type, compiled once per type.
func (v *Validator) ValidateType(t reflect.Type, raw json.RawMessage) error {
	return v.ValidateInput(core.ActionDef{Spec: core.ActionSpec{Name: v.typeName(t)}, InputType: t}, raw)
}

// typeName is t's key in the schema cache, "type-<n>". No action can take
// it: an action name has three dotted segments.
func (v *Validator) typeName(t reflect.Type) string {
	v.mu.Lock()
	defer v.mu.Unlock()
	if v.types == nil {
		v.types = typeNames{}
	}
	name, ok := v.types[t]
	if !ok {
		name = fmt.Sprintf("type-%d", len(v.types)+1)
		v.types[t] = name
	}
	return name
}

// paramsNode is the part of an input schema ParamsJSON reads.
type paramsNode struct {
	Ref        string                 `json:"$ref"`
	Type       json.RawMessage        `json:"type"`
	Items      *paramsNode            `json:"items"`
	Properties map[string]*paramsNode `json:"properties"`
}

// typeName is the node's JSON type: its type keyword, or the one type other
// than null a list of types names; "" when it names none.
func (n *paramsNode) typeName() string {
	var one string
	if json.Unmarshal(n.Type, &one) == nil {
		return one
	}
	var many []string
	_ = json.Unmarshal(n.Type, &many)
	var types []string
	for _, t := range many {
		if t != "null" {
			types = append(types, t)
		}
	}
	if len(types) == 1 {
		return types[0]
	}
	return ""
}

// ParamsJSON turns query parameters into the JSON object t's input schema
// describes: a string, integer, number or boolean property from one value,
// an array property from every value; an unknown key or a value of the
// wrong type is request.invalid_input. Required members and value
// constraints are left to the input schema's validation (ValidateType).
func ParamsJSON(t reflect.Type, q url.Values) (json.RawMessage, error) {
	raw, err := Input(t)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	var doc struct {
		paramsNode
		Defs map[string]*paramsNode `json:"$defs"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &doc); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("schema: parameters of %s: %w", t, err)
	}
	resolve := func(n *paramsNode) *paramsNode {
		if name, ok := strings.CutPrefix(n.Ref, "#/$defs/"); ok && doc.Defs[name] != nil {
			return doc.Defs[name]
		}
		return n
	}
	root := resolve(&doc.paramsNode)
	obj := make(map[string]json.RawMessage, len(q))
	for _, key := range slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(q)) {
		prop, ok := root.Properties[key]
		if !ok {
			return nil, invalidParam(key, "unknown parameter")
		}
		prop = resolve(prop)
		values := q[key]
		var v json.RawMessage
		if prop.typeName() == "array" && prop.Items != nil {
			items := make([]json.RawMessage, len(values))
			for i, s := range values {
				if items[i], err = paramValue(resolve(prop.Items).typeName(), s); err != nil {
					return nil, invalidParam(key, err.Error())
				}
			}
			if v, err = json.Marshal(items); err != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("schema: parameter %s: %w", key, err)
			}
		} else {
			if len(values) != 1 {
				return nil, invalidParam(key, "give it once")
			}
			if v, err = paramValue(prop.typeName(), values[0]); err != nil {
				return nil, invalidParam(key, err.Error())
			}
		}
		obj[key] = v
	}
	out, err := json.Marshal(obj)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("schema: parameters of %s: %w", t, err)
	}
	return out, nil
}

// paramValue is the JSON of one query value s for a property of JSON type
// typ. Its errors never quote s, which may be a secret.
func paramValue(typ, s string) (json.RawMessage, error) {
	switch typ {
	case "string":
		return json.Marshal(s)
	case "integer":
		n, err := strconv.ParseInt(s, 10, 64)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("want an integer")
		}
		return strconv.AppendInt(nil, n, 10), nil
	case "number":
		f, err := strconv.ParseFloat(s, 64)
		if err != nil || math.IsInf(f, 0) || math.IsNaN(f) {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("want a number")
		}
		return json.Marshal(f)
	case "boolean":
		if s != "true" && s != "false" {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("want true or false")
		}
		return json.RawMessage(s), nil
	}
	return nil, fmt.Errorf("cannot be given as a query parameter")
}

func invalidParam(key, msg string) error {
	return &errcode.Error{Code: errcode.InvalidInput, Detail: fmt.Sprintf("query parameter %s: %s", key, msg),
		Fields: []errcode.FieldError{{Path: "/" + escape(key), Message: msg}}}
}
```

```go
// rstFiles returns a writer for module "rst", which declares <dir>/user.rules
// as kind restore and <dir>/app.conf as kind file.
func rstFiles(t *testing.T) (*Files, *fakeOwnership, string) {
	t.Helper()
	dir := t.TempDir()
	f, own := fpFiles(t, FilesConfig{Owned: map[string][]core.OwnedPath{"rst": {
		{Path: filepath.Join(dir, "user.rules"), Kind: core.OwnedRestore},
		{Path: filepath.Join(dir, "app.conf"), Kind: core.OwnedFile},
	}}})
	return f, own, dir
}

func TestRestoreWrites(t *testing.T) {
	f, own, dir := rstFiles(t)
	ctx := context.Background()
	path := filepath.Join(dir, "user.rules")
	uid, gid := os.Geteuid(), os.Getegid()
	entry := core.RestoreEntry{Path: path, Present: true, Mode: 0o640, UID: uid, GID: gid, Data: []byte("x")}
	if err := f.Restore(ctx, "rst", entry); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Restore (create): %v", err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte("old\n"), 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.Chmod(path, 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := f.Restore(ctx, "rst", entry); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Restore (replace): %v", err)
	}
	info, err := os.Stat(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	st := info.Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t)
	if got := readFile(t, path); got != "x" || info.Mode().Perm() != 0o640 || int(st.Uid) != uid || int(st.Gid) != gid {
		t.Errorf("restored %q mode %o owner %d:%d, want x, 640, %d:%d", got, info.Mode().Perm(), st.Uid, st.Gid, uid, gid)
	}
	if names := dirNames(t, dir); !reflect.DeepEqual(names, []string{"user.rules"}) {
		t.Errorf("directory holds %v, want only user.rules (no temporary file left)", names)
	}
	if got, _ := own.List(ctx); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("ownership = %+v, want nothing recorded", got)
	}
}

// rstSymlink puts a symlink at user.rules pointing at victim.
func rstSymlink(t *testing.T, dir string) {
	t.Helper()
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "victim"), []byte("keep\n"), 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.Symlink(filepath.Join(dir, "victim"), filepath.Join(dir, "user.rules")); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

// rstVictimKept checks that the symlink and its target are unchanged.
func rstVictimKept(t *testing.T, dir string) {
	t.Helper()
	if got := readFile(t, filepath.Join(dir, "victim")); got != "keep\n" {
		t.Errorf("symlink target changed to %q", got)
	}
	if info, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(dir, "user.rules")); err != nil || info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink == 0 {
		t.Errorf("the symlink was replaced or removed: %v", err)
	}
}

// rstDirectory puts a directory at user.rules.
func rstDirectory(t *testing.T, dir string) {
	t.Helper()
	if err := os.Mkdir(filepath.Join(dir, "user.rules"), 0o700); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement Restore**

Replace the whole of `internal/platform/files_restore.go` (Task 25's stub) with:

```go
package platform

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"path/filepath"

	"golang.org/x/sys/unix"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
)

// Restore writes e.Path with e's data, mode and owner, or removes it when e is
// not present; module must declare the path as kind restore. Only a regular
// file is written or removed. Nothing is recorded: a restore path is a file of
// the host that uninstall never removes.
func (f *Files) Restore(ctx context.Context, module string, e core.RestoreEntry) error {
	if _, err := f.declaredKind(module, e.Path, core.OwnedRestore); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer f.lock(e.Path)()
	dir, name := filepath.Split(e.Path)
	fd, err := f.openDir(dir)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer func() { _ = unix.Close(fd) }()
	if e.Present {
		return writeFileAt(fd, name, e.Path, e.Data, e.Mode, e.UID, e.GID)
	}
	var st unix.Stat_t
	err = unix.Fstatat(fd, name, &st, unix.AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, unix.ENOENT):
		return nil
	case err != nil:
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: stat %s: %w", e.Path, err)
	case st.Mode&unix.S_IFMT != unix.S_IFREG:
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: %s is not a regular file", e.Path)
	}
	if err := unix.Unlinkat(fd, name, 0); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, unix.ENOENT) {
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: remove %s: %w", e.Path, err)
	}
	if err := unix.Fsync(fd); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: sync directory of %s: %w", e.Path, err)
	}
	return nil
}
```

`e.Mode`'s permission bits are applied (`writeFileAt` uses `mode.Perm()`); a restore entry carries a configuration file's mode, never set-user-ID bits.

This task fills `ReadSysctl` and `WriteSysctl`. A key matches a declaration of kind `sysctl` segment by segment; a declared `<iface>` segment takes `all`, `default` or a name matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_.@-]{1,15}$` other than `.` and `..` (so `a/b`, which adds a segment, and a 16-character name match nothing and are refused before the tree is touched). Both methods open the root (`FilesConfig.ProcSys`, or `/proc/sys`) with `openat2(RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS)`; for `/proc/sys` only, `fstatfs` must report `PROC_SUPER_MAGIC`. The key is opened below the root with `openBeneath` (`RESOLVE_BENEATH | RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS`), so an interface directory that does not exist fails with `ENOENT`, which wraps `fs.ErrNotExist` (C20), and a symlink anywhere fails with `ELOOP`; the opened key must be a regular file. `WriteSysctl` checks the value against `Pattern` before opening anything, holds the declaration's lock, writes with one `pwrite` at offset 0 without truncation (procfs allows no temporary file or rename), then reads the key back through a new descriptor and fails unless the content without one trailing newline equals the value. Nothing is recorded. Test helpers carry the prefix `sys`. Security risk: it runs alone.

```go
// sysUntouched checks that every regular file of the tree still holds the
// initial value.
func sysUntouched(t *testing.T, root string) {
	t.Helper()
	err := filepath.WalkDir(root, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
		if err != nil || !d.Type().IsRegular() {
			return err
		}
		if got := readFile(t, path); got != sysTreeValue {
			t.Errorf("%s holds %q, want it untouched", path, got)
		}
		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

Replace the whole of `internal/platform/files_sysctl.go` (Task 25's stub) with:

```go
package platform

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os"
	"regexp"
	"strings"

	"golang.org/x/sys/unix"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
)

const (
	// procSys is the sysctl root of a host.
	procSys = "/proc/sys"
	// sysctlIfaceSegment is the key segment that stands for a network
	// interface (net/ipv6/conf/<iface>/forwarding).
	sysctlIfaceSegment = "<iface>"
	// maxSysctlValue bounds a read; no parameter Darkpanel declares comes near.
	maxSysctlValue = 64 << 10
)

// sysctlIface is an interface name as a key segment: all, default, or a
// kernel interface name (IFNAMSIZ is 16 with the NUL).
var sysctlIface = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z0-9_.@-]{1,15}$`)

// ReadSysctl returns the value of the kernel parameter key, which module
// declares as kind sysctl, without one trailing newline.
func (f *Files) ReadSysctl(ctx context.Context, module, key string) (string, error) {
	if _, err := f.sysctlDeclared(module, key); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	root, err := f.openProcSys()
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	defer func() { _ = unix.Close(root) }()
	return readSysctl(root, key)
}

// WriteSysctl sets the kernel parameter key, which module declares as kind
// sysctl, to value, which must match the declaration's Pattern. procfs allows
// neither a temporary file nor a rename, so the value goes in one write at
// offset 0, and the key is read back to confirm the kernel took it. Nothing is
// recorded: uninstall never touches a kernel parameter.
func (f *Files) WriteSysctl(ctx context.Context, module, key, value string) error {
	op, err := f.sysctlDeclared(module, key)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	pattern, err := regexp.Compile(op.Pattern)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: sysctl %s: pattern: %w", op.Path, err)
	}
	if !pattern.MatchString(value) {
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: sysctl %s: value %q does not match %s", key, value, op.Pattern)
	}
	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer f.lock(op.Path)()
	root, err := f.openProcSys()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer func() { _ = unix.Close(root) }()
	fd, err := openSysctl(root, key, unix.O_WRONLY)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	n, err := unix.Pwrite(fd, []byte(value), 0)
	if cerr := unix.Close(fd); err == nil {
		err = cerr
	}
	switch {
	case err != nil:
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: write sysctl %s: %w", key, err)
	case n != len(value):
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: write sysctl %s: wrote %d of %d bytes", key, n, len(value))
	}
	got, err := readSysctl(root, key)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if got != value {
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: sysctl %s reads back %q after writing %q", key, got, value)
	}
	return nil
}

// sysctlDeclared returns module's sysctl declaration that key instantiates:
// equal segment by segment, where an <iface> segment of the declaration takes
// any valid interface name.
func (f *Files) sysctlDeclared(module, key string) (core.OwnedPath, error) {
	segs := strings.Split(key, "/")
	for _, op := range f.cfg.Owned[module] {
		if op.Kind == core.OwnedSysctl && sysctlMatches(strings.Split(op.Path, "/"), segs) {
			return op, nil
		}
	}
	return core.OwnedPath{}, fmt.Errorf("platform: module %s does not declare sysctl %s", module, key)
}

func sysctlMatches(decl, segs []string) bool {
	if len(decl) != len(segs) {
		return false
	}
	for i, d := range decl {
		switch {
		case d == sysctlIfaceSegment:
			if segs[i] == "." || segs[i] == ".." || !sysctlIface.MatchString(segs[i]) {
				return false
			}
		case d != segs[i]:
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

// openProcSys opens the sysctl root and, for the real /proc/sys, checks that
// procfs is mounted there, so a directory planted in place of an unmounted
// /proc is never written.
func (f *Files) openProcSys() (int, error) {
	root := f.cfg.ProcSys
	if root == "" {
		root = procSys
	}
	fd, err := unix.Openat2(unix.AT_FDCWD, root, &unix.OpenHow{
		Flags:   unix.O_RDONLY | unix.O_DIRECTORY | unix.O_CLOEXEC,
		Resolve: unix.RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS,
	})
	if err != nil {
		return -1, fmt.Errorf("platform: open %s: %w", root, err)
	}
	if f.cfg.ProcSys == "" {
		ok, err := isProcfs(fd)
		if err == nil && !ok {
			err = errors.New("not procfs")
		}
		if err != nil {
			_ = unix.Close(fd)
			return -1, fmt.Errorf("platform: %s: %w", root, err)
		}
	}
	return fd, nil
}

// isProcfs reports whether fd lies on a procfs mount.
func isProcfs(fd int) (bool, error) {
	var st unix.Statfs_t
	if err := unix.Fstatfs(fd, &st); err != nil {
		return false, fmt.Errorf("platform: fstatfs: %w", err)
	}
	return st.Type == unix.PROC_SUPER_MAGIC, nil
}

// openSysctl opens key below root, refusing a symlink anywhere in it, and
// checks that it is a regular file. A missing key, an interface that has gone
// among them, fails with an error wrapping fs.ErrNotExist.
func openSysctl(root int, key string, flags uint64) (int, error) {
	fd, err := openBeneath(root, key, flags, 0)
	if err != nil {
		return -1, fmt.Errorf("platform: open sysctl %s: %w", key, err)
	}
	var st unix.Stat_t
	if err := unix.Fstat(fd, &st); err != nil {
		_ = unix.Close(fd)
		return -1, fmt.Errorf("platform: stat sysctl %s: %w", key, err)
	}
	if st.Mode&unix.S_IFMT != unix.S_IFREG {
		_ = unix.Close(fd)
		return -1, fmt.Errorf("platform: sysctl %s is not a regular file", key)
	}
	return fd, nil
}

func readSysctl(root int, key string) (string, error) {
	fd, err := openSysctl(root, key, unix.O_RDONLY)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), key)
	defer func() { _ = file.Close() }()
	data, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(file, maxSysctlValue))
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("platform: read sysctl %s: %w", key, err)
	}
	return strings.TrimSuffix(string(data), "\n"), nil
}
```

The `<iface>` rule of spec 1.8 ("exists as a directory beside `all`") is enforced by opening the whole key below the root: `<iface>` is the directory beside `all`, and `openat2` fails with `ENOENT` when it is missing or `ENOTDIR` when it is not a directory.

**Files:**

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: C13 (`declaredKind`, `lock`, `openDir`, `openBeneath`, `writeFileAt`, `Ownership.Owns`; `fpFiles`, `fakeOwnership.onRecord`), C1 (`OwnedManagedDir`, `OwnedPath.Pattern`), C12 (kind `managed-dir` in `core_owned_files`; the tests use the in-memory fake).
- Produces: `Files.WriteManaged`, `Files.RemoveManaged` (C20).

**Items:** 64

**Depends on:** Task 1, Task 28

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-sonnet-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 1 - risk 3 = 5

This task fills `WriteManaged` and `RemoveManaged`. A name must be one flat entry (not `.`, `..` or containing `/`) matching the declaration's `Pattern`, or `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$` without one. Under the directory's lock, the parent is opened with `openDir` and the directory below it with `openBeneath`. A missing directory is, for a write, recorded as kind `managed-dir` first, then made with `mkdirat(0700)`, the parent `fsync`ed, opened and `fchmod`ed to 0700 (the umask must not decide); for a removal it means there is nothing to remove. An existing directory must be recorded as the module's (`Owns`), so a pre-existing directory is never adopted and later removed by uninstall, owned by the same uid as the parent check expects (root, or the test's uid in `TestMode`) and have no group or other bits. The file is written through `writeFileAt` with the caller's mode, uid and gid. `RemoveManaged` `fstatat(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)`s the name: missing is not an error, a directory is refused, anything else (a symlink included, never followed) is `unlinkat`ed and the directory `fsync`ed. Removing the whole directory at uninstall is Task 47's. Test helpers carry the prefix `mgd`. Security risk: it runs alone.

```go
				t.Fatalf("WriteManaged(%s) = %v, want ok %v", c.name, err, c.ok)
			}
			if rerr := f.RemoveManaged(context.Background(), "mgd", dir, c.name); c.ok != (rerr == nil) {
				t.Errorf("RemoveManaged(%s) = %v, want ok %v", c.name, rerr, c.ok)
			}
			if !c.ok {
				if _, err := os.Lstat(dir); !errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
					t.Errorf("a refused name created %s", dir)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestRemoveManaged(t *testing.T) {
	f, own, root := mgdFiles(t)
	ctx := context.Background()
	dir := filepath.Join(root, "tokens")
	if err := f.RemoveManaged(ctx, "mgd", dir, "a.token"); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("RemoveManaged before the directory exists: %v", err)
	}
	uid, gid := os.Geteuid(), os.Getegid()
	for _, name := range []string{"a.token", "b.token"} {
		if err := f.WriteManaged(ctx, "mgd", dir, name, []byte(name), 0o600, uid, gid); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	if err := f.RemoveManaged(ctx, "mgd", dir, "a.token"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("RemoveManaged: %v", err)
	}
	if err := f.RemoveManaged(ctx, "mgd", dir, "a.token"); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("RemoveManaged of a missing name: %v", err)
	}
	victim := filepath.Join(root, "victim")
	if err := os.WriteFile(victim, []byte("keep\n"), 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.Symlink(victim, filepath.Join(dir, "c.token")); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := f.RemoveManaged(ctx, "mgd", dir, "c.token"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("RemoveManaged of a symlink: %v", err)
	}
	if got := readFile(t, victim); got != "keep\n" {
		t.Errorf("symlink target changed to %q", got)
	}
	if err := os.Mkdir(filepath.Join(dir, "d.token"), 0o700); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := f.RemoveManaged(ctx, "mgd", dir, "d.token"); err == nil {
		t.Error("RemoveManaged of a subdirectory succeeded")
	}
	if names := dirNames(t, dir); !reflect.DeepEqual(names, []string{"b.token", "d.token"}) {
		t.Errorf("directory holds %v, want b.token and d.token", names)
	}
	if got, _ := own.List(ctx); len(got) != 1 {
		t.Errorf("ownership = %+v, want the directory still recorded", got)
	}
}

func TestManagedRefusals(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name  string
		dir   string // relative to the test directory
		setup func(t *testing.T, root string, own *fakeOwnership)
		want  string // in the error
	}{
		{name: "undeclared directory", dir: "other", want: "does not declare"},
		{name: "kind file", dir: "app.conf", want: "does not declare"},
		{name: "directory is a symlink", dir: "tokens", setup: func(t *testing.T, root string, own *fakeOwnership) {
			if err := os.Mkdir(filepath.Join(root, "real"), 0o700); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if err := os.Symlink("real", filepath.Join(root, "tokens")); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			mgdRecord(t, own, filepath.Join(root, "tokens"))
		}, want: "symbolic link"},
		{name: "directory not recorded", dir: "tokens", setup: func(t *testing.T, root string, _ *fakeOwnership) {
			if err := os.Mkdir(filepath.Join(root, "tokens"), 0o700); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
		}, want: "is not Darkpanel's"},
		{name: "directory open to others", dir: "tokens", setup: func(t *testing.T, root string, own *fakeOwnership) {
			if err := os.Mkdir(filepath.Join(root, "tokens"), 0o700); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if err := os.Chmod(filepath.Join(root, "tokens"), 0o750); err != nil { //nolint:gosec // G302: the unsafe mode under test
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			mgdRecord(t, own, filepath.Join(root, "tokens"))
		}, want: "has mode 750"},
		{name: "directory of another user", dir: "tokens", setup: func(t *testing.T, root string, own *fakeOwnership) {
			if os.Geteuid() != 0 {
				t.Skip("needs root to own a directory by another user")
			}
			if err := os.Mkdir(filepath.Join(root, "tokens"), 0o700); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if err := os.Chown(filepath.Join(root, "tokens"), 12345, 12345); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			mgdRecord(t, own, filepath.Join(root, "tokens"))
		}, want: "owned by uid 12345"},
		{name: "parent writable by others", dir: "tokens", setup: func(t *testing.T, root string, _ *fakeOwnership) {
			if err := os.Chmod(root, 0o707); err != nil { //nolint:gosec // G302: the unsafe mode under test
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
		}, want: "writable by group or others"},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			f, own, root := mgdFiles(t)
			if c.setup != nil {
				c.setup(t, root, own)
			}
			dir := filepath.Join(root, c.dir)
			err := f.WriteManaged(context.Background(), "mgd", dir, "a.token", []byte("x"), 0o600, os.Geteuid(), os.Getegid())
			if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), c.want) {
				t.Errorf("WriteManaged = %v, want a refusal containing %q", err, c.want)
			}
			err = f.RemoveManaged(context.Background(), "mgd", dir, "a.token")
			if c.setup != nil && (err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), c.want)) {
				t.Errorf("RemoveManaged = %v, want a refusal containing %q", err, c.want)
			}
			for _, d := range []string{"real", "tokens"} {
				if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(root, d, "a.token")); !errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
					t.Errorf("a refused write created %s/a.token", d)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}
```

```go
package platform

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io/fs"
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"

	"golang.org/x/sys/unix"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
)

// managedDirMode is the mode of a managed directory: its files may be
// secrets (tunnel tokens), so only root reads them.
const managedDirMode = 0o700

// managedDefaultName is a managed directory's file-name pattern when the
// declaration sets none.
var managedDefaultName = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`)

// WriteManaged writes the regular file name directly inside dir, which module
// declares as kind managed-dir, with data, mode's permission bits and the
// owner uid:gid. The directory is recorded, then created root-owned with mode
// 0700, on the first write; an existing directory the ownership store does not
// record as module's is refused.
func (f *Files) WriteManaged(ctx context.Context, module, dir, name string, data []byte, mode fs.FileMode, uid, gid int) error {
	op, err := f.declaredKind(module, dir, core.OwnedManagedDir)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := managedName(op, name); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer f.lock(dir)()
	fd, err := f.openManaged(ctx, module, dir, true)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer func() { _ = unix.Close(fd) }()
	return writeFileAt(fd, name, filepath.Join(dir, name), data, mode, uid, gid)
}

// RemoveManaged removes the file name from dir, which module declares as kind
// managed-dir. A missing directory or name is not an error, a symlink is
// unlinked without being followed, and a subdirectory or a directory the
// ownership store does not record as module's is refused.
func (f *Files) RemoveManaged(ctx context.Context, module, dir, name string) error {
	op, err := f.declaredKind(module, dir, core.OwnedManagedDir)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := managedName(op, name); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer f.lock(dir)()
	fd, err := f.openManaged(ctx, module, dir, false)
	if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
		return nil
	}
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer func() { _ = unix.Close(fd) }()
	path := filepath.Join(dir, name)
	var st unix.Stat_t
	err = unix.Fstatat(fd, name, &st, unix.AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, unix.ENOENT):
		return nil
	case err != nil:
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: stat %s: %w", path, err)
	case st.Mode&unix.S_IFMT == unix.S_IFDIR:
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: %s is a directory", path)
	}
	if err := unix.Unlinkat(fd, name, 0); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, unix.ENOENT) {
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: remove %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	if err := unix.Fsync(fd); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: sync directory %s: %w", dir, err)
	}
	return nil
}

// managedName refuses a name that is not one flat entry matching the
// declaration's Pattern, or the default pattern without one.
func managedName(op core.OwnedPath, name string) error {
	pattern := managedDefaultName
	if op.Pattern != "" {
		var err error
		if pattern, err = regexp.Compile(op.Pattern); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("platform: managed directory %s: pattern: %w", op.Path, err)
		}
	}
	if name == "." || name == ".." || filepath.Base(name) != name || !pattern.MatchString(name) {
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: %q is not a valid file name in %s", name, op.Path)
	}
	return nil
}

// openManaged opens dir, through its parent opened as openDir opens one, and
// checks that it is module's recorded directory, owned like that parent with
// no group or other access. With create, a missing dir is recorded, then made
// with mode 0700; without, a missing dir fails with an error wrapping
// fs.ErrNotExist.
func (f *Files) openManaged(ctx context.Context, module, dir string, create bool) (int, error) {
	parentDir, name := filepath.Split(dir)
	pfd, err := f.openDir(parentDir)
	if err != nil {
		return -1, err
	}
	defer func() { _ = unix.Close(pfd) }()
	fd, err := openBeneath(pfd, name, unix.O_RDONLY|unix.O_DIRECTORY, 0)
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, unix.ENOENT) && create:
		if fd, err = f.createManaged(ctx, module, dir, pfd, name); err != nil {
			return -1, err
		}
	case err != nil:
		return -1, fmt.Errorf("platform: open directory %s: %w", dir, err)
	default:
		owned, err := f.cfg.Ownership.Owns(ctx, module, dir)
		if err == nil && !owned {
			err = fmt.Errorf("platform: directory %s exists and is not Darkpanel's", dir)
		}
		if err != nil {
			_ = unix.Close(fd)
			return -1, err
		}
	}
	var st unix.Stat_t
	if err := unix.Fstat(fd, &st); err != nil {
		_ = unix.Close(fd)
		return -1, fmt.Errorf("platform: stat directory %s: %w", dir, err)
	}
	switch {
	case int(st.Uid) != f.parentUID:
		_ = unix.Close(fd)
		return -1, fmt.Errorf("platform: directory %s is owned by uid %d, want %d", dir, st.Uid, f.parentUID)
	case st.Mode&0o077 != 0:
		_ = unix.Close(fd)
		return -1, fmt.Errorf("platform: directory %s has mode %o, want %o", dir, st.Mode&0o7777, managedDirMode)
	}
	return fd, nil
}

// createManaged records dir as module's, makes it in pfd as name and opens it.
func (f *Files) createManaged(ctx context.Context, module, dir string, pfd int, name string) (int, error) {
	// Recorded before the directory exists, so a crash after the mkdir still
	// leaves it for uninstall to find.
	entry := core.OwnedEntry{Path: dir, Module: module, Kind: core.OwnedManagedDir, CreatedAt: f.cfg.Clock.Now().UTC()}
	if err := f.cfg.Ownership.Record(ctx, entry); err != nil {
		return -1, err
	}
	if err := unix.Mkdirat(pfd, name, managedDirMode); err != nil {
		return -1, fmt.Errorf("platform: create directory %s: %w", dir, err)
	}
	if err := unix.Fsync(pfd); err != nil {
		return -1, fmt.Errorf("platform: sync directory of %s: %w", dir, err)
	}
	fd, err := openBeneath(pfd, name, unix.O_RDONLY|unix.O_DIRECTORY, 0)
	if err != nil {
		return -1, fmt.Errorf("platform: open directory %s: %w", dir, err)
	}
	// Mkdirat applies the umask; the mode must not depend on it.
	if err := unix.Fchmod(fd, managedDirMode); err != nil {
		_ = unix.Close(fd)
		return -1, fmt.Errorf("platform: chmod directory %s: %w", dir, err)
	}
	return fd, nil
}
```

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-opus-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 2 - risk 3 = 6

This task fills the four service-dir methods. `EnsureServiceDir` looks the declaration's `User` up at call time (`FilesConfig.LookupUser`, or `os/user.Lookup`), opens the parent with `openDir` (root-owned, no symlink) and the directory below it with `openBeneath`. A missing directory is recorded as kind `service-dir`, then made with `mkdirat(0700)`; an existing one must be recorded as the module's, or it is refused as pre-existing. The directory, then each declared subdirectory (made when missing), must be owned by the user; one still owned by root, which only an interrupted creation leaves, is `fchown`ed to the user and `fchmod`ed to 0700, and any other owner is refused. Both directories are `fsync`ed. `RenameIn` and `RemoveIn` take `name` or `<subdir>/name`, the subdirectory declared and the name matching `Pattern` or `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,127}$`; they open the directory and subdirectory with `openBeneath` and require the user to own both. `RenameIn` opens the source with `openBeneath(O_PATH)`, so a symlink fails with `ELOOP`, requires a regular file owned by the user, renames within one directory with `renameat` and `fsync`s it. `RemoveIn` unlinks a symlink without following it, refuses a regular file of another owner or anything but a regular file, and treats a missing directory or name as done. `RemoveServiceDir` refuses an existing directory the store does not record, lists the directory and each declared subdirectory (through a fresh descriptor, `fstatat(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)` per name) and fails, naming every undeclared directory, before it removes anything; then it unlinks every non-directory entry, removes the subdirectories and the directory with `unlinkat(AT_REMOVEDIR)`, `fsync`s the parent and forgets the record. A missing directory or parent only forgets the record. Test helpers carry the prefix `svd`. Security and data-loss risk: it runs alone.

```go
// svdFiles returns a writer for module "svd", which declares <root>/derp as a
// service-dir of user "svd-user" with the subdirectory certs, <root>/ghost as
// a service-dir of user "ghost-user", and <root>/plain as a managed-dir.
// svd-user resolves to uid:gid; ghost-user does not exist.
func svdFiles(t *testing.T, uid, gid int) (*Files, *fakeOwnership, string) {
	t.Helper()
	root := t.TempDir()
	f, own := fpFiles(t, FilesConfig{
		Owned: map[string][]core.OwnedPath{"svd": {
			{Path: filepath.Join(root, "derp"), Kind: core.OwnedServiceDir, User: "svd-user", Subdirs: []string{"certs"}},
			{Path: filepath.Join(root, "ghost"), Kind: core.OwnedServiceDir, User: "ghost-user"},
			{Path: filepath.Join(root, "plain"), Kind: core.OwnedManagedDir},
		}},
		LookupUser: func(name string) (int, int, error) {
			if name != "svd-user" {
				return 0, 0, errors.New("unknown user")
			}
			return uid, gid, nil
		},
	})
	return f, own, root
}

	t.Helper()

	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	st := info.Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t)
	return info.Mode(), int(st.Uid), int(st.Gid)
}

			if err := os.Mkdir(filepath.Join(root, "real"), 0o700); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if err := os.Symlink("real", filepath.Join(root, "derp")); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			svdRecord(t, own, filepath.Join(root, "derp"))
		}, want: "symbolic link"},
		{name: "parent of another user", root: true, dir: "derp", setup: func(t *testing.T, root string, _ *fakeOwnership) {
			if err := os.Chown(root, 12345, 12345); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
		}, want: "owned by uid 12345"},
		{name: "directory of another user", root: true, dir: "derp", setup: func(t *testing.T, root string, own *fakeOwnership) {
			svdMkdirOwned(t, filepath.Join(root, "derp"), 12345)
			svdRecord(t, own, filepath.Join(root, "derp"))
		}, want: "owned by uid 12345"},
		{name: "subdirectory of another user", root: true, dir: "derp", setup: func(t *testing.T, root string, own *fakeOwnership) {
			if err := os.Mkdir(filepath.Join(root, "derp"), 0o700); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			svdMkdirOwned(t, filepath.Join(root, "derp", "certs"), 12345)
			svdRecord(t, own, filepath.Join(root, "derp"))
		}, want: "owned by uid 12345"},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if c.root {
				svdNeedRoot(t)
			}
			f, own, root := svdFiles(t, os.Geteuid(), os.Getegid())
			if c.setup != nil {
				c.setup(t, root, own)
			}
			err := f.EnsureServiceDir(context.Background(), "svd", filepath.Join(root, c.dir))
			if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), c.want) {
				t.Fatalf("EnsureServiceDir = %v, want a refusal containing %q", err, c.want)
			}
			if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(root, "real", "certs")); !errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
				t.Error("a refused EnsureServiceDir created certs through the symlink")
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestServiceDirRenameRemove(t *testing.T) {
	uid, gid := os.Geteuid(), os.Getegid()

	dir := filepath.Join(root, "derp")

	}
	for _, rel := range []string{"a.crt", "certs/a.crt", "2001:db8::1.crt"} {
		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, rel), []byte(rel), 0o600); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	for _, c := range [][2]string{{"a.crt", "b.crt"}, {"certs/a.crt", "certs/b.crt"}, {"2001:db8::1.crt", "2001:db8::2.crt"}} {
		if err := f.RenameIn(ctx, "svd", dir, c[0], c[1]); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("RenameIn(%s, %s): %v", c[0], c[1], err)
		}
		if got := readFile(t, filepath.Join(dir, c[1])); got != c[0] {
			t.Errorf("%s holds %q, want the renamed %s", c[1], got, c[0])
		}
	}
	for _, rel := range []string{"b.crt", "certs/b.crt", "2001:db8::2.crt", "missing.crt", "certs/missing.crt"} {
		if err := f.RemoveIn(ctx, "svd", dir, rel); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("RemoveIn(%s): %v", rel, err)
		}
	}
	if names := dirNames(t, dir); !reflect.DeepEqual(names, []string{"certs"}) {
		t.Errorf("directory holds %v, want only certs", names)
	}
	if names := dirNames(t, filepath.Join(dir, "certs")); len(names) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("certs holds %v, want nothing", names)
	}
	victim := filepath.Join(root, "victim")
	if err := os.WriteFile(victim, []byte("keep\n"), 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.Symlink(victim, filepath.Join(dir, "certs", "l.crt")); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := f.RenameIn(ctx, "svd", dir, "certs/l.crt", "certs/m.crt"); err == nil {
		t.Error("RenameIn of a symlink succeeded")
	}
	if err := f.RemoveIn(ctx, "svd", dir, "certs/l.crt"); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("RemoveIn of a symlink: %v", err)
	}
	if got := readFile(t, victim); got != "keep\n" {
		t.Errorf("symlink target changed to %q", got)
	}
	if names := dirNames(t, filepath.Join(dir, "certs")); len(names) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("certs holds %v after the symlink was removed", names)
	}
}

// svdRecord records dir as module svd's service directory.
func svdRecord(t *testing.T, own *fakeOwnership, dir string) {
	t.Helper()
	if err := own.Record(context.Background(), core.OwnedEntry{Path: dir, Module: "svd", Kind: core.OwnedServiceDir, CreatedAt: filesNow}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}

// svdMkdirOwned makes the directory path with mode 0700, owned by uid.
func svdMkdirOwned(t *testing.T, path string, uid int) {
	t.Helper()
	if err := os.Mkdir(path, 0o700); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.Chown(path, uid, uid); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

```go
package platform

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io/fs"
	"os"
	"os/user"
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"
	"slices"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"golang.org/x/sys/unix"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
)

// serviceDirMode is the mode of a service directory and its subdirectories.
const serviceDirMode = 0o700

// serviceDefaultName is a service directory's file-name pattern when the
// declaration sets none; it admits a certificate named after an IPv6 address.
var serviceDefaultName = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,127}$`)

// EnsureServiceDir creates dir, which module declares as kind service-dir, and
// its declared subdirectories with mode 0700, owned by the declaration's User
// looked up now; dir is recorded before it is created. An existing dir must be
// recorded as module's, and it and its subdirectories owned by User; one left
// owned by root by an interrupted creation is handed to User. Other entries
// are the service's and are not checked.
func (f *Files) EnsureServiceDir(ctx context.Context, module, dir string) error {
	op, err := f.declaredKind(module, dir, core.OwnedServiceDir)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	uid, gid, err := f.lookupUser(op.User)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer f.lock(dir)()
	parentDir, name := filepath.Split(dir)
	pfd, err := f.openDir(parentDir)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer func() { _ = unix.Close(pfd) }()
	fd, err := openBeneath(pfd, name, unix.O_RDONLY|unix.O_DIRECTORY, 0)
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, unix.ENOENT):
		// Recorded before the directory exists, so a crash after the mkdir
		// still leaves it for uninstall to find.
		entry := core.OwnedEntry{Path: dir, Module: module, Kind: core.OwnedServiceDir, CreatedAt: f.cfg.Clock.Now().UTC()}
		if err := f.cfg.Ownership.Record(ctx, entry); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if fd, err = makeServiceDir(pfd, name, dir); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	case err != nil:
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: open directory %s: %w", dir, err)
	default:
		owned, err := f.cfg.Ownership.Owns(ctx, module, dir)
		if err == nil && !owned {
			err = fmt.Errorf("platform: directory %s exists and is not Darkpanel's", dir)
		}
		if err != nil {
			_ = unix.Close(fd)
			return err
		}
	}
	defer func() { _ = unix.Close(fd) }()
	if err := f.handOver(fd, dir, uid, gid); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	for _, sub := range op.Subdirs {
		path := filepath.Join(dir, sub)
		sfd, err := openBeneath(fd, sub, unix.O_RDONLY|unix.O_DIRECTORY, 0)
		if errors.Is(err, unix.ENOENT) {
			sfd, err = makeServiceDir(fd, sub, path)
		} else if err != nil {
			err = fmt.Errorf("platform: open directory %s: %w", path, err)
		}
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		err = f.handOver(sfd, path, uid, gid)
		_ = unix.Close(sfd)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	if err := unix.Fsync(fd); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: sync directory %s: %w", dir, err)
	}
	if err := unix.Fsync(pfd); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: sync directory of %s: %w", dir, err)
	}
	return nil
}

// RenameIn renames the regular file from to to, both names in dir, which
// module declares as kind service-dir, or both in the same declared
// subdirectory of it ("certs/a.crt"). The file must be owned by the
// declaration's User; a symlink is refused.
func (f *Files) RenameIn(ctx context.Context, module, dir, from, to string) error {
	op, err := f.declaredKind(module, dir, core.OwnedServiceDir)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	fromSub, fromName, err := serviceEntry(op, from)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	toSub, toName, err := serviceEntry(op, to)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if fromSub != toSub {
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: rename %s to %s in %s: not in the same directory", from, to, dir)
	}
	uid, _, err := f.lookupUser(op.User)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer f.lock(dir)()
	fd, err := f.openServiceLoc(dir, fromSub, uid)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer func() { _ = unix.Close(fd) }()
	path := filepath.Join(dir, from)
	if err := ownedRegular(fd, fromName, path, uid); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := unix.Renameat(fd, fromName, fd, toName); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: rename %s to %s: %w", path, filepath.Join(dir, to), err)
	}
	if err := unix.Fsync(fd); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: sync directory of %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	return nil
}

// RemoveIn removes the file name from dir, which module declares as kind
// service-dir, or from a declared subdirectory of it ("certs/a.crt"). A
// regular file must be owned by the declaration's User; a symlink is unlinked
// without being followed; a missing directory or name is not an error.
func (f *Files) RemoveIn(ctx context.Context, module, dir, name string) error {
	op, err := f.declaredKind(module, dir, core.OwnedServiceDir)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	sub, base, err := serviceEntry(op, name)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	uid, _, err := f.lookupUser(op.User)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer f.lock(dir)()
	fd, err := f.openServiceLoc(dir, sub, uid)
	if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
		return nil
	}
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer func() { _ = unix.Close(fd) }()
	path := filepath.Join(dir, name)
	var st unix.Stat_t
	err = unix.Fstatat(fd, base, &st, unix.AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, unix.ENOENT):
		return nil
	case err != nil:
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: stat %s: %w", path, err)
	case st.Mode&unix.S_IFMT == unix.S_IFLNK:
	case st.Mode&unix.S_IFMT != unix.S_IFREG:
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: %s is not a regular file", path)
	case int(st.Uid) != uid:
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: %s is owned by uid %d, want %d", path, st.Uid, uid)
	}
	if err := unix.Unlinkat(fd, base, 0); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, unix.ENOENT) {
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: remove %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	if err := unix.Fsync(fd); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: sync directory of %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	return nil
}

// RemoveServiceDir removes dir, which module declares as kind service-dir:
// every non-directory entry of each declared subdirectory and of dir (a
// symlink is unlinked, never followed), then the subdirectories and dir, and
// forgets the record. A directory it does not declare fails the call, naming
// it, before anything is removed; a missing dir is not an error. A dir that
// exists but is not recorded as module's is refused.
func (f *Files) RemoveServiceDir(ctx context.Context, module, dir string) error {
	op, err := f.declaredKind(module, dir, core.OwnedServiceDir)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer f.lock(dir)()
	parentDir, name := filepath.Split(dir)
	pfd, err := f.openDir(parentDir)
	if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
		return f.cfg.Ownership.Forget(ctx, module, dir, "")
	}
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer func() { _ = unix.Close(pfd) }()
	fd, err := openBeneath(pfd, name, unix.O_RDONLY|unix.O_DIRECTORY, 0)
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, unix.ENOENT):
		return f.cfg.Ownership.Forget(ctx, module, dir, "")
	case err != nil:
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: open directory %s: %w", dir, err)
	}
	defer func() { _ = unix.Close(fd) }()
	owned, err := f.cfg.Ownership.Owns(ctx, module, dir)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if !owned {
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: directory %s exists and is not Darkpanel's", dir)
	}
	files, subs, err := serviceListing(fd, dir)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	var undeclared []string
	subFDs := map[string]int{}
	subFiles := map[string][]string{}
	defer func() {
		for _, sfd := range subFDs {
			_ = unix.Close(sfd)
		}
	}()
	for _, sub := range subs {
		if !slices.Contains(op.Subdirs, sub) {
			undeclared = append(undeclared, sub)
			continue
		}
		sfd, err := openBeneath(fd, sub, unix.O_RDONLY|unix.O_DIRECTORY, 0)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("platform: open directory %s: %w", filepath.Join(dir, sub), err)
		}
		subFDs[sub] = sfd
		inner, innerDirs, err := serviceListing(sfd, filepath.Join(dir, sub))
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		subFiles[sub] = inner
		for _, d := range innerDirs {
			undeclared = append(undeclared, sub+"/"+d)
		}
	}
	if len(undeclared) > 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: %s holds directories Darkpanel does not declare, so nothing was removed: %s",
			dir, strings.Join(undeclared, ", "))
	}
	for _, sub := range subs {
		if err := unlinkAll(subFDs[sub], filepath.Join(dir, sub), subFiles[sub]); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if err := unix.Unlinkat(fd, sub, unix.AT_REMOVEDIR); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("platform: remove directory %s: %w", filepath.Join(dir, sub), err)
		}
	}
	if err := unlinkAll(fd, dir, files); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := unix.Unlinkat(pfd, name, unix.AT_REMOVEDIR); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: remove directory %s: %w", dir, err)
	}
	if err := unix.Fsync(pfd); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: sync directory of %s: %w", dir, err)
	}
	return f.cfg.Ownership.Forget(ctx, module, dir, "")
}

// lookupUser returns the ids of the system user name.
func (f *Files) lookupUser(name string) (uid, gid int, err error) {
	if f.cfg.LookupUser != nil {
		if uid, gid, err = f.cfg.LookupUser(name); err != nil {
			return 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("platform: look up user %s: %w", name, err)
		}
		return uid, gid, nil
	}
	u, err := user.Lookup(name)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("platform: look up user %s: %w", name, err)
	}
	if uid, err = strconv.Atoi(u.Uid); err == nil {
		gid, err = strconv.Atoi(u.Gid)
	}
	if err != nil {
		return 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("platform: user %s: %w", name, err)
	}
	return uid, gid, nil
}

// makeServiceDir makes name in the directory pfd with mode 0700 and opens it.
func makeServiceDir(pfd int, name, path string) (int, error) {
	if err := unix.Mkdirat(pfd, name, serviceDirMode); err != nil {
		return -1, fmt.Errorf("platform: create directory %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	fd, err := openBeneath(pfd, name, unix.O_RDONLY|unix.O_DIRECTORY, 0)
	if err != nil {
		return -1, fmt.Errorf("platform: open directory %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	// Mkdirat applies the umask; the mode must not depend on it.
	if err := unix.Fchmod(fd, serviceDirMode); err != nil {
		_ = unix.Close(fd)
		return -1, fmt.Errorf("platform: chmod directory %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	return fd, nil
}

// handOver accepts the directory fd when uid owns it, gives it to uid:gid
// with mode 0700 when root, its creator, still owns it, and refuses it
// otherwise. Only root can create a root-owned entry, so handing one over
// never takes a directory from anyone else.
func (f *Files) handOver(fd int, path string, uid, gid int) error {
	var st unix.Stat_t
	if err := unix.Fstat(fd, &st); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: stat directory %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	switch int(st.Uid) {
	case uid:
		return nil
	case f.parentUID:
		if err := unix.Fchown(fd, uid, gid); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("platform: chown directory %s: %w", path, err)
		}
		// After Fchown, which clears set-group-ID bits.
		if err := unix.Fchmod(fd, serviceDirMode); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("platform: chmod directory %s: %w", path, err)
		}
		return nil
	default:
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: directory %s is owned by uid %d, want %d", path, st.Uid, uid)
	}
}

// serviceEntry splits rel, "name" or "<subdir>/name", into the declared
// subdirectory ("" for dir itself) and a name matching the declaration's
// Pattern, or the default pattern without one.
func serviceEntry(op core.OwnedPath, rel string) (sub, name string, err error) {
	name = rel
	if i := strings.IndexByte(rel, '/'); i >= 0 {
		sub, name = rel[:i], rel[i+1:]
		if !slices.Contains(op.Subdirs, sub) {
			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("platform: %q: %s declares no subdirectory %q", rel, op.Path, sub)
		}
	}
	pattern := serviceDefaultName
	if op.Pattern != "" {
		if pattern, err = regexp.Compile(op.Pattern); err != nil {
			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("platform: service directory %s: pattern: %w", op.Path, err)
		}
	}
	if name == "." || name == ".." || strings.Contains(name, "/") || !pattern.MatchString(name) {
		return "", "", fmt.Errorf("platform: %q is not a valid file name in %s", rel, op.Path)
	}
	return sub, name, nil
}

// openServiceLoc opens dir, through its parent opened as openDir opens one,
// or its subdirectory sub, checking that each is owned by uid. A missing dir
// or sub fails with an error wrapping fs.ErrNotExist.
func (f *Files) openServiceLoc(dir, sub string, uid int) (int, error) {
	parentDir, name := filepath.Split(dir)
	pfd, err := f.openDir(parentDir)
	if err != nil {
		return -1, err
	}
	defer func() { _ = unix.Close(pfd) }()
	fd, err := openOwnedDir(pfd, name, dir, uid)
	if err != nil || sub == "" {
		return fd, err
	}
	defer func() { _ = unix.Close(fd) }()
	return openOwnedDir(fd, sub, filepath.Join(dir, sub), uid)
}

// openOwnedDir opens the directory name below dirfd and checks that uid owns
// it.
func openOwnedDir(dirfd int, name, path string, uid int) (int, error) {
	fd, err := openBeneath(dirfd, name, unix.O_RDONLY|unix.O_DIRECTORY, 0)
	if err != nil {
		return -1, fmt.Errorf("platform: open directory %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	var st unix.Stat_t
	if err := unix.Fstat(fd, &st); err != nil {
		_ = unix.Close(fd)
		return -1, fmt.Errorf("platform: stat directory %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	if int(st.Uid) != uid {
		_ = unix.Close(fd)
		return -1, fmt.Errorf("platform: directory %s is owned by uid %d, want %d", path, st.Uid, uid)
	}
	return fd, nil
}

// ownedRegular checks that name in dirfd, opened without following a
// symlink, is a regular file owned by uid.
func ownedRegular(dirfd int, name, path string, uid int) error {
	fd, err := openBeneath(dirfd, name, unix.O_PATH, 0)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: open %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	defer func() { _ = unix.Close(fd) }()
	var st unix.Stat_t
	if err := unix.Fstat(fd, &st); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: stat %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	switch {
	case st.Mode&unix.S_IFMT != unix.S_IFREG:
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: %s is not a regular file", path)
	case int(st.Uid) != uid:
		return fmt.Errorf("platform: %s is owned by uid %d, want %d", path, st.Uid, uid)
	}
	return nil
}

// serviceListing returns the names in the directory fd, split into
// non-directories and directories; a symlink is a non-directory.
func serviceListing(fd int, path string) (files, dirs []string, err error) {
	// A descriptor of its own, so the listing does not move fd's offset.
	lfd, err := openBeneath(fd, ".", unix.O_RDONLY|unix.O_DIRECTORY, 0)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("platform: open directory %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	list := os.NewFile(uintptr(lfd), path)
	names, err := list.Readdirnames(-1)
	_ = list.Close()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("platform: list directory %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	slices.Sort(names)
	for _, n := range names {
		var st unix.Stat_t
		if err := unix.Fstatat(fd, n, &st, unix.AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW); err != nil {
			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("platform: stat %s: %w", filepath.Join(path, n), err)
		}
		if st.Mode&unix.S_IFMT == unix.S_IFDIR {
			dirs = append(dirs, n)
		} else {
			files = append(files, n)
		}
	}
	return files, dirs, nil
}

// unlinkAll unlinks names, none a directory, from the directory fd.
func unlinkAll(fd int, path string, names []string) error {
	for _, n := range names {
		if err := unix.Unlinkat(fd, n, 0); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, unix.ENOENT) {
			return fmt.Errorf("platform: remove %s: %w", filepath.Join(path, n), err)
		}
	}
	return nil
}
```

```go
// mscReached records the dispatcher calls that passed authorization.
func mscReached(h *harness) *[]string {
	var reached []string
	h.disp.ReadFunc = func(_ context.Context, _ core.Principal, _ string, a core.ActionRef, _ json.RawMessage) (json.RawMessage, error) {

func TestMinScopeOnActionRoutes(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHarnessWith(t, mscModule{})
	reached := mscReached(h)
	operate, admin := h.token(core.ScopeOperate), h.token(core.ScopeAdmin)
	const host = "/api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/"
	body := `{"input":{"name":"x"}}`
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		path, token string
		need        core.Scope // "" when the call is authorized
	}{
		{host + "msc.secret.list/v1/read", operate, core.ScopeAdmin},
		{host + "msc.secret.list/v1/read", admin, ""},
		{host + "msc.key.rotate/v1/plan", operate, core.ScopeAdmin},
		{host + "msc.key.rotate/v1/plan", admin, ""},
		{host + "msc.item.add/v1/plan", operate, ""},
		{"/api/v1/actions/msc.stack.deploy/v1/plan", operate, core.ScopeAdmin},
		{"/api/v1/actions/msc.stack.deploy/v1/plan", admin, ""},
	} {
		rec := h.serve(withToken(request("POST", tc.path, body), tc.token))
		if tc.need == "" {
			if rec.Code != 200 {
				t.Errorf("%s: %d %s, want it dispatched", tc.path, rec.Code, rec.Body)
			}
			continue
		}
		p := decodeProblem(t, rec, 403, errcode.Forbidden)
		if p.Detail != "this request needs the "+string(tc.need)+" scope" {
			t.Errorf("%s: detail %q, want it to name %s", tc.path, p.Detail, tc.need)
		}
	}
	want := []string{"read msc.secret.list", "plan msc.key.rotate", "plan msc.item.add", "plan msc.stack.deploy"}
	if !slices.Equal(*reached, want) {
		t.Errorf("the dispatcher saw %v, want %v", *reached, want)
	}
}
```

```go
// RequiredScope is the scope a principal needs for an action of class on
// side (spec section 10). Read actions need read. Mutating agent-side
// actions, the module actions, need operate for plan and apply, as their
// changes' confirm and revert do. Mutating controller-side actions, the
// core's token and module-enablement actions, need admin. An unknown class
// or side needs admin, so a mistake fails closed.
func RequiredScope(class core.Class, side core.Side) core.Scope {
	switch {
	case class == core.ClassRead:
		return core.ScopeRead
	case side == core.SideAgent &&
		(class == core.ClassRevertible || class == core.ClassCompensable || class == core.ClassIrreversible):
		return core.ScopeOperate
	default:
		return core.ScopeAdmin
	}
}
```

```go
// core.RequiredScope of its spec (spec 1.7).
func RequiredScope(class core.Class, side core.Side) core.Scope {
	return core.DefaultScope(class, side)
}
```

```go
// authorizeChange applies to a confirm or revert the scope of the change's
// own action, never of the route: RequiredScope of its class and side. v
// must be networkVisible, so an unregistered action is agent-side and its
// stored class decides.
func (s *Server) authorizeChange(p core.Principal, v core.ChangeView) error {
	class, side := v.Class, core.SideAgent
	if def, ok := s.cfg.Registry.Action(core.ActionRef{Name: v.Action, Version: v.Version}); ok {
		class, side = def.Spec.Class, def.Spec.Side
	}
	return authorize(p, RequiredScope(class, side))
}
```

```go
// authorizeChange applies to an operation on a change the scope of the
// change's own action, never of the route: core.RequiredScope of its spec,
// MinScope included. v must be networkVisible, so an unregistered action is
// agent-side and its stored class decides.
func (s *Server) authorizeChange(p core.Principal, v core.ChangeView) error {
	if def, ok := s.cfg.Registry.Action(core.ActionRef{Name: v.Action, Version: v.Version}); ok {
		return authorize(p, core.RequiredScope(def.Spec))
	}
	return authorize(p, RequiredScope(v.Class, core.SideAgent))
}
```

```go
			}
			identity, value, err := h.Reveal(ctx, Env{HostID: "h1"}, json.RawMessage(`{"name":"ada"}`))
			if err != nil || identity != "password of ada on h1" || string(value) != `{"user":"ada","password":"hunter2"}` {
				t.Errorf("Reveal = %q, %s, %v; want the identity and the unredacted value", identity, value, err)
			}
			if _, value, err := h.Reveal(ctx, Env{}, json.RawMessage(`{"name":"fail"}`)); err == nil || err.Error() != "no such user" || value != nil {
				t.Errorf("failing Reveal = %s, %v; want no value and the handler's error", value, err)
			}
			var coded *errcode.Error
			if _, _, err := h.Reveal(ctx, Env{}, json.RawMessage(`{"name":"ada","extra":1}`)); !errors.As(err, &coded) || coded.Code != errcode.InvalidInput {
				t.Errorf("unknown field: err = %v, want %s", err, errcode.InvalidInput)
			}
```

```go
func erasedReveal[In, Out any](reveal func(ctx context.Context, env Env, in In) (Revealed[Out], error)) func(context.Context, Env, json.RawMessage) (string, json.RawMessage, error) {
	return func(ctx context.Context, env Env, raw json.RawMessage) (string, json.RawMessage, error) {
		in, err := decode[In](raw)
		if err != nil {
			return "", nil, err
		}
		r, err := reveal(ctx, env, in)
		if err != nil {
			return "", nil, err
		}
		value, err := encode(r.Value)
		if err != nil {
			return "", nil, err
		}
		return r.Identity, value, nil
	}
}

// DefineReveal declares a reveal action: a read action that returns one
// stored secret once, served only by the reveal path, which audits
// Revealed.Identity. The value is encoded without redaction; secret fields of
// Out keep their tag, which marks them in the schema only. spec.MinScope must
// be admin.
func DefineReveal[In, Out any](spec ActionSpec, reveal func(ctx context.Context, env Env, in In) (Revealed[Out], error)) ActionDef {
	spec.Class, spec.Reveal = ClassRead, true
	return ActionDef{
		Spec: spec, InputType: typeOf[In](), OutputType: typeOf[Out](),
		Handler: ErasedHandler{Reveal: erasedReveal(reveal)},
	}
}

// DefineInternalRead declares an Internal read action: the controller
// dispatches it itself, through the reveal path, and the API and the CLI do
// not expose it.
func DefineInternalRead[In, Out any](spec ActionSpec, read func(ctx context.Context, env Env, in In) (Revealed[Out], error)) ActionDef {
	spec.Class, spec.Internal = ClassRead, true
	return ActionDef{
		Spec: spec, InputType: typeOf[In](), OutputType: typeOf[Out](),
		Handler: ErasedHandler{Reveal: erasedReveal(read)},
	}
}

// DefineResource declares a resource named "<module>.<resource>".
```

```go
// checkReveal applies the rules of reveal actions and Internal reads (spec
// 1.7, 1.14): both are read actions whose only handler is Reveal, never both
// at once, and a reveal action needs admin. Every other action has no Reveal
// handler.
func checkReveal(a ActionDef) error {
	s, h := a.Spec, a.Handler
	ref := a.Ref()
	flagged := s.Reveal || s.Internal
	switch {
	case s.Reveal && s.Internal:
		return fmt.Errorf("action %s: an action is a reveal action or an internal read, not both", ref)
	case flagged && s.Class != ClassRead:
		return fmt.Errorf("action %s: reveal actions and internal reads are read actions", ref)
	case flagged && (h.Reveal == nil || h.Read != nil):
		return fmt.Errorf("action %s: a reveal action or internal read has a Reveal handler and no Read handler", ref)
	case !flagged && h.Reveal != nil:
		return fmt.Errorf("action %s: only reveal actions and internal reads have a Reveal handler", ref)
	case s.Reveal && s.MinScope != ScopeAdmin:
		return fmt.Errorf("action %s: a reveal action declares MinScope admin", ref)
	}
	return nil
}
```

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: C1 (`GuardSpec`, `Guarded`, `Guard.Overridable`, `Guard.Overridden`), C7 (`newFixtureWith`), C10 (the registry accepts `gfx`).
- Produces: C18; the shared fixture `gfx`, with `newGfx(t *testing.T) (*fixture, *gfxHost)`.

**Items:** 48, 59

**Depends on:** Task 6, Task 21, Task 31

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-sonnet-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 2 - risk 2 = 5

For an action that declares `Guards`, the engine refuses at plan an `overrides` entry that is not one of its `Overridable` guard ids (`request.invalid_input`, field `/overrides/<i>`), and after every handler `Plan`, at plan and at apply's re-plan, it fails with `internal` a reported guard the action does not declare, or one reported overridden that is not overridable, not in the input's `overrides` or not passing. It copies `Overridable` from the `GuardSpec` and adds one diff line `guard <id> overridden: <message>` per overridden guard, so the stored plan, its diff and, through the stored input, the journal record the override. Both checks run in `makePlan`, which plans, repair plans and composite plans share, and in `recheck`. Actions without `Guards` are unchanged (ruling R7). The "fails with internal" errors are plain errors, as the engine's other module mistakes are (`returned no confirmation phrase`), which `errcode.From` reports as `internal`. It creates the shared fixture `gfx`: `gfxModule{h *gfxHost}`, `gfxInput`, `gfxHost` with `seen()` (every handler call's method and `Env.Call`) and `setExtra(ids...)` (guard ids every later plan reports passing, the host flipping between plan and apply), and `newGfx`.
