```go
package lifecycle

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"slices"
	"sync"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
)

// The fixture module "gfx" has one guarded action, gfx.rule.set, whose plan
// reports its two declared guards, and its repair action gfx.rule.fix.

var (
	refGfxSet = core.ActionRef{Name: "gfx.rule.set", Version: 1}
	refGfxFix = core.ActionRef{Name: "gfx.rule.fix", Version: 1}
)

// gfxInput is gfx.rule.set's input. Failing names the declared guards its
// plan fails unless overridden; Extra adds one passing guard per id, which
// gfx.rule.set does not declare.
type gfxInput struct {
	core.Guarded
	Name    string   `json:"name"`
	Failing []string `json:"failing,omitempty"`
	Extra   []string `json:"extra,omitempty"`
}

type gfxFixInput struct {
	Name string `json:"name"`
}

type gfxOut struct {
	Name string `json:"name"`
}

// gfxCall is one handler call of module gfx: its method and the Env.Call it
// saw.
type gfxCall struct {
	Method string
	Call   core.CallContext
}

// gfxHost is module gfx's host: the rules it holds, the extra guard ids every
// plan of gfx.rule.set reports passing, and every handler call.
type gfxHost struct {
	mu    sync.Mutex
	rules map[string]bool
	extra []string
	calls []gfxCall
}

func (h *gfxHost) saw(method string, env core.Env) {
	h.mu.Lock()
	defer h.mu.Unlock()
	h.calls = append(h.calls, gfxCall{Method: method, Call: env.Call})
}

// seen returns the handler calls so far.
func (h *gfxHost) seen() []gfxCall {
	h.mu.Lock()
	defer h.mu.Unlock()
	return slices.Clone(h.calls)
}

// setExtra makes every later plan of gfx.rule.set report ids passing too.
func (h *gfxHost) setExtra(ids ...string) {
	h.mu.Lock()
	defer h.mu.Unlock()
	h.extra = ids
}

type gfxSet struct{ host *gfxHost }

func (x gfxSet) Plan(_ context.Context, env core.Env, in gfxInput) (core.PlanOutcome, error) {
	x.host.saw("Plan", env)
	x.host.mu.Lock()
	defer x.host.mu.Unlock()
	out := core.PlanOutcome{
		Diff:      []core.DiffLine{{Op: "+", Text: "rule " + in.Name}},
		StateHash: fmt.Sprint(x.host.rules[in.Name]),
	}
	for _, id := range []string{"gfx.lockout", "gfx.quota"} {
		g := core.Guard{ID: id, OK: true, Message: id + " holds"}
		if slices.Contains(in.Failing, id) {
			g.OK, g.Message = false, id+" fails"
			if slices.Contains(in.Overrides, id) {
				g.OK, g.Overridden = true, true
			}
		}
		out.Guards = append(out.Guards, g)
	}
	for _, id := range slices.Concat(in.Extra, x.host.extra) {
		out.Guards = append(out.Guards, core.Guard{ID: id, OK: true, Message: id + " holds"})
	}
	return out, nil
}

func (x gfxSet) Apply(_ context.Context, env core.Env, in gfxInput) (gfxOut, error) {
	x.host.saw("Apply", env)
	x.host.mu.Lock()
	defer x.host.mu.Unlock()
	x.host.rules[in.Name] = true
	return gfxOut{Name: in.Name}, nil
}

func (x gfxSet) Verify(_ context.Context, env core.Env, in gfxInput, _ gfxOut) error {
	x.host.saw("Verify", env)
	x.host.mu.Lock()
	defer x.host.mu.Unlock()
	if !x.host.rules[in.Name] {
		return fmt.Errorf("rule %s is missing", in.Name)
	}
	return nil
}

func (x gfxSet) Snapshot(_ context.Context, env core.Env, in gfxInput) ([]byte, error) {
	x.host.saw("Snapshot", env)
	x.host.mu.Lock()
	defer x.host.mu.Unlock()
	return json.Marshal(map[string]bool{in.Name: x.host.rules[in.Name]})
}

func (x gfxSet) Revert(_ context.Context, env core.Env, snapshot []byte) (core.RevertOutcome, error) {
	x.host.saw("Revert", env)
	var before map[string]bool
	if err := json.Unmarshal(snapshot, &before); err != nil {
		return core.RevertOutcome{}, err
	}
	x.host.mu.Lock()
	defer x.host.mu.Unlock()
	for name, present := range before {
		if present {
			x.host.rules[name] = true
		} else {
			delete(x.host.rules, name)
		}
	}
	return core.RevertOutcome{}, nil
}

type gfxFix struct{ host *gfxHost }

func (x gfxFix) Plan(_ context.Context, env core.Env, in gfxFixInput) (core.PlanOutcome, error) {
	x.host.saw("Plan", env)
	return core.PlanOutcome{Diff: []core.DiffLine{{Op: "+", Text: "rule " + in.Name}}}, nil
}

func (x gfxFix) Apply(_ context.Context, env core.Env, in gfxFixInput) (gfxOut, error) {
	x.host.saw("Apply", env)
	x.host.mu.Lock()
	defer x.host.mu.Unlock()
	x.host.rules[in.Name] = true
	return gfxOut(in), nil
}

func (x gfxFix) Verify(_ context.Context, env core.Env, _ gfxFixInput, _ gfxOut) error {
	x.host.saw("Verify", env)
	return nil
}

type gfxModule struct{ h *gfxHost }

func (m gfxModule) Manifest() core.Manifest {
	return core.Manifest{ID: "gfx", Version: 1, Actions: []core.ActionDef{
		core.DefineRevertible(core.ActionSpec{
			Name: refGfxSet.Name, Version: 1, Side: core.SideAgent, LockKeys: []string{"gfx"}, RepairedBy: refGfxFix.Name,
			Guards: []core.GuardSpec{{ID: "gfx.lockout", Overridable: true}, {ID: "gfx.quota"}},
		}, gfxSet{m.h}),
		core.DefineMutating(core.ActionSpec{
			Name: refGfxFix.Name, Version: 1, Class: core.ClassCompensable, Side: core.SideAgent,
			LockKeys: []string{"gfx"}, ForwardOnly: true, Converges: true,
		}, gfxFix{m.h}),
	}}
}

// newGfx is a fixture whose registry also has module gfx, and gfx's host.
func newGfx(t *testing.T) (*fixture, *gfxHost) {
	t.Helper()
	h := &gfxHost{rules: map[string]bool{}}
	return newFixtureWith(t, gfxModule{h}), h
}
```

```go
package lifecycle

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"

	"slices"

	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"

func TestCheckGuards(t *testing.T) {
	def := core.ActionDef{Spec: core.ActionSpec{Name: "gfx.rule.set", Version: 1,
		Guards: []core.GuardSpec{{ID: "gfx.lockout", Overridable: true}, {ID: "gfx.quota"}}}}
	lockout := core.Guard{ID: "gfx.lockout", OK: true, Overridden: true, Message: "m"}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name      string
		def       core.ActionDef
		overrides []string
		guards    []core.Guard
		want      []core.Guard // nil: fails with internal
		diff      []core.DiffLine
	}{
		{"declared guards", def, nil, []core.Guard{{ID: "gfx.lockout", Message: "m"}, {ID: "gfx.quota", OK: true}},
			[]core.Guard{{ID: "gfx.lockout", Message: "m", Overridable: true}, {ID: "gfx.quota", OK: true}}, nil},
		{"an overridden guard", def, []string{"gfx.lockout"}, []core.Guard{lockout},
			[]core.Guard{{ID: "gfx.lockout", OK: true, Overridden: true, Overridable: true, Message: "m"}},
			[]core.DiffLine{{Op: " ", Text: "guard gfx.lockout overridden: m"}}},
		{"an undeclared guard", def, nil, []core.Guard{{ID: "gfx.other", OK: true}}, nil, nil},
		{"overridden but not overridable", def, []string{"gfx.quota"},
			[]core.Guard{{ID: "gfx.quota", OK: true, Overridden: true}}, nil, nil},
		{"overridden but not in overrides", def, nil, []core.Guard{lockout}, nil, nil},
		{"overridden and failing", def, []string{"gfx.lockout"},
			[]core.Guard{{ID: "gfx.lockout", Overridden: true}}, nil, nil},
		{"an action without guards", core.ActionDef{Spec: core.ActionSpec{Name: "fix.item.set", Version: 1}}, nil,
			[]core.Guard{{ID: "anything", Overridden: true}}, []core.Guard{{ID: "anything", Overridden: true}}, nil},
	} {
		out := core.PlanOutcome{Guards: tc.guards}
		err := checkGuards(tc.def, tc.overrides, &out)
		switch {
		case tc.want == nil:
			if errcode.From(err).Code != errcode.Internal {
				t.Errorf("%s: checkGuards = %v, want an internal error", tc.name, err)
			}
		case err != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(out.Guards, tc.want) || !reflect.DeepEqual(out.Diff, tc.diff):
			t.Errorf("%s: checkGuards = %v, guards %+v, diff %+v; want guards %+v, diff %+v",
				tc.name, err, out.Guards, out.Diff, tc.want, tc.diff)
		}
	}
}

func TestPlanRefusesUnknownOverride(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		overrides string
		field     string
	}{
		{`["gfx.quota"]`, "/overrides/0"},
		{`["nope"]`, "/overrides/0"},
		{`["gfx.lockout","nope"]`, "/overrides/1"},
	} {
		f, _ := newGfx(t)
		_, err := f.eng.Plan(context.Background(), alice, refGfxSet,
			json.RawMessage(`{"name":"a","overrides":`+tc.overrides+`}`), core.PlanOptions{})
		wantCode(t, err, errcode.InvalidInput)
		if fields := errcode.From(err).Fields; len(fields) != 1 || fields[0].Path != tc.field {
			t.Errorf("overrides %s: field errors %+v, want %s", tc.overrides, fields, tc.field)
		}
		if n := f.count("SELECT count(*) FROM core_plans"); n != 0 {
			t.Errorf("overrides %s: %d plans stored, want none", tc.overrides, n)
		}
	}
}

func TestPlanOverriddenGuard(t *testing.T) {
	f, _ := newGfx(t)
	pl := f.plan(alice, refGfxSet, `{"name":"a","failing":["gfx.lockout"],"overrides":["gfx.lockout"]}`)
	want := []core.Guard{
		{ID: "gfx.lockout", OK: true, Overridden: true, Overridable: true, Message: "gfx.lockout fails"},
		{ID: "gfx.quota", OK: true, Message: "gfx.quota holds"},
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(pl.Guards, want) {
		t.Errorf("guards %+v\nwant %+v", pl.Guards, want)
	}
	if line := (core.DiffLine{Op: " ", Text: "guard gfx.lockout overridden: gfx.lockout fails"}); !slices.Contains(pl.Diff, line) {
		t.Errorf("diff %+v lacks %+v", pl.Diff, line)
	}
	var stored []core.Guard
	var raw string
	if err := f.db.Read().QueryRow("SELECT guards_json FROM core_plans WHERE id = ?", pl.PlanID).Scan(&raw); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(raw), &stored); err != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(stored, want) {
		t.Errorf("stored guards %s (%v), want %+v", raw, err, want)
	}
	v := f.apply(alice, pl.PlanID, core.ApplyOptions{})
	if v.State != core.StatePending {
		t.Fatalf("state %s, want pending", v.State)
	}
	if e := f.lastEntry(); e.Phase != phaseApply || !strings.Contains(string(e.Input), `"overrides":["gfx.lockout"]`) {
		t.Errorf("journal entry %s with input %s, want the apply recording the override", e.Phase, e.Input)
	}
}

func TestPlanFailingGuards(t *testing.T) {
```

```go
package lifecycle

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"slices"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
)

// guardOverrides returns the overrides of a guarded action's canonical input,
// refusing an entry that is not an Overridable guard of the action with
// request.invalid_input (spec 1.5). An action without Guards has none.
func guardOverrides(def core.ActionDef, input json.RawMessage) ([]string, error) {
	if len(def.Spec.Guards) == 0 {
		return nil, nil
	}
	var in struct {
		Overrides []string `json:"overrides"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(input, &in); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("lifecycle: read the overrides of %s: %w", def.Ref(), err)
	}
	var fields []errcode.FieldError
	for i, id := range in.Overrides {
		if !slices.ContainsFunc(def.Spec.Guards, func(g core.GuardSpec) bool { return g.ID == id && g.Overridable }) {
			fields = append(fields, errcode.FieldError{
				Path: fmt.Sprintf("/overrides/%d", i), Message: fmt.Sprintf("%s has no overridable guard %q", def.Ref(), id),
			})
		}
	}
	if len(fields) > 0 {
		return nil, &errcode.Error{Code: errcode.InvalidInput, Detail: "overrides names a guard that cannot be overridden", Fields: fields}
	}
	return in.Overrides, nil
}

// checkGuards checks the guards a guarded action's Plan reported against its
// declaration (spec 1.5). An undeclared id, or a guard reported overridden
// that is not Overridable, not in overrides or not passing, is the module's
// mistake and fails with internal. It sets each guard's Overridable from its
// GuardSpec and adds one diff line per overridden guard, so the plan, the
// diff and the audit record the override. An action without Guards is left
// as it is.
func checkGuards(def core.ActionDef, overrides []string, out *core.PlanOutcome) error {
	if len(def.Spec.Guards) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	for i := range out.Guards {
		g := &out.Guards[i]
		at := slices.IndexFunc(def.Spec.Guards, func(s core.GuardSpec) bool { return s.ID == g.ID })
		if at < 0 {
			return fmt.Errorf("lifecycle: %s reported guard %s, which it does not declare", def.Ref(), g.ID)
		}
		g.Overridable = def.Spec.Guards[at].Overridable
		if !g.Overridden {
			continue
		}
		switch {
		case !g.Overridable:
			return fmt.Errorf("lifecycle: %s reported guard %s overridden, which is not overridable", def.Ref(), g.ID)
		case !slices.Contains(overrides, g.ID):
			return fmt.Errorf("lifecycle: %s reported guard %s overridden, which the input does not override", def.Ref(), g.ID)
		case !g.OK:
			return fmt.Errorf("lifecycle: %s reported guard %s overridden and failing", def.Ref(), g.ID)
		}
		out.Diff = append(out.Diff, core.DiffLine{Op: " ", Text: "guard " + g.ID + " overridden: " + g.Message})
	}
	return nil
}
```

```go
// recheck is apply's step 1: the handler plans again from the stored input,
// its guards are checked against the action's declaration as at plan, and

func (e *Engine) recheck(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, def core.ActionDef, pl planRecord, input json.RawMessage) error {
	overrides, err := guardOverrides(def, input)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	var out core.PlanOutcome
	err = e.protect(def.Ref(), "Plan", func() error {
		var err error
		out, err = def.Handler.Plan(ctx, env, input)
		return err
	})
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := checkGuards(def, overrides, &out); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return checkReplan(pl, out)
}
```

```go
package runtime

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"maps"
	"sync"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
)

// The test module "uex" owns the unit darkpanel-uex.service; each of its
// preflight check, resource and action handlers, and the read handler of
// the test core module, probes the unit client it got.

const uexUnit = "darkpanel-uex.service"

var (
	uexRefSet  = core.ActionRef{Name: "uex.unit.set", Version: 1}
	uexRefCore = core.ActionRef{Name: "core.units.get", Version: 1}
)

// uexUnits answers State for every unit; the scoped client decides which
// calls reach it.
type uexUnits struct{ core.Units }

func (uexUnits) State(context.Context, string) (core.UnitState, error) {
	return core.UnitState{LoadState: "loaded", ActiveState: "active"}, nil
}

type uexHost struct {
	mu  sync.Mutex
	saw map[string]string // call → what its unit client allowed
}

// probe records what env's unit client allows: "nil" without one, else
// whether State of the module's own unit and of nginx.service passed.
func (h *uexHost) probe(ctx context.Context, call string, env core.Env) {
	got := "nil"
	if env.Units != nil {
		_, own := env.Units.State(ctx, uexUnit)
		_, other := env.Units.State(ctx, "nginx.service")
		got = fmt.Sprintf("own=%v other=%v", own == nil, other == nil)
	}
	h.mu.Lock()
	defer h.mu.Unlock()
	h.saw[call] = got
}

func (h *uexHost) seen() map[string]string {
	h.mu.Lock()
	defer h.mu.Unlock()
	return maps.Clone(h.saw)
}

type uexIn struct {
	Name string `json:"name"`
}

type uexSet struct{ h *uexHost }

func (x uexSet) Plan(context.Context, core.Env, uexIn) (core.PlanOutcome, error) {
	return core.PlanOutcome{StateHash: "uex"}, nil
}

func (x uexSet) Apply(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in uexIn) (uexIn, error) {
	x.h.probe(ctx, "apply", env)
	return in, nil
}

func (x uexSet) Verify(context.Context, core.Env, uexIn, uexIn) error { return nil }

type uexCoreGet struct{ h *uexHost }

func (x uexCoreGet) Read(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in uexIn) (uexIn, error) {
	x.h.probe(ctx, "core read", env)
	return in, nil
}

type uexModule struct{ h *uexHost }

func (m uexModule) Manifest() core.Manifest {
	return core.Manifest{
		ID: "uex", Version: 1, DefaultEnabled: true,
		OwnedPaths: []core.OwnedPath{{Path: "/etc/systemd/system/" + uexUnit, Kind: core.OwnedUnit}},
		Actions: []core.ActionDef{core.DefineMutating(core.ActionSpec{
			Name: uexRefSet.Name, Version: 1, Class: core.ClassCompensable, Side: core.SideAgent,
			LockKeys: []string{"uex"}, ForwardOnly: true, Converges: true,
		}, uexSet(m))},
		Resources: []core.ResourceDef{core.DefineResource("uex.status", func(ctx context.Context, env core.Env) (uexIn, error) {
			m.h.probe(ctx, "resource", env)
			return uexIn{}, nil
		})},
		Preflight: []core.PreflightCheck{{ID: "probe", Run: func(ctx context.Context, env core.Env) error {
			m.h.probe(ctx, "preflight", env)
			return nil
		}}},
	}
}

// uexCoreModule is a core module with one read action.
type uexCoreModule struct{ h *uexHost }

func (m uexCoreModule) Manifest() core.Manifest {
	return core.Manifest{ID: core.ModuleIDCore, Version: 1, Actions: []core.ActionDef{
		core.DefineRead(core.ActionSpec{Name: uexRefCore.Name, Version: 1, Side: core.SideAgent}, uexCoreGet(m)),
	}}
}

// uexRun opens a runtime over the uex modules with units as Config.Units,
// reads the uex resource, applies uex.unit.set and reads core.units.get,
// and returns what each handler's unit client allowed.
func uexRun(t *testing.T, units core.Units) map[string]string {
	t.Helper()
	h := &uexHost{saw: map[string]string{}}
	f := newFixtureWith(t, uexModule{h}, uexCoreModule{h})
	f.units = units
	f.restart()
	ctx := context.Background()
	if _, err := f.rt.Resource(ctx, alice, "uex.status"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	pl, err := f.rt.Plan(ctx, alice, uexRefSet, json.RawMessage(`{"name":"a"}`), core.PlanOptions{})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if v, err := f.rt.Apply(ctx, alice, pl.PlanID, core.ApplyOptions{}); err != nil || v.State != core.StateCompleted {
		t.Fatalf("Apply = %+v, %v; want completed", v, err)
	}
	if _, err := f.rt.Read(ctx, alice, uexRefCore, json.RawMessage(`{"name":"a"}`)); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return h.seen()
}

func TestRuntimeScopesModuleUnits(t *testing.T) {

	if got := uexRun(t, nil); !maps.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("unit clients allowed %v, want %v", got, want)
```

```ts
// EvtSource stands in for EventSource, which jsdom lacks: it records every
// stream opened and lets a test dispatch named events on it.
export class EvtSource extends EventTarget {
  static instances: EvtSource[] = []
  readonly url: string
  closed = false

  constructor(url: string | URL) {
    super()
    this.url = String(url)
    EvtSource.instances.push(this)
  }

  close(): void {
    this.closed = true
  }

  // emit dispatches one server-sent event of type with data as its JSON.
  emit(type: string, data: unknown): void {
    this.dispatchEvent(new MessageEvent(type, { data: typeof data === "string" ? data : JSON.stringify(data) }))
  }
}
```

```ts
import { QueryClient, type QueryKey } from "@tanstack/react-query"
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest"
import { EvtSource } from "@/test/evt-source"
import { connectEvents } from "./events"

const cached: QueryKey[] = [
  ["hosts"],
  ["audit"],
  ["changes"],
  ["changes", { hostId: "h1" }],
  ["change", "c1"],
  ["change", "c2"],
  ["steps", "c1"],
  ["resource", "h1", "hostinfo.summary"],
  ["resource", "h2", "hostinfo.summary"],
  ["tokens"],
]

// evtConnect connects a client whose cache holds every key of cached, and
// returns it with the fake stream it opened.
function evtConnect() {
  const client = new QueryClient()
  for (const key of cached) client.setQueryData(key, {})
  let source: EvtSource | undefined
  const close = connectEvents(client, (url) => {
    source = new EvtSource(url)
    return source as unknown as EventSource
  })
  if (source === undefined) throw new Error("connectEvents opened no stream")
  return { client, source, close }
}

// evtInvalidated lists the cached keys whose queries are invalidated.
function evtInvalidated(client: QueryClient): QueryKey[] {
  return cached.filter((key) => client.getQueryState(key)?.isInvalidated === true)
}

describe("connectEvents", () => {
  test("opens one stream at /api/v1/events and closes it", () => {
    const { source, close } = evtConnect()
    expect(EvtSource.instances).toEqual([source])
    expect(source.url).toBe("/api/v1/events")
    expect(source.closed).toBe(false)
    close()
    expect(source.closed).toBe(true)
  })

  test.each<[string, unknown, QueryKey[]]>([
    [
      "change",
      { hostId: "h1", changeId: "c1", action: "demo.item.add", state: "completed", updatedAt: "2026-10-22T12:00:00Z" },
      [["audit"], ["changes"], ["changes", { hostId: "h1" }], ["change", "c1"]],
    ],
    ["composite.step", { changeId: "c1", stepId: "s1", state: "confirmed", childChangeId: "k1" }, [["change", "c1"], ["steps", "c1"]]],
    ["host", { hostId: "h1", online: false }, [["hosts"]]],
    [
      "module",
      { hostId: "h1", moduleId: "hostinfo", enabled: false, available: true },
      [["hosts"], ["resource", "h1", "hostinfo.summary"]],
    ],
    ["reset", {}, cached],
  ])("a %s event invalidates the queries it names", (type, data, want) => {
    const { client, source } = evtConnect()
    source.emit(type, data)
    expect(evtInvalidated(client)).toEqual(cached.filter((key) => want.some((w) => JSON.stringify(w) === JSON.stringify(key))))
  })

  test("ignores an event whose data is not JSON", () => {
    const { client, source } = evtConnect()
    source.emit("change", "{not json")
    expect(evtInvalidated(client)).toEqual([])
  })

  test("uses the browser's EventSource without a factory", () => {
    const close = connectEvents(new QueryClient())
    expect(EvtSource.instances.map((s) => s.url)).toEqual(["/api/v1/events"])
    close()
    expect(EvtSource.instances[0]?.closed).toBe(true)
  })
})
```

Create `web/src/api/events.ts`:

```ts
import type { QueryClient, QueryKey } from "@tanstack/react-query"
import { HOSTS_QUERY_KEY } from "./client"

export type EventSourceFactory = (url: string) => EventSource

interface ChangeEventData {
  changeId: string
}

interface StepEventData {
  changeId: string
}

interface ModuleEventData {
  hostId: string
}

function parse<T>(event: MessageEvent): T | null {
  if (typeof event.data !== "string") return null
  try {
    return JSON.parse(event.data) as T
  } catch {
    return null
  }
}

// connectEvents keeps the controller's event stream open and refetches the
// queries each event names (spec 1.6). EventSource reconnects on its own with
// the last id it saw, so the controller replays what was missed or sends a
// reset. The returned function closes the stream.
export function connectEvents(client: QueryClient, factory: EventSourceFactory = (url) => new EventSource(url)): () => void {
  const source = factory("/api/v1/events")
  function on<T>(type: string, keys: (data: T) => QueryKey[]) {
    source.addEventListener(type, (event: MessageEvent) => {
      const data = parse<T>(event)
      if (data === null) return
      for (const queryKey of keys(data)) void client.invalidateQueries({ queryKey })
    })
  }
  on<ChangeEventData>("change", (d) => [["changes"], ["change", d.changeId], ["audit"]])
  on<StepEventData>("composite.step", (d) => [["change", d.changeId], ["steps", d.changeId]])
  on<object>("host", () => [HOSTS_QUERY_KEY])
  on<ModuleEventData>("module", (d) => [HOSTS_QUERY_KEY, ["resource", d.hostId]])
  source.addEventListener("reset", () => void client.invalidateQueries())
  return () => source.close()
}
```

Adds `Engine.Reveal` and `Engine.ReadInternal` (C24, ruling R8): validate the input, run `Handler.Reveal` under `Protect` with no `Redact`, then append one journal entry with phase `reveal` and the handler's identity (never the value) in its own committed `DB.Write`, and only then return the value; a failed handler, a refused input or a failed append journals nothing and returns no value. On the agent the entry lands in `core_journal`, which the controller ingests; on the controller `Journal` is the audit store. `Engine.Read` answers `action.unknown` for reveal and internal actions, so neither can leak through the redacting read path. Security risk: it runs alone. The agent, dispatcher and API paths over it are Tasks 62, 71, 75 and 55. Test identifiers carry the prefix `rv`.

```go
	return func(_ context.Context, env core.Env, in rvIn) (core.Revealed[rvOut], error) {
		if in.Fail {
			return core.Revealed[rvOut]{}, errors.New("rv vault is sealed")
		}
		return core.Revealed[rvOut]{Identity: "rv " + kind + ", host " + env.HostID,
			Value: rvOut{Name: in.Name, Password: rvSecret}}, nil
	}
}

type rvRead struct{}

func (rvRead) Read(context.Context, core.Env, rvIn) (rvOut, error) { return rvOut{Name: "plain"}, nil }

type rvModule struct{}

func (rvModule) Manifest() core.Manifest {
	return core.Manifest{ID: "rv", Version: 1, Actions: []core.ActionDef{
		core.DefineReveal(core.ActionSpec{Name: refRvReveal.Name, Version: 1, Side: core.SideAgent, MinScope: core.ScopeAdmin},
			rvReveal("key")),
		core.DefineInternalRead(core.ActionSpec{Name: refRvInternal.Name, Version: 1, Side: core.SideAgent},
			rvReveal("certificate")),
		core.DefineRead(core.ActionSpec{Name: refRvRead.Name, Version: 1, Side: core.SideAgent}, rvRead{}),
	}}
}

// rvJournal returns every journal entry of the fixture.
func (f *fixture) rvJournal() []core.JournalEntry {
	f.t.Helper()
	entries, err := f.journal.Entries(context.Background(), 0, 0)
	if err != nil {
		f.t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return entries
}

// rvFailingJournal refuses every append.
type rvFailingJournal struct{}

func (rvFailingJournal) Append(context.Context, *sql.Tx, core.JournalEntry) error {
	return errors.New("rv journal is full")
}
```

```go
package lifecycle

import (
	"context"
	"database/sql"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
)

// phaseReveal is the journal phase of a reveal and of an internal read.
const phaseReveal = "reveal"

// revealAudit is the journal input of a reveal: what was revealed, never the
// value.
type revealAudit struct {
	Identity string `json:"identity"`
}

// Reveal runs a reveal action (spec 1.14) and returns its value, which no
// Redact touches. The reveal is journaled before the value is returned, so a
// value is never returned unaudited. Any action but a reveal action is
// action.unknown.
func (e *Engine) Reveal(ctx context.Context, p core.Principal, ref core.ActionRef, input json.RawMessage) (json.RawMessage, error) {
	return e.reveal(ctx, p, ref, input, false)
}

// ReadInternal runs an Internal read (spec 1.7) as Reveal runs a reveal
// action. Any action but an Internal read is action.unknown.
func (e *Engine) ReadInternal(ctx context.Context, p core.Principal, ref core.ActionRef, input json.RawMessage) (json.RawMessage, error) {
	return e.reveal(ctx, p, ref, input, true)
}

func (e *Engine) reveal(ctx context.Context, p core.Principal, ref core.ActionRef, input json.RawMessage, internal bool) (json.RawMessage, error) {
	def, err := e.action(ref)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	served := def.Spec.Reveal
	if internal {
		served = def.Spec.Internal
	}
	if !served || def.Handler.Reveal == nil {
		return nil, errcode.New(errcode.ActionUnknown, fmt.Sprintf("unknown action %s", ref))
	}
	if err := e.cfg.Validator.ValidateInput(def, input); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	var identity string
	var value json.RawMessage
	err = e.protect(ref, "Reveal", func() error {
		var err error
		identity, value, err = def.Handler.Reveal(ctx, e.env(p, def), input)
		return err
	})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	audit, err := json.Marshal(revealAudit{Identity: identity})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("lifecycle: encode the audit of %s: %w", ref, err)
	}
	err = e.cfg.Base.DB.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
		return e.cfg.Journal.Append(ctx, tx, core.JournalEntry{
			At: e.cfg.Base.Clock.Now(), Actor: p.Actor, Action: ref.Name, Version: ref.Version, Phase: phaseReveal,
			Input: audit, Result: resultOK, Source: p.Source,
		})
	})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("lifecycle: journal the reveal of %s: %w", ref, err)
	}
	return value, nil
}
```

```go
// kindsModule declares a managed directory outside the data directory and one
// inside it, a service directory with the subdirectory certs, a unit, a
// restore file and a kernel parameter.
type kindsModule struct{ l Layout }

func (m kindsModule) paths() (outside, inside, svc, unit, restore string) {
	etc := filepath.Dir(m.l.ConfigDir)
	return filepath.Join(etc, "kinds-debs"), filepath.Join(m.l.DataDir, "kinds-tokens"), filepath.Join(etc, "kinds-svc"),
		m.l.UnitPath("darkpanel-kinds.service"), filepath.Join(etc, "kinds.rules")
}

func (m kindsModule) Manifest() core.Manifest {
	outside, inside, svc, unit, restore := m.paths()
	return core.Manifest{ID: "kinds", Version: 1, OwnedPaths: []core.OwnedPath{
		{Path: outside, Kind: core.OwnedManagedDir},
		{Path: inside, Kind: core.OwnedManagedDir},
		{Path: svc, Kind: core.OwnedServiceDir, User: "kinds", Subdirs: []string{"certs"}},
		{Path: unit, Kind: core.OwnedUnit},
		{Path: restore, Kind: core.OwnedRestore},
		{Path: "net/ipv4/ip_forward", Kind: core.OwnedSysctl, Pattern: `^[01]$`},
	}}
}

// kindsInstall lets kindsModule write its paths on h, as its actions would:
// two files in each managed directory, the service directory with a
// certificate, the unit file and the restore file.
func kindsInstall(t *testing.T, h *testHost) kindsModule {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	m := kindsModule{l: h.layout}
	outside, inside, svc, unit, restore := m.paths()
	db, err := store.Open(ctx, h.layout.Paths.AgentDB())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer func() { _ = db.Close() }()
	uid, gid := os.Geteuid(), os.Getegid()
	files := platform.NewFiles(platform.FilesConfig{
		Owned: platform.OwnedPaths([]core.Manifest{m.Manifest()}), Ownership: platform.NewOwnership(db), Clock: h.clock,
		TestMode: true, LookupUser: func(string) (int, int, error) { return uid, gid, nil },
	})
	for _, dir := range []string{outside, inside} {
		for _, name := range []string{"a.token", "b.token"} {
			if err := files.WriteManaged(ctx, "kinds", dir, name, []byte(name), 0o600, uid, gid); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
		}
	}
	if err := files.EnsureServiceDir(ctx, "kinds", svc); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(svc, "certs", "a.crt"), []byte("cert"), 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := files.WriteFile(ctx, "kinds", unit, []byte("[Unit]\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(restore, []byte("rules\n"), 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return m
}

// kindsConfig is h's uninstall with the demo module and kindsModule.
func kindsConfig(h *testHost, m *demoModule, km kindsModule, keepData bool) UninstallConfig {
	cfg := h.uninstallConfig(m, keepData)
	cfg.Modules = append(cfg.Modules, km)
	return cfg
}

func TestUninstallRemovesManagedDirs(t *testing.T) {
	h, m := installHost(t, RoleController)
	km := kindsInstall(t, h)
	outside, inside, _, _, _ := km.paths()
	u, err := PlanUninstall(context.Background(), kindsConfig(h, m, km, false))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var plan bytes.Buffer
	u.Describe(&plan)
	_ = u.Close()
	for _, dir := range []string{outside, inside} {
		if want := "managed-dir " + dir + ", of module kinds"; !strings.Contains(plan.String(), want) {
			t.Errorf("plan lacks %q:\n%s", want, plan.String())
		}
	}
	if out, err := runUninstall(t, kindsConfig(h, m, km, false)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Run: %v\n%s", err, out)
	}
	for _, dir := range []string{outside, inside} {
		if exists(t, dir) {
			t.Errorf("%s is left", dir)
		}
	}

	h, m = installHost(t, RoleController)
	km = kindsInstall(t, h)
	outside, inside, _, _, _ = km.paths()
	if out, err := runUninstall(t, kindsConfig(h, m, km, true)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Run with --keep-data: %v\n%s", err, out)
	}
	if exists(t, outside) {
		t.Errorf("--keep-data kept %s, which is outside the data directory", outside)
	}
	for _, name := range []string{"a.token", "b.token"} {
		if !exists(t, filepath.Join(inside, name)) {
			t.Errorf("--keep-data removed %s from %s", name, inside)
		}
	}
	got := manifest(t, h.layout)
	if !slices.Contains(got, "managed-dir "+inside+" (module kinds)") || slices.Contains(got, "managed-dir "+outside+" (module kinds)") {
		t.Errorf("manifest %v: want the kept directory recorded and the removed one forgotten", got)
	}
}
```

```go
// removeManagedDir removes a managed directory with everything in it. A
// symlink in any component of the path is refused, never followed (ADR 0009);
// removeTree then removes a symlink inside the directory itself.
func removeManagedDir(path string) error {
	fd, err := unix.Openat2(unix.AT_FDCWD, path, &unix.OpenHow{
		Flags:   unix.O_PATH | unix.O_CLOEXEC,
		Resolve: unix.RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS,
	})
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, unix.ENOENT):
		return nil
	case err != nil:
		return fmt.Errorf("install: open managed directory %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	_ = unix.Close(fd)
	return removeTree(path)
}

// removeUnits stops and disables the modules' units, removes the unit files,
// then their drop-in directories when nothing else is left in them, and
// reloads systemd. The core's units were stopped and disabled by the services
// step, and their files go as before.
func (u *Uninstall) removeUnits(ctx context.Context, units, dirs []core.OwnedEntry) (string, error) {
	for _, e := range units {
		if e.Module == core.ModuleIDCore {
			continue
		}
		if err := u.stopUnit(ctx, filepath.Base(e.Path)); err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
	}
	for _, e := range units {
		if e.Module != core.ModuleIDCore && u.files != nil {
			if err := u.files.Remove(ctx, e.Module, e.Path); err != nil {
				return "", err
			}
			continue
		}
		if err := os.Remove(e.Path); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
			return "", err
		}
		if err := u.forget(ctx, e); err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
	}
```

```go
// stopUnit stops a module's unit, waits until it is down and disables it; a
// unit systemd does not know is left to the file removal.
func (u *Uninstall) stopUnit(ctx context.Context, unit string) error {
	st, err := u.cfg.Systemd.State(ctx, unit)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if st.LoadState == "not-found" {
		return nil
	}
	if err := u.cfg.Systemd.Stop(ctx, unit); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := u.waitStopped(ctx, unit); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return u.cfg.Systemd.Disable(ctx, unit)
}
```

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-sonnet-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 2 - risk 2 = 5

Adds `guardRefresh` to the `Darkpanel-Call` object (`wire.CallContext`, omitted when nil) and hands an apply's guard refresh to the handler calls of that apply only: the re-plan in `begin`, `Snapshot`, `Apply` and `Verify` see it in `Env.Call.GuardRefresh` (seam S5). It is never stored: `core_plans.call` keeps `storedCall`, which has no such field, the intent carries it in memory, and a revert, an undo, recovery and task-unit processes read the stored call and see nil. `Engine.Plan` drops a guard refresh a plan's call carries, since the refresh is apply-only (spec 1.5). An apply whose call names another parent or step than its plan's stays `plan.state_changed`. The task-unit path (`Spec.Task`) runs Apply in another process from stored rows, so it gets no refresh; no guarded action is a task action in v1. The dispatcher sending the refresh is Task 58.

```go
var gfxRefresh = &core.GuardContext{AgentPeers: []netip.Addr{netip.MustParseAddr("192.0.2.30")}}

func TestApplyHandsGuardRefresh(t *testing.T) {
	f, h := newGfx(t)
	ctx := context.Background()
	pl := f.plan(alice, refGfxSet, `{"name":"a"}`)
	v, err := f.eng.Apply(ctx, alice, pl.PlanID, core.ApplyOptions{Call: &core.CallContext{GuardRefresh: gfxRefresh}})
	if err != nil || v.State != core.StatePending {
		t.Fatalf("Apply = %s, %v; want pending", v.State, err)
	}
	if n := f.count("SELECT count(*) FROM core_plans WHERE id = ? AND call IS NULL", pl.PlanID); n != 1 {
		t.Error("the apply's guard refresh was stored with the plan")
	}
	if _, err := f.eng.Revert(ctx, alice, v.ID); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// A plan is never given a guard refresh, even when its call carries one.
	if _, err := f.eng.Plan(ctx, alice, refGfxSet, json.RawMessage(`{"name":"b"}`),
		core.PlanOptions{Call: &core.CallContext{GuardRefresh: gfxRefresh}}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var got []string
	for _, c := range h.seen() {
		got = append(got, fmt.Sprintf("%s refreshed=%v", c.Method, c.Call.GuardRefresh == gfxRefresh))
	}
	// The plan; the apply's re-plan, snapshot, apply and verify; the revert;
	// the second plan.
	want := []string{
		"Plan refreshed=false",
		"Plan refreshed=true", "Snapshot refreshed=true", "Apply refreshed=true", "Verify refreshed=true",
		"Revert refreshed=false",
		"Plan refreshed=false",
	}
	if !slices.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("handler calls\n got %q\nwant %q", got, want)
	}
}
```

```go
// CallContext is core.CallContext without RepairOf, which the agent derives
// from a repair plan and never receives (spec 1.5). The agent decodes it
// with unknown members refused, so a repairOf member is
// request.invalid_input.
type CallContext struct {
	ParentChangeID string   `json:"parentChangeId"`
	ParentAction   string   `json:"parentAction"`
	StepID         string   `json:"stepId"`
	Retired        []string `json:"retired"`
}

// FromCall converts c, leaving out RepairOf.
func FromCall(c core.CallContext) CallContext {
	return CallContext{ParentChangeID: c.ParentChangeID, ParentAction: c.ParentAction, StepID: c.StepID,
		Retired: slices.Clone(c.Retired)}
}

// Core converts c back; RepairOf stays empty.
func (c CallContext) Core() core.CallContext {
	return core.CallContext{ParentChangeID: c.ParentChangeID, ParentAction: c.ParentAction, StepID: c.StepID,
		Retired: slices.Clone(c.Retired)}
}
```

with:

```go
// CallContext is core.CallContext without RepairOf, which the agent derives
// from a repair plan and never receives (spec 1.5). The agent decodes it
// with unknown members refused, so a repairOf member is
// request.invalid_input. GuardRefresh is sent with an apply only.
type CallContext struct {
	ParentChangeID string             `json:"parentChangeId"`
	ParentAction   string             `json:"parentAction"`
	StepID         string             `json:"stepId"`
	Retired        []string           `json:"retired"`
	GuardRefresh   *core.GuardContext `json:"guardRefresh,omitempty"`
}

// FromCall converts c, leaving out RepairOf.
func FromCall(c core.CallContext) CallContext {
	return CallContext{ParentChangeID: c.ParentChangeID, ParentAction: c.ParentAction, StepID: c.StepID,
		Retired: slices.Clone(c.Retired), GuardRefresh: c.GuardRefresh}
}

// Core converts c back; RepairOf stays empty.
func (c CallContext) Core() core.CallContext {
	return core.CallContext{ParentChangeID: c.ParentChangeID, ParentAction: c.ParentAction, StepID: c.StepID,
		Retired: slices.Clone(c.Retired), GuardRefresh: c.GuardRefresh}
}
```

```go
package runtime

import (
	"context"
	"database/sql"
	"errors"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
)

// MetaModuleEnabledPrefix starts the core_meta key of a module's enabled flag
// (spec 1.4): module_enabled.<id> holds "1" or "0" as the controller last
// pushed it. The controller's core_module_state stays the authority; only the
// background tasks read this copy.
const MetaModuleEnabledPrefix = "module_enabled."

var _ core.AgentEnablement = (*Runtime)(nil)

// SetModuleEnabled stores moduleID's enabled flag as the controller pushed
// it. A module the registry lacks is not_found.
func (r *Runtime) SetModuleEnabled(ctx context.Context, moduleID string, enabled bool) error {
	if _, ok := r.cfg.Registry.Module(moduleID); !ok {
		return errcode.New(errcode.NotFound, fmt.Sprintf("no module %s", moduleID))
	}
	value := "0"
	if enabled {
		value = "1"
	}
	err := r.cfg.DB.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
		_, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `INSERT INTO core_meta (key, value) VALUES (?, ?)
			ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value`, MetaModuleEnabledPrefix+moduleID, value)
		return err
	})
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("runtime: store the enabled flag of %s: %w", moduleID, err)
	}
	return nil
}

// moduleEnabled reads moduleID's enabled flag; without one the module's
// DefaultEnabled holds, as it does on the controller before an operator
// enables or disables the module.
func (r *Runtime) moduleEnabled(ctx context.Context, moduleID string) (bool, error) {
	m, ok := r.cfg.Registry.Module(moduleID)
	if !ok {
		return false, errcode.New(errcode.NotFound, fmt.Sprintf("no module %s", moduleID))
	}
	var value string
	err := r.cfg.DB.Read().QueryRowContext(ctx, "SELECT value FROM core_meta WHERE key = ?",
		MetaModuleEnabledPrefix+moduleID).Scan(&value)
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
		return m.DefaultEnabled, nil
	case err != nil:
		return false, fmt.Errorf("runtime: read the enabled flag of %s: %w", moduleID, err)
	}
	return value == "1", nil
}
```

Create `internal/agent/runtime/availability.go`:

```go
package runtime

import (
	"context"
	"strings"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
)

var _ core.AgentAvailability = (*Runtime)(nil)

// Availability runs moduleID's preflight checks again, as Preflight does, and
// answers which of the module's agent-side actions are available (spec 1.7).
// When the preflight fails, the module and every action are unavailable with
// its reason; otherwise each action name is asked through the engine's
// Available at its highest version. An unknown module is not_found.
func (r *Runtime) Availability(ctx context.Context, moduleID string) (core.ModuleAvailability, error) {
	st, err := r.Preflight(ctx, moduleID)
	if err != nil {
		return core.ModuleAvailability{}, err
	}
	out := core.ModuleAvailability{Module: moduleID, Available: st.Available, Reason: st.Reason,
		Actions: []core.ActionAvailability{}}
	for _, def := range r.latestActions(moduleID) {
		a := core.ActionAvailability{Name: def.Spec.Name, Available: st.Available, Reason: st.Reason}
		if st.Available {
			if err := r.engine.Available(ctx, def.Ref()); err != nil {
				a.Available, a.Reason = false, err.Error()
			}
		}
		out.Actions = append(out.Actions, a)
	}
	return out, nil
}

// latestActions returns the highest version of every agent-side action of
// moduleID, sorted by name.
func (r *Runtime) latestActions(moduleID string) []core.ActionDef {
	var out []core.ActionDef
	for _, def := range r.cfg.Registry.Actions() {
		if def.Spec.Side != core.SideAgent || !strings.HasPrefix(def.Spec.Name, moduleID+".") {
			continue
		}
		// Actions sorts by name, then version, so a later entry of the
		// same name is a higher version.
		if n := len(out); n > 0 && out[n-1].Spec.Name == def.Spec.Name {
			out[n-1] = def
			continue
		}
		out = append(out, def)
	}
	return out
}
```

```go
// StreamInfo is one stream an agent serves, as GET /agent/v1/streams lists it.
type StreamInfo struct {
	Module     string `json:"module"`
	Name       string `json:"name"`
	SchemaHash string `json:"schemaHash"`
}

// DefineStream builds a StreamDef from typed parameters and events. Run
// decodes the parameters like an action input, refusing unknown members.
func DefineStream[P, E any](name string, run func(ctx context.Context, env Env, p P, emit func(E) error) error) StreamDef {
	return StreamDef{
		Name: name, ParamsType: typeOf[P](), EventType: typeOf[E](),
		Run: func(ctx context.Context, env Env, params json.RawMessage, emit func(event any) error) error {
			p, err := decode[P](params)
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			return run(ctx, env, p, func(e E) error { return emit(e) })
		},
	}
}
```

```go
// addStreams checks and indexes module's streams.
func (r *Registry) addStreams(module string, defs []StreamDef) []error {
	var errs []error
	for _, d := range defs {
		key := module + "." + d.Name
		switch {
		case !streamNamePattern.MatchString(d.Name):
			errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("module %s: stream %q must match %s", module, d.Name, streamNamePattern))
		case d.Run == nil || d.ParamsType == nil || d.EventType == nil:
			errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("stream %s needs Run, ParamsType and EventType", key))
		case r.streams[key].Module != "":
			errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("stream %s registered twice", key))
		default:
			r.streams[key] = ModuleStream{Module: module, Def: d}
		}
	}
	return errs
}

// checkCLINames refuses names whose CLI commands (spec section 15) would
// clash: an action <m>.<noun>.<verb> is `<m> <noun> <verb>`, a resource
// <m>.<r> is `<m> <r> get`, and the core drops its module segment, so a core
// noun or resource must not be a module id. A stream <m>.<n> is the command
// `<m> <n> --follow`, which can be neither another command nor the group of
// one.
```

```go
// Stream returns one stream of module.
func (r *Registry) Stream(module, name string) (StreamDef, bool) {
	st, ok := r.streams[module+"."+name]
	return st.Def, ok
}

// Streams returns every stream, sorted by module and then name.
func (r *Registry) Streams() []ModuleStream {
	out := make([]ModuleStream, 0, len(r.streams))
	for _, st := range r.streams {
		out = append(out, st)
	}
	sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
		if out[i].Module != out[j].Module {
			return out[i].Module < out[j].Module
		}
		return out[i].Def.Name < out[j].Def.Name
	})
	return out
}

// Modules returns the manifests in registration order.
```

```go
// StreamHash is the lower-case hex SHA-256 of {"params": <input schema of
// ParamsType>, "event": <output schema of EventType>} re-encoded by
// encoding/json. The controller relays a stream only when the agent reports
// the hash of its own registry's definition.
func StreamHash(def core.StreamDef) (string, error) {
	params, err := schema.Input(def.ParamsType)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("schemas: stream %s params: %w", def.Name, err)
	}
	event, err := schema.Output(def.EventType)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("schemas: stream %s event: %w", def.Name, err)
	}
	doc, err := json.Marshal(map[string]json.RawMessage{"params": params, "event": event})
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("schemas: stream %s: %w", def.Name, err)
	}
	return Hash(doc)
}
```

```go
// pubWant reads ch until an event of eventType arrives, within five
// seconds, and checks that its data marshals like want.
func pubWant(t *testing.T, ch <-chan events.Event, eventType string, want any) {
	t.Helper()
	b, err := json.Marshal(want)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	deadline := time.After(5 * time.Second)
	for {
		select {
		case ev := <-ch:
			if ev.Type != eventType {
				continue
			}
			if string(ev.Data) != string(b) {
				t.Fatalf("%s event = %s, want %s", eventType, ev.Data, b)
			}
			return
		case <-deadline:
			t.Fatalf("no %s event", eventType)
		}
	}
}

// TestServerEventWiring shows the event bus fed by the controller engine's

func TestServerEventWiring(t *testing.T) {

	s.engineConfig(s.registry).Publish(lifecycle.EventCompositeStep, step)
	pubWant(t, ch, events.TypeCompositeStep, step)

	plan := planDisable(t, s)
	const id = "01WIRED000000000000000000X"
	if _, err := s.controllerDB.Writer().ExecContext(ctx,
		`INSERT INTO core_changes (id, plan_id, host_id, action, version, class, compensated_by, actor, state,
		 input_json, created_at, updated_at)
		 VALUES (?, ?, '', 'core.module.disable', 1, 'compensable', 'core.module.enable', 'local:root@h', 'completed', '{}', ?, ?)`,
		id, plan.PlanID, clock.Now().Format(timeFormat), clock.Now().Format(timeFormat)); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := s.controllerDB.Writer().ExecContext(ctx,
		"UPDATE core_module_state SET enabled = 0 WHERE host_id = ? AND module_id = 'hostinfo'", s.LocalHostID()); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	clock.Advance(events.PollInterval)
	pubWant(t, ch, events.TypeChange, events.ChangeEvent{ChangeID: id, Action: "core.module.disable", State: core.StateCompleted,
```

```go
// hostOnline publishes the session registry's online changes as host
// events.
func hostOnline(bus *events.Bus) func(hostID string, online bool) {
	return func(hostID string, online bool) {
		bus.Publish(events.TypeHost, events.HostEvent{HostID: hostID, Online: online})
	}
}

// engineConfig is the controller engine's configuration. Its Publish hands
// the composite.step events to the event bus.
func (s *Server) engineConfig(reg *core.Registry) lifecycle.Config {
	return lifecycle.Config{
		Side: core.SideController, Registry: reg, Validator: schema.NewValidator(), Journal: s.auditLog,
		Redact: schema.Redact, Publish: s.events.Publish,
		Base: core.Env{
			DB: s.controllerDB, Sealer: s.controllerSealer, Clock: s.clock, Log: s.log, Agents: s.hosts,
		},
	}
}

// ingestedEntries is the audit ingester's OnEntries: it wakes the
// composites following the stored entries' changes and publishes those
// changes, read through change, as change events.
func (s *Server) ingestedEntries(wake func(changeIDs ...string),
	change func(ctx context.Context, hostID, changeID string) (core.ChangeView, error)) func(hostID string, entries []core.JournalEntry) {
	wakeFn, publish := wakeComposites(wake), events.AgentChanges(s.events, change, s.log)
	return func(hostID string, entries []core.JournalEntry) {
		wakeFn(hostID, entries)
		publish(hostID, entries)
	}
}

// agentChange reads changeID from hostID's agent.
func (s *Server) agentChange(ctx context.Context, hostID, changeID string) (core.ChangeView, error) {
	agent, err := s.hosts.Agent(ctx, hostID)
	if err != nil {
		return core.ChangeView{}, err
	}
	return agent.Change(ctx, changeID)
}
```

```go
// wakeComposites wakes the composites following the changes of the stored
// entries in wakePhases, each change once: Wake runs a query per id under
// the ingestion lock.
func wakeComposites(wake func(changeIDs ...string)) func(hostID string, entries []core.JournalEntry) {
	return func(_ string, entries []core.JournalEntry) {
		var ids []string
		seen := map[string]bool{}
		for _, e := range entries {
			if wakePhases[e.Phase] && e.ChangeID != "" && !seen[e.ChangeID] {
				seen[e.ChangeID] = true
				ids = append(ids, e.ChangeID)
			}
		}
```

The mutating command of every action with `Guards` gains a repeatable `--override <guard id>` whose usage lists the overridable guards; the ids go into the plan input's `overrides`, on the API and with `--local` alike, and the engine validates them (Task 41). A guarded input type's `guard` and `overrides` get no generated flag (`guard` is the controller's, `overrides` comes from `--override`), and `override` joins the reserved flags so no input field can take it. When a plan reports a failing guard that is overridable, the CLI prints `override it with --override <id>` before refusing; it applies nothing in either case. `--yes` and `--confirm` keep their meaning (spec 1.13). Test helpers carry the prefix `cov`: `covInput`, `covModule` (registered in `testRegistry`) and `covPlan`.

```go
// embedsGuarded reports whether the struct type t embeds core.Guarded.
func embedsGuarded(t reflect.Type) bool {
	if t.Kind() != reflect.Struct {
		return false
	}
	for i := range t.NumField() {
		if f := t.Field(i); f.Anonymous && f.Type == reflect.TypeFor[core.Guarded]() {

		}
	}
	return false
```

```go
// addMutatingFlags adds --yes, --confirmation for an irreversible action or
// --confirm for a revertible one, and --override for an action with Guards.
func addMutatingFlags(cmd *cobra.Command, spec core.ActionSpec) {
	cmd.Flags().Bool("yes", false, "apply without asking Apply? [y/N]; an irreversible action still needs its confirmation phrase")
	switch spec.Class {
	case core.ClassIrreversible:
		cmd.Flags().String("confirmation", "", "the confirmation phrase the plan names, instead of typing it")
	case core.ClassRevertible:
		cmd.Flags().Bool("confirm", false, "confirm the change at once instead of leaving it pending until its revert deadline")
	}
	if len(spec.Guards) == 0 {
		return
	}
	var ids []string
	for _, g := range spec.Guards {
		if g.Overridable {
			ids = append(ids, g.ID)
		}
	}
	usage := "plan again with this failing guard overridden (repeatable)"
	if len(ids) > 0 {
		usage += "; overridable: " + strings.Join(ids, ", ")
	}
	cmd.Flags().StringArray("override", nil, usage)
}

// withOverrides sets the input's overrides to the --override ids when the
// flag was given.
func withOverrides(cmd *cobra.Command, input json.RawMessage) (json.RawMessage, error) {
	if !cmd.Flags().Changed("override") {
		return input, nil
	}
	ids, err := cmd.Flags().GetStringArray("override")
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	var obj map[string]json.RawMessage
	if err := json.Unmarshal(input, &obj); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cli: read the input: %w", err)
	}
	if obj["overrides"], err = json.Marshal(ids); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return json.Marshal(obj)
}
```

```go
package api

import (
	"net/http"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/agent/wire"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
)

// handleAvailability answers which actions of a module are available on a
// host, from the dispatcher's cached answer (spec 1.7), so the UI can grey
// out the others. Internal actions are left out: no public route names them.
func (s *Server) handleAvailability(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	c, _ := callerFrom(r.Context())
	err := authorize(c.principal, core.ScopeRead)
	if err == nil && s.cfg.Availability == nil {
		err = errcode.New(errcode.NotFound, "module availability is not served by this controller")
	}
	var m core.ModuleAvailability
	if err == nil {
		m, err = s.cfg.Availability(r.Context(), r.PathValue("host"), r.PathValue("module"))
	}
	if err != nil {
		writeProblem(w, s.log, err)
		return
	}
	actions := make([]core.ActionAvailability, 0, len(m.Actions))
	for _, a := range m.Actions {
		if !s.internal(a.Name) {
			actions = append(actions, a)
		}
	}
	m.Actions = actions
	writeJSON(w, s.log, http.StatusOK, wire.FromModuleAvailability(m))
}

// internal reports whether any version of the action name is Internal.
func (s *Server) internal(name string) bool {
	for _, def := range s.cfg.Registry.Actions() {
		if def.Spec.Name == name && def.Spec.Internal {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}
```

- Produces: C33 (`MaxStreamEvent`, `Runtime.Streams`, `Runtime.OpenStream`, the JSON-lines body, `Runtime.Close` ending open streams).

**Items:** 47

**Depends on:** Task 43, Task 51, Task 34

**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 2 - risk 3 = 6

The second half of the brief's Task 56. `Runtime.Streams` lists every registered stream with its schema hash. `Runtime.OpenStream` checks the stream, the module (`usable`, as `Read` does) and the parameters, then runs the stream's `Run` on its own goroutine under `Protect`, with `moduleEnv` and the caller as principal. The lines go through `streamPipe`, which hands the reader one C33 line per `Read` when the reader's buffer is large enough, so the route (Task 80) flushes whole lines. Unlike `io.Pipe`, a waiting `emit` gives up when its context ends, so nothing waits on a reader that stopped reading. An event over `MaxStreamEvent` fails `emit` with `request.too_large` and ends the stream with `error`; every later `emit` returns the same error. A 5xx end error carries only the code's title, as the agent API's problem details do, and an internal one is logged. Closing the reader, or the end of `ctx`, cancels `Run`'s context, and no end line is written then.

Every stream's `Run` context also ends with the runtime's `streamSet`. `Runtime.Close` calls `streamSet.close` first: it cancels every open stream, waits until each `Run` returned, and refuses later opens with `unavailable`. A stream that is still read then ends with the error `unavailable`. So closing or replacing the runtime ends open streams promptly (the daemon half, Task 81, keeps the daemon's lock from waiting for them). The validator for parameters is one per process (`streamParams`), so each parameter type compiles once. Test modules carry the prefix `sm`; the helpers `smFixture` and `smOpen` are this file's only.

```go
package runtime

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"log/slog"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"sync"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/lifecycle"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/schema"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/schemas"
)

// MaxStreamEvent is the largest encoded event a module stream may emit (spec
// 1.6).
const MaxStreamEvent = 64 << 10

var _ core.AgentStreams = (*Runtime)(nil)

// streamParams validates stream parameters; it compiles each parameter type
// once for the process.
var streamParams = schema.NewValidator()

// errStreamClosed is the error end of a stream whose runtime closed under
// it: the controller may open it again on the runtime that replaces this one.
var errStreamClosed = errcode.New(errcode.Unavailable, "the agent runtime closed; open the stream again")

// Streams lists every registered module stream with its schema hash.
func (r *Runtime) Streams(context.Context) ([]core.StreamInfo, error) {
	out := []core.StreamInfo{}
	for _, s := range r.cfg.Registry.Streams() {
		hash, err := schemas.StreamHash(s.Def)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("runtime: stream %s.%s: %w", s.Module, s.Def.Name, err)
		}
		out = append(out, core.StreamInfo{Module: s.Module, Name: s.Def.Name, SchemaHash: hash})
	}
	return out, nil
}

// OpenStream starts module's stream name with the parameters in params and
// returns its body: one {"data": <event>} line per event, then one
// {"end": ...} line. Run's context ends when ctx ends, when the reader is
// closed, or when Close closes the runtime; the stream then ends with the
// error unavailable. A stream the registry lacks is not_found, a module
// whose migrations failed is module.unavailable, parameters the stream's
// schema refuses are request.invalid_input, and a closed runtime is
// unavailable.
func (r *Runtime) OpenStream(ctx context.Context, p core.Principal, module, name string, params url.Values) (io.ReadCloser, error) {
	def, ok := r.cfg.Registry.Stream(module, name)
	if !ok {
		return nil, errcode.New(errcode.NotFound, fmt.Sprintf("no stream %s.%s", module, name))
	}
	if err := r.usable(module + "." + name); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	raw, err := schema.ParamsJSON(def.ParamsType, params)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if err := streamParams.ValidateType(def.ParamsType, raw); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	all, err := r.streams.add()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	env := r.moduleEnv(module)
	env.Principal = p
	runCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
	stop := context.AfterFunc(all, cancel)
	pipe := newStreamPipe(cancel)
	go func() {
		defer r.streams.wg.Done()
		defer stop()
		defer cancel()
		err := lifecycle.Protect(r.cfg.Log, module+"."+name, "stream", func() error {
			return def.Run(runCtx, env, raw, func(event any) error { return pipe.emit(runCtx, event) })
		})
		var end []byte
		switch {
		case pipe.readerGone() || ctx.Err() != nil:
			// Nobody reads the end any more.
		case all.Err() != nil:
			end = pipe.endLine(r.cfg.Log, errStreamClosed)
		default:
			end = pipe.endLine(r.cfg.Log, err)
		}
		pipe.finish(end)
	}()
	return pipe, nil
}

// streamSet is the runtime's running module streams. Its zero value is
// ready to use.
type streamSet struct {
	mu     sync.Mutex
	ctx    context.Context // every stream's Run context ends with it
	cancel context.CancelFunc
	closed bool
	wg     sync.WaitGroup // one per Run still running
}

// add counts one more stream and returns the context its Run must also end
// with; once close began it answers unavailable.
func (s *streamSet) add() (context.Context, error) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	if s.closed {
		return nil, errcode.New(errcode.Unavailable, "the agent runtime is closed")
	}
	if s.ctx == nil {
		s.ctx, s.cancel = context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	}
	s.wg.Add(1)
	return s.ctx, nil
}

// close ends every stream's Run context and waits until each Run returned.
// A Run blocked in emit returns at once, because emit stops waiting for the
// reader when its context ends.
func (s *streamSet) close() {
	s.mu.Lock()
	s.closed = true
	if s.cancel != nil {
		s.cancel()
	}
	s.mu.Unlock()
	s.wg.Wait()
}

// streamPipe hands a stream's lines to its reader one at a time. Unlike
// io.Pipe, a writer stops waiting when its context ends, so Close never
// waits on a reader that stopped reading.
type streamPipe struct {
	lines  chan []byte   // event lines; closed by finish
	done   chan struct{} // closed by Close
	fin    chan struct{} // closed when finish begins
	once   sync.Once
	cancel context.CancelFunc

	mu       sync.Mutex
	failed   error  // an event that could not be sent; every later emit returns it
	finished bool   // finish ran; emit must not send any more
	end      []byte // the end line, written before lines closes

	buf []byte // the reader's unread rest of a line
	eof bool
}

func newStreamPipe(cancel context.CancelFunc) *streamPipe {
	return &streamPipe{lines: make(chan []byte), done: make(chan struct{}), fin: make(chan struct{}), cancel: cancel}
}

var (
	errStreamReaderGone = errors.New("runtime: the stream's reader is gone")
	errStreamFinished   = errors.New("runtime: the stream has ended")
)

// emit sends one event line and waits until the reader takes it; it fails
// once the reader is gone, ctx ended, an event was too large, or the stream
// ended.
func (p *streamPipe) emit(ctx context.Context, event any) error {
	p.mu.Lock()
	defer p.mu.Unlock()
	switch {
	case p.failed != nil:
		return p.failed
	case p.finished:
		return errStreamFinished
	}
	b, err := json.Marshal(event)
	if err != nil {
		p.failed = fmt.Errorf("runtime: encode a stream event: %w", err)
		return p.failed
	}
	if len(b) > MaxStreamEvent {
		p.failed = errcode.New(errcode.TooLarge, fmt.Sprintf("a stream event of %d bytes exceeds %d bytes", len(b), MaxStreamEvent))
		return p.failed
	}
	line := make([]byte, 0, len(b)+10)
	line = append(line, `{"data":`...)
	line = append(line, b...)
	line = append(line, "}\n"...)
	select {
	case p.lines <- line:
		return nil
	case <-p.done:
		return errStreamReaderGone
	case <-p.fin:
		return errStreamFinished
	case <-ctx.Done():
		return ctx.Err()
	}
}

// readerGone reports whether Close ran.
func (p *streamPipe) readerGone() bool {
	select {
	case <-p.done:
		return true
	default:
		return false
	}
}

// streamProblem is the error of an end line: the code and the client-safe
// detail, as the agent API's problem details carry them.
type streamProblem struct {
	Code   errcode.Code `json:"code"`
	Detail string       `json:"detail"`
}

type streamEnd struct {
	Reason string         `json:"reason"`
	Error  *streamProblem `json:"error,omitempty"`
}

// endLine is the end line: done when err is nil and no emit failed, else
// error with the first emit failure or err. Like the agent API's problem
// details, a 5xx code carries only its title; an internal error is logged.
func (p *streamPipe) endLine(log *slog.Logger, err error) []byte {
	p.mu.Lock()
	if p.failed != nil {
		err = p.failed
	}
	p.mu.Unlock()
	e := streamEnd{Reason: "done"}
	if err != nil {
		c := errcode.From(err)
		code := c.Code
		if !errcode.Known(code) {
			code = errcode.Internal
		}
		problem := &streamProblem{Code: code, Detail: c.Detail}
		if code.Status() >= http.StatusInternalServerError {
			problem.Detail = code.Title()
		}
		if code == errcode.Internal {
			log.Error("runtime: stream failed", "code", c.Code, "err", err)
		}
		if problem.Detail == "" {
			problem.Detail = code.Title()
		}
		e = streamEnd{Reason: "error", Error: problem}
	}
	b, merr := json.Marshal(map[string]streamEnd{"end": e})
	if merr != nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("runtime: marshal a stream end: %v", merr)) // strings only
	}
	return append(b, '\n')
}

// finish ends the stream after Run returned: emit fails from now on, and
// the reader gets end, if any, after the last event line, then io.EOF.
func (p *streamPipe) finish(end []byte) {
	close(p.fin)
	p.mu.Lock()
	defer p.mu.Unlock()
	p.finished = true
	p.end = end
	close(p.lines)
}

// Read returns the next part of the current line; a line whose reader
// buffer is large enough arrives in one Read.
func (p *streamPipe) Read(b []byte) (int, error) {
	for len(p.buf) == 0 {
		if p.eof {
			return 0, io.EOF
		}
		select {
		case line, ok := <-p.lines:
			if !ok {
				p.buf, p.eof = p.end, true
				continue
			}
			p.buf = line
		case <-p.done:
			return 0, io.ErrClosedPipe
		}
	}
	n := copy(b, p.buf)
	p.buf = p.buf[n:]
	return n, nil
}

// Close ends the stream for its reader and cancels Run's context.
func (p *streamPipe) Close() error {
	p.once.Do(func() {
		close(p.done)
		p.cancel()
	})
	return nil
}
```

### Task 57: Uninstall barrier step, stop-tasks and abort

Wires w0a's barrier into `darkpanel uninstall` (seam S4, spec 1.11, C36): a first `barrier` step, `UninstallConfig.StopTasks` and `Actor`, and `install.AbortUninstall`. Without `StopTasks` the step lists `darkpanel-task-*.service` first and refuses with `core.change_busy` while one is neither inactive nor failed, then calls `lifecycle.BeginUninstall(ctx, db, false)`, which refuses while a change is unfinished; a refusal therefore leaves no barrier behind. With `StopTasks` it sets the barrier first, so no task starts after its unit was stopped, then stops every such unit and waits for each with the existing `waitStopped` (`StopTimeout` per unit). The `--keep-data` data step deletes the barrier row from the kept `agent.db`, because a later install must accept changes. `AbortUninstall` clears the barrier only while `darkpanel-agent.service` is active. Split from Task 18 by Rule S. Data-loss and concurrency risk: it runs alone. Test helpers carry the prefix `bar`.

with:

```go
// setBarrier sets the uninstall barrier, so the agent accepts no new change
// and starts no task while the uninstall runs (spec 1.3c and 1.11). Without
// --stop-tasks it refuses, before setting the barrier, while a task unit is
// active or a change is unfinished. With --stop-tasks it sets the barrier
// first, so no task starts after its unit was stopped, then stops every
// active task unit and waits for each to stop.
func (u *Uninstall) setBarrier(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
	if u.db == nil {
		return "no agent database; no change can be running", nil
	}
	if !u.cfg.StopTasks {
		active, err := u.activeTaskUnits(ctx)
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		if len(active) > 0 {
			return "", errcode.New(errcode.ChangeBusy, "the task units "+strings.Join(active, ", ")+
				" are active; wait for them to finish, or uninstall with --stop-tasks")
		}
		if err := lifecycle.BeginUninstall(ctx, u.db, false); err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		return "set the uninstall barrier; no change is unfinished", nil
	}
	if err := lifecycle.BeginUninstall(ctx, u.db, true); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	active, err := u.activeTaskUnits(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	for _, unit := range active {
		if err := u.cfg.Systemd.Stop(ctx, unit); err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
	}
	for _, unit := range active {
		if err := u.waitStopped(ctx, unit); err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
	}
	if len(active) == 0 {
		return "set the uninstall barrier; no task unit was active", nil
	}
	return "set the uninstall barrier and stopped " + strings.Join(active, ", "), nil
}

// activeTaskUnits names the task units that are neither inactive nor
// failed, as waitStopped counts a stopped unit.
func (u *Uninstall) activeTaskUnits(ctx context.Context) ([]string, error) {
	units, err := u.cfg.Systemd.List(ctx, taskUnits)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	var active []string
	for _, st := range units {
		if st.ActiveState != "inactive" && st.ActiveState != "failed" {
			active = append(active, st.Name)
		}
	}
	return active, nil
}

// clearBarrier removes the uninstall barrier from the agent database
// --keep-data keeps: the uninstall finished, and a later install must
// accept changes.
func (u *Uninstall) clearBarrier(ctx context.Context) error {
	if u.db == nil {
		return nil
	}
	return u.db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
		_, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, "DELETE FROM core_meta WHERE key = ?", lifecycle.MetaUninstalling)
		return err
	})
}

// AbortUninstall clears the uninstall barrier an uninstall set before it
// stopped the services, so the agent accepts changes again (spec 1.11), and
// audits it as cfg.Actor in the agent journal. It acts only while the agent
// service is active: once the services were stopped, running the uninstall
// again is the only way on, and AbortUninstall reports that it changed
// nothing. It uses cfg's Layout, Systemd and Actor.
func AbortUninstall(ctx context.Context, cfg UninstallConfig) (string, error) {
	switch {
	case cfg.Systemd == nil:
		return "", errors.New("install: UninstallConfig.Systemd is required")
	case cfg.Actor == "":
		return "", errors.New("install: UninstallConfig.Actor is required")
	}
	st, err := cfg.Systemd.State(ctx, update.AgentUnit)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if st.ActiveState != "active" {
		return "the services were stopped; there is nothing to abort", nil
	}
	db, err := store.Open(ctx, cfg.Layout.Paths.AgentDB())
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("install: abort uninstall: %w", err)
	}
	err = lifecycle.AbortUninstall(ctx, db, cfg.Actor)
	if cerr := db.Close(); err == nil {
		err = cerr
	}
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return "the uninstall barrier is cleared; the agent accepts changes again", nil
}

// stopServices stops the services that exist, waits until they are down,
```

```go
package dispatch

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"net/netip"
	"sync"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/coretest"
)

// The fixture module "dg" has a guarded agent-side action and a guarded
// controller-side action; their handlers record the guard context of every
// plan and the call context of every apply.

var (
	refDgAgent = core.ActionRef{Name: "dg.rule.set", Version: 1}
	refDgCtl   = core.ActionRef{Name: "dg.ctl.set", Version: 1}
)

type dgInput struct {
	core.Guarded
	Name string `json:"name"`
}

type dgOut struct {
	Name string `json:"name"`
}

// dgSeen holds, per side, the guard context of the last plan and the call
// context of the last apply.
type dgSeen struct {
	mu     sync.Mutex
	guards map[core.Side]*core.GuardContext
	calls  map[core.Side]core.CallContext
}

func (s *dgSeen) guard(side core.Side) *core.GuardContext {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return s.guards[side]
}

func (s *dgSeen) call(side core.Side) core.CallContext {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return s.calls[side]
}

type dgHandler struct {
	side core.Side
	seen *dgSeen
}

func (h dgHandler) Plan(_ context.Context, _ core.Env, in dgInput) (core.PlanOutcome, error) {
	h.seen.mu.Lock()
	defer h.seen.mu.Unlock()
	h.seen.guards[h.side] = in.Guard
	return core.PlanOutcome{Diff: []core.DiffLine{{Op: "+", Text: in.Name}}, StateHash: "dg"}, nil
}

func (h dgHandler) Apply(_ context.Context, env core.Env, in dgInput) (dgOut, error) {
	h.seen.mu.Lock()
	defer h.seen.mu.Unlock()
	h.seen.calls[h.side] = env.Call
	return dgOut{Name: in.Name}, nil
}

func (dgHandler) Verify(context.Context, core.Env, dgInput, dgOut) error { return nil }

type dgModule struct{ seen *dgSeen }

func (m dgModule) Manifest() core.Manifest {
	guards := []core.GuardSpec{{ID: "dg.lockout", Overridable: true}}
	return core.Manifest{ID: "dg", Version: 1, DefaultEnabled: true, Actions: []core.ActionDef{
		core.DefineMutating(core.ActionSpec{Name: refDgAgent.Name, Version: 1, Class: core.ClassCompensable,
			Side: core.SideAgent, CompensatedBy: refDgAgent.Name, Guards: guards}, dgHandler{core.SideAgent, m.seen}),
		core.DefineMutating(core.ActionSpec{Name: refDgCtl.Name, Version: 1, Class: core.ClassCompensable,
			Side: core.SideController, CompensatedBy: refDgCtl.Name, Guards: guards}, dgHandler{core.SideController, m.seen}),
	}}
}

// dgAgent is h1's agent: the harness runtime, with the raw input of every
// plan and the options of every apply recorded.
type dgAgent struct {
	core.AgentClient
	mu     sync.Mutex
	inputs []string
	opts   []core.ApplyOptions
}

func (a *dgAgent) Plan(ctx context.Context, p core.Principal, ref core.ActionRef, input json.RawMessage, opts core.PlanOptions) (core.PlanView, error) {
	a.mu.Lock()
	a.inputs = append(a.inputs, string(input))
	a.mu.Unlock()
	return a.AgentClient.Plan(ctx, p, ref, input, opts)
}

func (a *dgAgent) Apply(ctx context.Context, p core.Principal, planID string, opts core.ApplyOptions) (core.ChangeView, error) {
	a.mu.Lock()
	a.opts = append(a.opts, opts)
	a.mu.Unlock()
	return a.AgentClient.Apply(ctx, p, planID, opts)
}

func (a *dgAgent) lastInput() string {
	a.mu.Lock()
	defer a.mu.Unlock()
	return a.inputs[len(a.inputs)-1]
}

func (a *dgAgent) lastOpts() core.ApplyOptions {
	a.mu.Lock()
	defer a.mu.Unlock()
	return a.opts[len(a.opts)-1]
}

var (
	dgTopology = Topology{
		PanelListen: []netip.AddrPort{netip.MustParseAddrPort("127.0.0.1:8443")},
		AgentListen: []netip.AddrPort{netip.MustParseAddrPort("[::]:7443")},
		AgentPeers:  []netip.Addr{netip.MustParseAddr("192.0.2.30")},
	}
	dgPeer = core.Peer{Addr: netip.MustParseAddr("192.0.2.7"), Port: 51234}
	// dgFull is the guard context of dgTopology and dgPeer.
	dgFull = &core.GuardContext{Client: &dgPeer, PanelListen: dgTopology.PanelListen,
		AgentListen: dgTopology.AgentListen, AgentPeers: dgTopology.AgentPeers}
)

// newDg is a dispatcher with module dg and topology topo over a harness whose
// agent is a dgAgent.
func newDg(t *testing.T, topo func() Topology) (*Dispatcher, *dgSeen, *dgAgent) {
	t.Helper()
	seen := &dgSeen{guards: map[core.Side]*core.GuardContext{}, calls: map[core.Side]core.CallContext{}}
	h := newHarnessWith(t, dgModule{seen})
	agent := &dgAgent{AgentClient: h.rt}
	h.clients.Add(testHost, agent)
	cfg := h.config(&coretest.MemAudit{})
	cfg.Topology = topo
	d, err := New(cfg)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return d, seen, agent
}

// dgJSON is v as JSON, so guard contexts compare by their wire form.
func dgJSON(t *testing.T, v any) string {
	t.Helper()
	b, err := json.Marshal(v)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return string(b)
}

func TestPlanFillsGuard(t *testing.T) {
	d, seen, agent := newDg(t, func() Topology { return dgTopology })
	ctx := core.WithClientPeer(context.Background(), dgPeer)
	want := dgJSON(t, dgFull)
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name, host string
		ref        core.ActionRef
		side       core.Side
		input      string
	}{
		{"an agent action", testHost, refDgAgent, core.SideAgent, `{"name":"a"}`},
		{"an agent action given a guard", testHost, refDgAgent, core.SideAgent,
			`{"name":"a","guard":{"agentPeers":["203.0.113.9"]},"GUARD":{}}`},
		{"a controller action given a guard", "", refDgCtl, core.SideController, `{"name":"a","guard":{}}`},
	} {
		if _, err := d.Plan(ctx, alice, tc.host, tc.ref, json.RawMessage(tc.input), core.PlanOptions{}); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s: %v", tc.name, err)
		}
		if got := dgJSON(t, seen.guard(tc.side)); got != want {
			t.Errorf("%s: the handler saw guard %s, want %s", tc.name, got, want)
		}
	}
	const unguarded = `{ "value": "1", "name": "a" }`
	if _, err := d.Plan(ctx, alice, testHost, refSet, json.RawMessage(unguarded), core.PlanOptions{}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got := agent.lastInput(); got != unguarded {
		t.Errorf("the agent got input %s for an unguarded action, want %s byte for byte", got, unguarded)
	}
}

		want *core.GuardContext

func TestApplySendsGuardRefresh(t *testing.T) {
	d, seen, agent := newDg(t, func() Topology { return dgTopology })
	ctx := core.WithClientPeer(context.Background(), dgPeer)
	want := dgJSON(t, dgFull)
	plan := func(hostID string, ref core.ActionRef, input string, call *core.CallContext) string {
		t.Helper()
		v, err := d.Plan(ctx, alice, hostID, ref, json.RawMessage(input), core.PlanOptions{Call: call})
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		return v.PlanID
	}

	// A top-level agent apply gains a call context with the guard refresh.
	planID := plan(testHost, refSet, `{"name":"a","value":"1"}`, nil)
	if _, err := d.Apply(ctx, alice, testHost, refSet, planID, core.ApplyOptions{ConfirmNow: true}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	got := agent.lastOpts()
	if got.Call == nil || dgJSON(t, got.Call.GuardRefresh) != want || got.Call.ParentChangeID != "" || !got.ConfirmNow {
		t.Errorf("top-level apply options %+v, call %+v; want only the guard refresh %s added", got, got.Call, want)
	}

	// A composite step's apply keeps its call context, and the caller's is
	// not changed.
	call := &core.CallContext{ParentChangeID: "01COMPOSITE", ParentAction: "cfx.deploy.add", StepID: "a"}
	planID = plan(testHost, refDgAgent, `{"name":"b"}`, call)
	if _, err := d.Apply(ctx, alice, testHost, refDgAgent, planID, core.ApplyOptions{Call: call}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	got = agent.lastOpts()
	if got.Call == nil || got.Call == call || got.Call.ParentChangeID != call.ParentChangeID ||
		got.Call.StepID != call.StepID || dgJSON(t, got.Call.GuardRefresh) != want {
		t.Errorf("step apply call %+v, want a copy of %+v with the guard refresh", got.Call, call)
	}
	if call.GuardRefresh != nil {
		t.Error("the caller's call context was changed")
	}
	if seenRefresh := seen.call(core.SideAgent).GuardRefresh; dgJSON(t, seenRefresh) != want {
		t.Errorf("the agent handler's apply saw guard refresh %s, want %s", dgJSON(t, seenRefresh), want)
	}

	// A controller-side apply runs with the options as given.
	planID = plan("", refDgCtl, `{"name":"c"}`, nil)
	if _, err := d.Apply(ctx, alice, "", refDgCtl, planID, core.ApplyOptions{}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if c := seen.call(core.SideController); c.GuardRefresh != nil {
		t.Errorf("the controller handler's apply saw guard refresh %s, want none", dgJSON(t, c.GuardRefresh))
	}
}
```

```go
package dispatch

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"net/netip"
	"strings"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
)

// Topology is the controller's side of a guard context (spec 1.5): its web
// and agent listeners and its live agents' addresses.
type Topology struct {
	PanelListen []netip.AddrPort
	AgentListen []netip.AddrPort
	AgentPeers  []netip.Addr
}

// guardContext is the guard context of a call now: the client peer the API
// stored in ctx and the configured topology. A composite's children run on
// the engine's context and so carry no client peer.
func (d *Dispatcher) guardContext(ctx context.Context) core.GuardContext {
	var g core.GuardContext
	if d.cfg.Topology != nil {
		t := d.cfg.Topology()
		g.PanelListen, g.AgentListen, g.AgentPeers = t.PanelListen, t.AgentListen, t.AgentPeers
	}
	if p, ok := core.ClientPeer(ctx); ok {
		g.Client = &p
	}
	return g
}

// withGuard returns input with its top-level guard member set to g. Members
// whose name matches guard ignoring case are dropped first, because
// encoding/json would decode any of them as the guard. An input that is not
// a JSON object is returned as it is, for the validator to refuse.
func withGuard(input json.RawMessage, g core.GuardContext) (json.RawMessage, error) {
	var obj map[string]json.RawMessage
	if err := json.Unmarshal(input, &obj); err != nil || obj == nil {
		return input, nil
	}
	for key := range obj {
		if strings.EqualFold(key, "guard") {
			delete(obj, key)
		}
	}
	raw, err := json.Marshal(g)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("dispatch: encode the guard context: %w", err)
	}
	obj["guard"] = raw
	out, err := json.Marshal(obj)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("dispatch: encode the input: %w", err)
	}
	return out, nil
}

// withGuardRefresh returns opts whose call context carries the guard context
// now, on a copy, so the caller's call context is never changed.
func (d *Dispatcher) withGuardRefresh(ctx context.Context, opts core.ApplyOptions) core.ApplyOptions {
	var call core.CallContext
	if opts.Call != nil {
		call = *opts.Call
	}
	g := d.guardContext(ctx)
	call.GuardRefresh = &g
	opts.Call = &call
	return opts
}
```
